FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE.

D.S. Bradley
J.D.I. Grubb

In accordance with the instructions of the
Commissioner of Police, Khoong Kyung Sung (孔慶增),
Sung Ping Chien (沈炳謙) alias Sung Heng Ih(沈恒一)
and Yeng Chien Chu (楊劍), were handed over to
the Japanese Consular Police for trial on 24/3/39.

All the documents seized in the homes of the
accused at House 48, Lane 920, Sinza Road, 671 Rue
Lafayette and No.36 Garden Villa off Route Vallon,
were handed over to the Japanese Consular Police who
wished to use them as evidence at the trial of the
three accused.

The Japanese Consular Police have signed a
receipt for both the prisoners and the documents and
they have promised to let the S.M.Police know the
result of the trial.

H.C.

JBradley.

日期：1939年3月25日

关于进一步协助日本领事馆警察事宜。

D.S. Bradley
J.D.I. Grubb

遵照警务处处长的指示，孔慶增（Khoong Kyung Sung）、沈炳謙（Sung Ping Chien），别名沈恒一（Sung Heng Ih）以及楊劍（Yeng Chien Chu），已于1939年3月24日移交给日本领事馆警察进行审判。

在新闸路920弄48号、辣斐德路671号以及华伦路（Route Vallon）花园别墅36号的被告住所内查获的所有文件，均已移交给日本领事馆警察，他们希望将这些文件作为审判这三名被告的证据。

日本领事馆警察已就囚犯和文件签署了收据，并承诺将审判结果告知上海公共租界工部局警务处。

H.C.

JBradley.

Summary of report re assistance to the
Japanese Consular Police in the arrest
of three persons suspected to be
trafficking in firearms.

On the forenoon of 15-3-39 the Japanese
Consular Police requested the assistance of the S. M.
Police to arrest 3 male Chinese who were suspected to
be members of a guerilla unit.
The necessary assistance was given and at
about 3.20 p.m. same date 3 male Chinese were arrested
on Railway Road, whilst they were travelling in a
Taylor hire car.
The 3 Chinese named Koong Kyung Sung
(孔广增), Sung Ping Chien (宋炳钱) and Yang Chien
Chu (杨钱珠) were brought to C.B.H.Q. where they were
searched and interrogated and it was found that they
had been in contact with 3 Europeans who pretended to
be in a position to sell firearms for the use of
guerilla troops in Chekiang.
Negotiations for the purchase of the arms
had been concluded and the 3 persons were arrested
whilst they were on their way to the place where the
firearms were to be handed over.
The 3 suspects admitted that it was their
intention to buy firearms for guerilla troops and on
the person of one of the suspects was a document from
Brigadier General Sung (  ), Officer in charge of the
Chekiang Chinese Army authorising him to act as his agent.
The 3 suspects were then handed over to the
Japanese Consular Police for 3 days to allow them to
continue enquiries and a further extension of 5 days was
later granted to them. The homes of the 3 suspects at

关于协助日本领事馆警察逮捕三名涉嫌贩卖枪支人员的报告摘要。

1939年3月15日上午，日本领事馆警察请求上海公共租界工部局警务处协助逮捕三名中国男子，怀疑他们是游击队成员。
警方提供了必要的协助，同日约下午3时20分，三名中国男子在铁路路（Railway Road）乘坐一辆泰勒（Taylor）租赁汽车时被逮捕。
这三名中国人名为孔广增（Koong Kyung Sung）、宋炳钱（Sung Ping Chien）和杨钱珠（Yang Chien Chu），被带至中央捕房总部（C.B.H.Q.）。经搜查和审讯，发现他们曾与三名欧洲人接触，这些欧洲人谎称有能力出售枪支供浙江的游击队使用。
购买武器的谈判已结束，这三人在前往移交枪支地点的途中被捕。
三名嫌疑人承认其意图为游击队购买枪支，其中一名嫌疑人的身上有一份宋将军（Brigadier General Sung）（原文不清）签署的文件，宋将军是负责浙江中国军队的军官，授权该嫌疑人作为其代理人。
随后，这三名嫌疑人被移交给日本领事馆警察拘留三天，以便他们继续调查，后来又获准延长五天。对这三名嫌疑人位于新闸路920弄46号、辣斐德路671号以及

No. 36, Garden Villa, Route Vallon, were searched and
a large number of documents seized and handed over to
the Japanese Consular Police after they had been
translated at C.B.H.Q.. Documents seized in the French
Concession homes of the accused were loaned to the
Japanese Consular Police and they have been returned
and are being kept at C.B.H.Q..

The Japanese Consular Police desire that

stand trial for being concerned in anti-Japanese
activities.

There is no doubt that the 3 suspects were
guilty of attempting to purchase arms for the use of the
Chinese Army.

Attached is a translation of the document
found in possession of Koong Kyung Sung together with
4 cablegrams and one other document issued by the
Chekiang Provincial Government.

日本领事馆警察希望永久移交这三名嫌疑人，以便以参与反日活动为由对他们进行审判。

毫无疑问，这三名嫌疑人犯有试图为中国军队购买武器的罪行。

犯罪科副主任（D.C. Crime）获悉此请求后指示，在日本警察提供所需协助的细节后，上海公共租界工部局警务处应前往法国警察总部，而日本领事馆警察在上海公共租界工部局警务处申请协助并进行所需搜查期间，应留在中央捕房总部。

Japanese Consular Police. 58 Documents, 9 photographs,
12 visiting cards, 3 invitation cards and one book
was seized and no arrests made.

At about 10.30 p.m. same date the room of Yang
Chieh Chu at 36 Garden Villa, Route Mollon was searched

All the seized documents were taken to Lokawei

The Japanese Consular Police then wished to
search the home of Koong Kyung Sung ( 孔 景 松 ) at
179 Kweichow Road, but when C.D.I. Grubb and party
reached that address they found it was a branch of
the Door of Hope which is a British Missionary
Institution. The Japanese Consular Police were
informed that the premises could not be searched
without a British Court Warrant.

Enquiries were made at the premises and Mrs.
Koong, mother of Koong Kyung Sung, was questioned
and she stated that her son did not reside at that
address although he came to see her daily. She was
under the impression that he cohabited with a girl
at an address on Sinza Road, but she did not know
the exact address. Mrs. Koong is the Chinese
supervisor of this branch of the Door of Hope.

The Japanese Consular Police seemed satisfied

法国警察执行，D.S. Mitsushima 在一旁守候，寻找日本领事馆警察提到的文件。查获58份文件、9张照片、12张名片、3张请柬和一本书，未实施逮捕。

同日晚上约10时30分，搜查了莫伦路（Route Mollon）花园别墅36号杨杰楚（Yang Chieh Chu）的房间，查获19份文件，未实施逮捕。

所有查获的文件均被带往卢家湾，目前由法国警察保管，以待事态进一步发展。

随后，日本领事馆警察希望搜查孔景松（Koong Kyung Sung）位于贵州路179号的住所，但当 C.D.I. Grubb 及其随行人员到达该地址时，发现那是“怀恩堂”（Door of Hope）的一个分部，这是一个英国传教机构。日本领事馆警察被告知，若无英国法院搜查令，不得搜查该场所。

在该场所进行了查询，并讯问了孔景松的母亲孔夫人，她表示她的儿子不住在该地址，尽管他每天来看望她。她以为他与一名女孩同居在新闸路的某个地址，但她不知道确切地址。孔夫人是该“怀恩堂”分部的中方主管。

日本领事馆警察似乎对

pages.en:
List of documents seized at No.36 Garden Terrace, (Hwo Yuen
Bei Sz), Route Vallon, Home of Yang Wei Kong (楊維康).

1. Draft of a letter addressed by Yang Chien Dao (楊劍),
International Soap Works, to a Japanese named Yoo Dien
Loong Yih Long (和田龍一郎), entrusting the latter with
the task of removing the machine, raw material, etc. from
the International Soap Works, Ching Kee Jao, Nantao.
The letter dated 10.2.39.

2. A letter addressed by Wong Seu Tsuh (王守則) to the San
Fu University stating that he agrees to serve as a lecturer
in the university. The letter dated Jan., 1939.

3. An official letter addressed by Chiang Tseng Kwang (蔣震寰)
to Wong Yao Ding (王耀庭) and Yang Chien Dao (楊劍儔),
entrusting the latter with the task of removing a total of
1,600 tons of raw materials from the International Soap
Works in Nantao to House 534 Ferry Road. The total cost
of the materials is estimated at $500,000.00.

4. Draft of an agreement relating to the removal of raw materials
from the International Soap Works.

5. A medical prescription for Mrs. Yang.

6. Two articles written by one named Yang on Chinese literature.

7. A pamphlet entitled "A Manifesto issued by the Chinese
Republic Reformed Government" announcing its inauguration
on March 23 in Nanking. It also denounces the National
Government for its corrupt administration which leads
to the present crisis. (Note: This handbill was issued
on March 23, 1939).

8. A copy of the regulations governing the "Association of
Eastern Nations". According to the regulations, the
Association has for its aim the promotion of peace in
Asia and over the world. It will establish its hdqrs.
at Shanghai and branches at various places. The mission
of the Association will be (1) to study the disputes
between Japan and China as a measure to eliminate warfare,
and (2) to study measures for the establishment of permanent
peace in Asia, (3) to promote the culture of Asia and (4)
to unite the nations of Asia against communism.

9. A copy of the regulations governing the "Association of
Eastern Nations" (in Japanese).

10. Draft of an article asserting that a number of Chinese who
have been hoodwinked by communism and juggling policies of
European and American countries have advocated "resistance
to Japan" as a national salvation policy. The writer of
the article points out that this is fundamentally wrong.
China cannot obtain salvation from Soviet Russia nor
any European or American countries. If she wants to save
herself, the only way is for her to unite with other Asiatic
nations, chiefly Japan, the article concludes.

11. A written copy of the regulations governing the Shanghai
Branch of the Great Asia Association of China. According
to the regulations of the Association, the aim of the
Association is to promote friendship between the Asiatic
countries and unite them into one strong body; and its
activities will be to propagate Asianism, introduce Chinese
culture to foreign countries and to study the commerce of
the Asiatic countries.
pages.zh:
在华伦路花园别墅36号（华园北墅），杨维康（Yang Wei Kong）住所查获的文件清单。

1. 杨剑（Yang Chien Dao，国际肥皂厂）写给一名叫和田龍一郎（Yoo Dien Loong Yih Long）的日本人的信函草稿，委托后者负责将机器、原材料等从南市庆记皂厂的国际肥皂厂搬走。信函日期为1939年2月10日。

2. 王守則（Wong Seu Tsuh）写给三福大学（San Fu University）的一封信，表示同意担任该大学的讲师。信函日期为1939年1月。

3. 蔣震寰（Chiang Tseng Kwang）写给王耀庭（Wong Yao Ding）和杨剑儔（Yang Chien Dao）的公函，委托后者负责将总计1,600吨原材料从南市的国际肥皂厂搬运至渡船路534号。材料总成本估计为500,000.00美元。

4. 关于从国际肥皂厂搬运原材料的协议草稿。

5. 杨夫人的医疗处方。

6. 一名姓杨的人写的两篇关于中国文学的文章。

7. 一本小册子，题为《中华民国维新政府宣言》，宣布其于3月23日在南京成立。它还谴责国民政府的腐败统治导致了当前的危机。（注：此传单发布于1939年3月23日）。

8. 《东亚协会》规章副本。根据规章，该协会旨在促进亚洲及世界的和平。将在上海设立总部，并在各地设立分会。协会的使命将是（1）研究中日争端，作为消除战争的措施，（2）研究建立亚洲永久和平的措施，（3）促进亚洲文化，以及（4）团结亚洲各国对抗共产主义。

9. 《东亚协会》规章副本（日文版）。

10. 一篇文章的草稿，声称许多被共产主义和欧美国家的操纵政策所蒙蔽的中国人提倡以“抗日”作为救国政策。文章作者指出这在根本上是错误的。中国无法从苏俄或任何欧美国家获得救赎。如果想自救，唯一的办法是与其他亚洲国家，主要是日本，团结起来，文章最后总结道。

11. 中国大亚细亚协会上海分会规章的手抄本。根据协会规章，协会的宗旨是促进亚洲各国之间的友谊，并将它们团结成一个强大的整体；其活动将是宣传亚细亚主义，向外国介绍中国文化，并研究亚洲各国的商业。

pages.en:
12. Draft of an article entitled "The reason and aim of
forming the Great Asia Association of China". The
article begins by criticising the Chinese National
Government for having failed to approach Japan for
cooperation in its reconstruction work. China, being
one of the countries in Asia, the article continues,
should unite with the other Asiatic nations for the
development of the continent, but to the country she
has been adopting an anti-Japanese policy for the
past several decades. China should change her policy
and should together with Japan **〔此处转录不清〕**
struggle for the realization of "Asianism."

13. Draft of an official letter appointing a certain
person to undertake negotiations with the Japanese
authorities for the issue of a permit for operating a
club.

14. 17 name cards of different persons including two Japanese
named Wada, House Manager of Ritz Theatre, and Chung Ching
Yien Chih (中井硯士), employed with the Special Service
Section of the Japanese Military.

15. One photograph.

16. A note -book containing addresses of a number of persons.
pages.zh:
12. 一篇题为《组建中华大亚细亚协会的原因与宗旨》的文章草稿。文章开篇批评中国国民政府未能在重建工作中寻求与日本合作。文章接着指出，中国作为亚洲国家之一，本应与其他亚洲国家联合以谋求大陆的发展，但该国在过去几十年里一直采取反日政策。中国应当改变其政策，并与日本**〔此处转录不清〕**共同奋斗，以实现“亚细亚主义”。

13. 一份委任某人就经营俱乐部许可证一事与日本当局进行谈判的公函草稿。

14. 17张不同人士的名片，其中包括两名日本人：丽都大戏院（Ritz Theatre）经理和田（Wada），以及受雇于日本军方特务机关的中井砚士（Chung Ching Yien Chih）。

List of Documents Seized at No.617 Rue Lafayette, Home of

1) Official despatch dated December, 1938 issued by the
Chekiang Provincial Government:
"To Mr. Sung Hung-yih,
"We hereby send officials to Shanghai to make
purchases of various kinds of commodities that are
being required by this government.
"From Huang Shao-hsiung,
Chairman of the Chekiang Provincial Govt!

2) A Sheet of paper containing a list in English of arms
in stock in Shanghai (copy attached).

3) Letter dated May 10 addressed by one Chang (張) to
Chairman Huang Chi-kwan (黃季寬):
"Dear Chi-kwan,
"One of my friends named Sung Hung-yih has undertaken
the post of Manager of Dodge Chrysler Motor Car Company.
It is learned that the latter has many cars in stock in
Hongkong and is willing to sell them at a cheap price.
"It goes without saying that cars are necessary
to facilitate communications at this time of military
operations. I hope you will purchase some of them.
"Chang"

a Dramatic Plays Research Society.

Hung-yih, dated July 7 telling the latter that his
intention to buy a motor car would be cancelled and asking
him to send back the sum of $2,500 he (Chang) had paid.

had been remitted to him for the purchase of **〔此处转录不清〕**

formation of a Dramatic Plays Research Society.

10) Four telegrams to and from Chang Zau-dong (張紹棠),
Kinhwa, and Sung Hung-yih, regarding the purchase of
motor cars.
One telegram not decoded.

Hung-yih, stating that the Shanghai Women's and Children's

FURTHER REMARKS TO THE JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE.

D. I. Bradley C.D.I. Grubb.

Sir,

At about 7.30 p.m. 16.3.39, Mr. Hashizume,
requested the assistance of the S.M.Police to
search the homes of Sung Heng Ih (沈亨 - ) and
Yong Chien Chu (楊劍秋) who had given their
address as 671 Rue Lafayette and No. 56 Gordon
Villa Route Allon.

The D.C. Crime was informed of the request and he
gave instructions that the S.M.Police were to proceed
to French Police H.Q., after the J.C.Police had given
details of the assistance required and the J.C.Police
were to remain at C.B.H. whilst the S.M.Police
applied for assistance and carried out the required
search.

These instructions were communicated to Mr.
Hashizuma by C.D.I. Grubb, but he refused to stay
and insisted on proceeding to French Police H.Q.
It was then arranged that Mr. Hashizuma should
proceed to the French Police H.Q. where he would
meet the D.C. Crime and Mr. Jobez, Deputy Commissioner
of the Political Branch of the French Police.

At French Police H.Q. it was arranged that the
French Police would render assistance to the S.M.Police
in searching the stated addresses whilst the J.C.Police
were to wait at Lokawei.

At about 9.40 p.m. D.M. Rhodes, J.D.S. Mitsushima
C.D.C. 290 and the undersigned accompanied by the
French Police party searched No. 617 Rue Lafayette,
the home of Sung Heng Ih. The actual search was

致日本领事警察的补充说明。

D. I. Bradley C.D.I. Grubb.

先生，

1939年3月16日晚7时30分左右，桥爪先生（Mr. Hashizume）请求工部局警务处协助搜查沈亨一（Sung Heng Ih，地址为霞飞路671号）和杨剑秋（Yong Chien Chu，地址为亚伦路56号戈登别墅）的住所。

刑事侦缉处长获悉此请求后指示，在日本领事警察提供所需协助的细节后，工部局警务处人员应前往法国警察总部，而日本领事警察则在中央捕房等候，直至工部局警务处申请协助并执行所需搜查。

这些指示由刑事侦缉督察格鲁布（C.D.I. Grubb）传达给桥爪先生，但他拒绝留下，并坚持前往法国警察总部。随后安排桥爪先生前往法国警察总部，在那里他将会见刑事侦缉处长及法国警察政治部副主任乔贝兹先生（Mr. Jobez）。

在法国警察总部，商定由法国警察协助工部局警务处搜查上述地址，而日本领事警察则在骆家威等候。

pages.en:
carried out by the French Police with D.S. Mitsushima
standing by looking for documents mentioned by the
Japanese Consular Police. 36 documents, 9 photographs,
12 visiting cards, 8 invitation cards and one book
were seized and no arrests made.

At about 10.30 p.m. same date the room of Yung
Kyung Sung at 56 Garden Villa, Route de Lion was searched
and 10 documents were seized and no arrests made.

All the seized documents were taken to Hokawei
where they are now being held by the French Police
pending further developments.

The Japanese Consular Police then wished to
search the home of Loong Kyung Sung (   ) at
179 Kweicho Road, but when J.C.I. drugs and party
reached that address they found it was a branch of
the Door of Hope which is a British Missionary
Institution. The Japanese Consular Police were
informed that the premises could not be searched
without a British Court Warrant.

Inquiries were made at the premises and Mrs.
Koong, mother of Loong Kyung Sung, was questioned
and she stated that her son did not reside at that
address although he came to see her daily. She was
under the impression that he cohabited with a girl
at an address on Sinza Road, but she did not know
the exact address. Mrs. Koong is the Chinese
supervisor of this branch of the Door of Hope.

The Japanese Consular Police seemed satisfied

当晚约9时40分，副督察罗兹（D.M. Rhodes）、日本侦探三岛（J.D.S. Mitsushima）、刑事侦缉警长290号及本人，在法国警察人员的陪同下，搜查了霞飞路617号沈亨一的住所。实际搜查工作
（续）
由法国警察执行，日本侦探三岛在一旁守候，寻找日本领事警察提及的文件。搜获文件36份、照片9张、名片12张、请柬8张及书籍一本，无人被捕。

同日晚上约10时30分，搜查了狮子路56号花园别墅杨景松（Yung Kyung Sung）的房间，搜获文件10份，无人被捕。

所有搜获的文件均被带至骆家威，目前由法国警察保管，以待后续发展。

随后，日本领事警察希望搜查桂果路179号龙景松（Loong Kyung Sung，   ）的住所，但当日本领事警察情报员及随行人员到达该地址时，发现那是“救主堂”（Door of Hope）的一个分部，这是一家英国传教机构。日本领事警察被告知，若无英国法院搜查令，不得搜查该处所。

经在该处所查询，并对龙景松的母亲孔太太（Mrs. Koong）进行问话，她表示其子虽每日前来看望她，但并不居住在该地址。她印象中其子与新闸路某地址的一名女子同居，但她不知道确切地址。孔太太是该“救主堂”分部的中方主管。

日本领事警察似乎对

Re: Temporary release of a member
of guerilla unit.

Sir,

I have the pleasure to inform you that
Loh Zung Ching (駱振清), aged 35, a member of
guerilla unit, who was handed over to us from
your police force on May 1, 1939, was released
on September 2, 1939 on guarantee, as he was
suffering from beri-beri and have been emaciated
remarkably.

Yours faithfully,

Sealed : Col. K. Kamaya,

Officer-in-command.

6.

Whilst in the custody of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Loh Zung Ching made a statement
a copy of which is on file (statement No.2.)
In this statement Loh Zung Ching admits that
in Aug. 1938 he became a member of the Peace
Preservation Corps in Hupoo and gives full
particulars of the commanders and personnel
of the various sections of the Corps, which
he states was under the supervision of the
Japanese forces.

Loh Zung Ching was further questioned
by C.B.H.Q. detectives regarding this state-
ment and admits same, except that he now
claims that this corps was not under the supervision
of the Japanese, neither was it a guerrilla
unit, but a purely local organization formed for
the purpose of maintaining peace in the Hupoo
area. It is worthy of note that when questioned
at the time of arrest Loh Zung Ching maintained
that he had resided in Shanghai since the
hostilities and made no mention of ever having
been in Hupoo.

Later, the Japanese Gendarmerie forwarded
to the S.M.P. a report made by Sgt. Kuroji to

6.

罗宗清在日本宪兵队拘留期间曾作出一份供词，副本在案（供词第2号）。在该供词中，罗宗清承认他于1938年8月成为沪东和平维持团的一员，并详细说明了该团各分队指挥官及人员的情况，他称该团受日军监督。

刑事侦缉处总部侦探就这份供词进一步讯问了罗宗清，他予以承认，但此时他声称该团并非受日本监督，也不是游击队单位，而是一个纯粹为了维护沪东地区和平而成立的地方组织。值得注意的是，罗宗清在被捕受审时坚称自战事爆发以来一直居住在上海，只字未提曾去过沪东。

后来，日本宪兵队向工部局警务处转交了黑井军曹（Sgt. Kuroji）所作的一份报告，内容为

pages.en:
6/2.

the effect that he had made enquiries and ascer-
tained that Loh Zung Ching he never been a
member of the Hsupoo Peace Preservation Corps.
The Japanese Gendarmerie also forwarded
the copy of a statement made by Yuen Ming Ping
(袁明斌), the Gendarmerie prisoner who supplied
the information which led to the arrest of Loh
Zung Ching. The gist of this statement is as
follows : -
Yuen Ming Ping had known Loh Zung Ching since
1931 when they were both members of the S.M.P.,
attached to Wayside Station. Yuen again met
Loh in January 1938, and in February 1938, heard
that Loh had left Shanghai for Hsupoo. Hearing
that Loh had returned to Shanghai in Aug. 1938
Yuen visited Loh's home, but the latter was
absent. Yuen was informed by 3 or 4 strangers
whom he met in Loh's home, that Loh had come
from Hsupoo to recruit guerrilla troops, and
had returned to Hsupoo on Aug. 19th, 1938. Yuen
was also later informed by Loh's wife that Loh
was employed as adjutant to a guerrilla leader named
Weo Vang Sing (吴文信).

D. S. I.
pages.zh:
6/2.

称其已进行调查并查明，骆振清（Loh Zung Ching）从未曾是沪西保安团（Hsupoo Peace Preservation Corps）的成员。日本宪兵队还转来了一份由袁明斌（Yuen Ming Ping）所作的陈述副本，袁是宪兵队的囚犯，正是他提供了导致骆振清被捕的情报。该陈述的要点如下：

袁明斌自1931年起便认识骆振清，当时两人均为隶属于路边巡捕房（Wayside Station）的工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警员。袁于1938年1月再次遇见骆，并于1938年2月听说骆已离开上海前往沪西（Hsupoo）。听说骆于1938年8月返回上海后，袁曾拜访骆的住所，但骆不在家。袁在骆的家中遇到的三四个陌生人告知他，骆是从沪西来招募游击队员的，并已于1938年8月19日返回沪西。袁后来还从骆的妻子处得知，骆受雇于一位名为吴文信（Weo Vang Sing，音译）的游击队首领，担任副官。

D. S. I.

LOH LUNG CHING (駱隆清)
Hupeh
acting in the capacity of a Judicial Police Officer,
Rep.Gend.R.C.           17-3-39
xx Provost Sgt. Risuke Kurouji,
Soo Chen Dai (蘇陳戴)

My name is Loh Lung Ching, aged 35, native of
Chiang Loh Lieu Village (姜駱樓村), 5 li to the south-west of
Tsing-fung Hsien (清豐縣), Hupeh Province, employed by the
Hollywood Club and residing at No. 31 Yoong Zeu Li (永壽里),
Amoy Road, Shanghai.

I have never served as a soldier in the Chinese Army
I was born at the above-mentioned place and studied
from 9 to 12 years old at a private school there. Between the
age of 13 and 19 I stayed home and engaged in farming. When
I was 20 years old, I came to Shanghai and worked for four
years as a cook in the cotton spinning company in Shanghai.
I lived with a friend of mine named Tsang Yue Ching (鄭有金)
on Robison Road. When I was 25 years old I joined the S.M.P.
but resigned after serving for 7 years, for I had to return
to my native place to look after domestic affairs owing to my
mother's death. When I was 33 years old, I came to Shanghai
again and entered the Police Bureau of the Greater Shanghai
City Government through the introduction of Tsang Zung Tsung
(張仁証), owner of Dong Tah (同泰) Cigarettes Shop,
Singapore Road. I had to leave the post after working for less
than two months due to the outbreak of the present Sino-
Japanese hostilities. Then I lived with my father-in-law
named Loh Tsang Er Mau (駱張二毛), proprietor of a Chinese Food
Shop at the above-mentioned address, helping his business.
In August last year, I entered the Peace Preserva-
tion Corps at Hsu Poo (許浦), being recommended by someone
but on December 9, I resigned owing to the illness of my
pages.zh:
骆隆清（LOH LUNG CHING）
湖北
以司法警察官身份行事，
中华民国宪兵队代表           1939年3月17日
xx 纠察中士 黑氏理助（Risuke Kurouji），
苏陈戴（Soo Chen Dai，音译）

我叫骆隆清，现年35岁，籍贯湖北省清丰县姜骆楼村（Chiang Loh Lieu Village，音译），该村位于县城西南五里处。我受雇于好莱坞俱乐部（Hollywood Club），居住在上海爱麦虞介路（Amoy Road）永寿里（Yoong Zeu Li）31号。

我从未在中国军队中服过兵役。
我出生于上述地点，9至12岁时在当地私塾读书。13至19岁期间，我留在家中务农。20岁时，我来到上海，在上海的一家棉纺公司当了四年厨师。我与一位名叫郑有金（Tsang Yue Ching）的朋友同住罗宾森路（Robison Road）。25岁时，我加入工部局警务处（S.M.P.），但在服役七年后辞职，因为母亲去世，我必须回老家处理家务。33岁时，我再次来到上海，通过新加坡路（Singapore Road）同泰（Dong Tah）烟纸店老板张仁証（Tsang Zung Tsung）的介绍，进入大上海市政府警察局工作。由于当前中日战事爆发，我在职不到两个月便不得不离职。此后，我与岳父骆张二毛（Loh Tsang Er Mau，音译）同住，他是上述地址一家中式食品店的店主，我协助他经营生意。去年八月，经人推荐，我进入许浦（Hsu Poo）保安团，但因岳父生病，于12月9日辞职并来到上海。我在好莱坞俱乐部找到工作以维持生计，直至被捕时一直受雇于此。

关于保安团的情况。

(1). 我认识许浦保安团成员吴之信（Woo Vung Sing，音译）已有五六年。吴之信的侄子陈得标（Zung Tuh Pian，音译）与我岳父是同乡，每当他来上海时，常到我家拜访。1938年8月8日，陈得标拜访我，请求我陪同他前往许浦，商讨其叔父正计划组建保安团的事宜。由于我当时失业，便同意了，并于当日与陈得标一同前往许浦见吴之信。

(2). 当我见到吴之信时，他命令我在许浦招募保安团成员，为此我从吴之信处收到150.00美元。他们还劝说我加入该团，我接受了，月薪为20.00美元。

(3). 1938年8月13日，我返回上海招募成员。通过与我在上海的朋友合作，我成功招募了23名年龄在22至36岁之间的失业人员。我按每人2.20美元支付了路费。到达许浦时，我身上只剩9.00美元。我告诉 recruits（新兵），他们的月薪将是10.00美元 ____

father-in-law and came to Shanghai. I found my employment
with the Hollywood Club to earn my living, where I had been
employed until the time of arrest.

In Connection with the Peace Preservation Corps.

(1). I have been acquainted with Woo Vung Sing (吳之信),
member of the Peace Preservation Corps in Hsu Poo for 5 or 6
years. Zung Tuh Pian (陳得標), nephew of Woo Vung Sing, being
a man from the same country as my father-in-law, used to call
at our home whenever he had occasion to come to Shanghai.
On August 8, 1938, Zung Tuh Pian called on me and requested me
to accompany him to Hsu Poo to discuss the matter concerning
the organisation of a Peace Preservation Corps which his uncle
was planning. As I was then unemployed I agreed and went
on that date together with Zung Tuh Pian to Hsu Poo to see Woo
Vung Sing.

(2). When I met Woo Vung Sing he ordered me to recruit
members of the Peace Preservation Corps in Hsu Poo and for that
purpose I received a sum of $150.00 from Woo Vung Sing. They
also persuaded me to enlist with the Corps, which I accepted
at a pay of $20.00 per mensem.

(3). On 13-8-38 I returned to Shanghai to recruit members.
Working in conjunction with my friends in Shanghai, I managed
to recruit 23 men, who were unemployed and of ages between 22
and 36 years. I paid $2.20 per head for the passage
accordingly. I had only $9.00 when I arrived at Hsu Poo. I
told the recruits that their pay will be $10.00 per mensem.

Zau Bei Faung (趙培芳), are about 48 years, is the commander of the Hsu Poo Peace Preservation Corps. He resides at Hsu Poo and supervises duties performed by the members.
Tsang Mo Fung (張慕芳), age 36 years, is a company commander of the Hsu Poo Peace Preservation Corps. He resides in Hsu Poo and works as a tax collector in Hsu Poo and in outlying districts.

organized on or about September 20, last year, and is

Means of Communication.
The Peace Preservation Corps of Hsu Poo is an
independent organisation and has no communication with other
Corps.
....................
Question : Is the Hsu Poo Peace Preservation Corps connected
with the Japanese Force?
Answer : It is working under the supervision of the Japanese
Force. Whenever the Japanese launch mopping-up operations in
our districts against the guerillas, members of the Corps act
as guides on those occasions. We are supplied with arm bands
bearing the inscription "Great Japan".
Question : What is the character of Woo Vung Sing?
Answer : Woo Vung Sing and Tsang Mo Faung are relatives.
Following the occupation of Hsu Poo by the Japanese Force,
Tsang Mo Faung introduced Woo Vung Sing to the Japanese and
the latter became the follower of the Japanese Force. I do
not know what he was doing during the hostilities, but I know
that he was a peddler of provisions.
Question : What is the character of Kuh Shu Hwa (葛學華)?
Answer : Kuh Shu Hwa and Woo Vung Sing were doing same
business and were always together in their movements, but Kuh
was not connected with the Peace Preservation Corps.
Question : Do you know Kuh Shu Hwa and Woo Vung Sing were
pages.zh:
- 5 -
去年9月20日左右，其职能是为许浦及其他七个村庄维持治安和秩序。
通讯方式。
许浦保安团是一个独立的组织，与其他保安团没有通讯联络 ____ 
问：许浦保安团是否与日军有关联？
答：它在日军的监督下运作。每当日军在我们辖区对游击队进行扫荡作战时，保安团成员会在这些场合充当向导。我们获发印有“大日本”字样的臂章。
问：吴永信（Woo Vung Sing，音译）的为人如何？
答：吴永信与张慕芳（Tsang Mo Faung，音译，前文为Tsang Mo Fung）是亲戚。在日军占领许浦后，张慕芳将吴永信介绍给日本人，后者随后成为日军的追随者。我不知道他在战事期间做过什么，但我知道他曾是一名食品小贩。
问：葛学华（Kuh Shu Hwa）的为人如何？
答：葛学华与吴永信从事相同的生意，行动总是保持一致，但葛与保安团没有关联。
问：你是否知道葛学华和吴永信是

pages.en:
- 6 -

former members of the Mobile Unit, and that they were
connected with Yoong Chien Tung (甌劍東)?
Answer : I do not know whether they were connected with the
Mobile Unit, but personally I do not think so.
Question : Why did you hesitate to admit Kuh Shu Hwa's
address on the day of your arrest?
Answer : I could not recollect Kuh Shu Hwa's address, which
was written on his name card, given to me two years ago when
he had visited my wife's father who was then lying in bed
suffering from lung trouble. On arrival at the S.M. Police
Station, I recollected his address. The address which I
admitted as Kuh's was his concubine's home. My wife's father
and Kuh were born in the same province, and have been
acquainted for many years. It seems to me that Kuh is 56 or
57 years old.
Question : Did you give any assistance to the members of the
Corps?
Answer : I recruited 20 men as Zangzoh Police on request
made by Zung (陳) (?), Cantonese, who arrived in Shanghai
from Zangzoh in May last year and who was introduced to me
by my friend named Zee Tuh Piau (徐得標). I also went to
Zangzoh together with the recruits. At that time I received
$2.00 in Shanghai and $3.00 in Zangzoh.
Question : Have you anything else to state?
Answer : No.
............................

pages.zh:

前流动部队（Mobile Unit）成员，且他们与甌劍東（Yoong Chien Tung，音译）有关联？
答：我不知道他们是否与流动部队有关联，但我个人并不这么认为。
问：为什么你在被捕当天犹豫不肯承认葛学华的住址？
答：我记不起葛学华的住址了，那是写在名片上的，这张名片是两年前他来看望我卧病在床、患有肺病的岳父时给我的。到达工部局警务处（S.M. Police Station）后，我想起了他的住址。我所承认的葛的住址是他妾室的住所。我的岳父与葛是同省人，相识多年。在我看来，葛大约56或57岁。
问：你是否向保安团成员提供过任何协助？
答：应一名去年五月从庄桥（Zangzoh，音译）来到上海、由我的朋友徐得标（Zee Tuh Piau）介绍给我的广东人陈（Zung，音译）的请求，我招募了20名庄桥警察。我还随同这些 recruits（新兵）一起去了庄桥。当时我在上海收到2.00美元，在庄桥收到3.00美元。
问：你还有其它要陈述的吗？
答：没有 ____

Sir,

At 6 p.m. 15.3.39, in accordance with the instructions of D.C. (Crime) assistance was rendered to Japanese Gendarmerie.

Sgt. Major Hikiji brought to C.M.R. (W.I.) a Chinese prisoner named Yuen Ming Sing (袁明斌) and stated that this man was a member of a guerrilla unit which operated around Nangzoh. He had been arrested by the Japanese Gendarmerie in the Western Area of Shanghai on 27.2.39 and had implicated one named Loh Zung Ching (駱振清) living at House 21 Lane 161 Amoy Road as an accomplice. Sgt. Major Hikiji requested assistance to arrest Loh Zung Ching and stated that according to the information supplied by his prisoner, this man could supply information regarding another man named Kuh Shu Hwa (高書華), who was also wanted for being a member of the same guerrilla unit.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I. Fryde, D.S. Rhodes, D.S. Sugimoto and D.C. Yamahara, D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung, C.D.S. 85 and 172 accordingly, and Loh Zung Ching arrested at 6.30 a.m. 16.3.39 in a downstairs back room of the stated address. A search of the room was made and the only property seized was

17 name cards in the name of Loh Zung Ching
One scribbling pad with "Chiang Kai Shih" written in Chinese characters on one page.

先生：

1939年3月15日下午6时，遵照刑事处副主任的指示，向日本宪兵队提供了协助。

宪兵曹长樋路（Hikiji，音译）将一名名为袁明斌（Yuen Ming Sing）的中国囚犯带至西区中央捕房，并称此人是活跃于南翔（Nangzoh，音译）一带的游击队成员。他于1939年2月27日被日本宪兵队在上海西区逮捕，并供出一名住在爱麦虞介路（Amoy Road）161弄21号的骆振清（Loh Zung Ching）为同伙。樋路曹长请求协助逮捕骆振清，并称根据其囚犯提供的信息，此人还能提供关于另一名名为高书华（Kuh Shu Hwa）的男子的信息，高书华也因是同一游击队成员而遭通缉。

副督察长弗赖德、侦探罗德（Rhodes）、侦探杉本（Sugimoto）及警员山原（Yamahara，音译）、副督察长宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung）、便衣警员85号和172号随即提供了协助，并于1939年3月16日上午6时30分在上述地址楼下的一间后屋内逮捕了骆振清。对该房间进行了搜查，仅查获以下物品：

印有骆振清姓名的名片17张
一本涂写簿，其中一页上用汉字写着“蒋介石”。

The remainder of the rooms in the house were

The arrested , Loh Yung Ching, was removed

Questioning of Loh Yung Ching revealed that he
knew Kuh Shu Hw, but had not seen him since January
1939. That he did not know this man's exact where-
abouts, but had once seen a name card of this man
giving the address "4 Hung Tuh Li, (洪德里) Chekiang
Road". This address which proved to be 609/4 Chekiang
Road was raided at 8 a.m. where it was ascertained
that the wife of Kuh Shu Hw lived there, but the
wanted man had left for Hongpu three days ago.
search of the room was made and Japanese Naval
Landing Party pass for Hongkew, bearing the female's
photograph and one letter addressed to Kuh Shu Hw
were seized.

The arrested man Loh Yung Ching was previously
C.P.C. 2112 attached to Cent. Station, and states
that he absconded from the Force about 10 years ago.
He returned to Shanghai just prior to the Sino-

随后查看了该房屋内的其他房间，日本宪兵队的囚犯辨认了屋内居住者，但未认出其他任何被通缉的男子 ed uh au（原文不清）。

被捕者骆振清（Loh Yung Ching，音译，与前文骆振清为同一人）被送往中央医院，应樋路少校（Lt. Major Hikiji）的要求，第179号便衣警员连同工部局警务处的几名警员留在爱麦虞介路161/21号，以防在审讯骆振清关于高书华（Kuh Shu Hw）下落期间有人离开该房屋。

对骆振清的审讯显示，他认识高书华，但自1939年1月以来未再见过面。他不知道此人的确切下落，但曾见过此人的一张名片，上面写的地址是“浙江路洪德里4号”。该地址经查实为浙江路609/4号，于上午8时遭到突击搜查，查明高书华的妻子住在那里，但该被通缉男子已于三天前前往虹口（Hongpu，即虹口）。对房间进行了搜查，缴获了一张带有该女子照片的进入虹口的日本海军陆战队通行证，以及一封写给高书华的信。

被捕男子骆振清此前是隶属于中央巡捕房的第2112号中国巡捕，并称他大约在10年前从警队潜逃。他在中日战事爆发前夕回到上海，但一直失业，直到约3个月前才在豫园路（Yu Yuen Road）的“好莱坞赌场”找到一份苦力的工作。他否认曾参与任何游击队活动。

上午8时10分，警员山原和便衣警员172号从爱麦虞介路161/29号撤离。

樋路曹长称，此案是就1939年3月8日进行的逮捕行动（案件编号 C.1.25/39）进行进一步调查的结果。

February 29, 1939.

Dear Brother Yah Hwa,

I have to thank you from the bottom
of my heart for the sum of money you presented to
me last year.

We have now entered into a new year,
and I do hope that you would be enjoying the best
of your health and luck the year round.

It was my intention, to come to Shanghai
at the beginning of the 1st. Moon and see you regarding
those plans which you have formulated in respect of
the "fish" business for the new Spring Season, however,
my prolonged illness prevented me from doing so.

You are thereby requested to supply me a
brief idea of your plans, so that I may handle the
rest at the first available chance. It would be best,
however, for you to come to "Ling" (place) yourself and
discuss the matter with me in details.

Awaiting your reply & wishing you a very
happy new year,

Your loving brother,
Signed : MA YUEN WOO.
pages.zh:
1939年2月29日。

亲爱的亚华兄：

我衷心感谢你去年赠予我的那笔钱款。

我们要进入新的一年了，我希望你全年都能享有最佳的健康和运气。

我本打算在正月初来到上海，与你商讨你为新春季节制定的关于“鱼”生意的计划，然而，我的久病使我未能成行。

因此，请你向我简要介绍你的计划，以便我在第一时间有机会处理后续事宜。不过，最好还是请你亲自到“灵”（Ling，音译，地点）来，与我详细讨论此事。

等候你的回复，并祝你新年快乐，

爱弟，
签名：马元武（MA YUEN WOO，音译）。

    Reference to attached application for assistance to

at 6 a.m. 18.3.39, as per previous arrangements, and after

was no such number as Lane 341, and that this number belonged

Woo (大沪) Hotel, the number of which is 343.
    Owing to the close proximity of this hotel and as a
mistake may have been made in the number, it was decided to

Sung Kung (李润耕), about one year ago, and that it was at
present occupied by two of his relatives named Lee Nyoh Ting
(李妙汀), age 60, native of Kiangying, M/dye-merchant, and
Tse Ping Yee (朱品彝), age 46, native of Wusieh, M/rubber
merchant, who had occupied same for the period already mentioned
As none of these names corresponded to the name given by the
Japanese Consular Police, also as the address was incorrect,
and a search failing to produce anything of an incriminating n
nature, these persons, who appeared to be of very respectable
character, were not arrested.

however, when this address (351 Boulevard de Montigny) was

    关于所附协助搜查法租界爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII）341弄5号大公（Dah Kung）酒店418房间的援助申请，具名人偕同侦探松岛（Matsushima，音译）、代理首席侦探督察黄东武（Wong Tung Woo，音译）、便衣警员115号及便衣警员，按照事先安排，于1939年3月18日上午6时前往卢家湾警察局，在获得必要协助后，前往上述地址。然而，到达那里后发现并没有341弄这个号码，该号码属于一家位于大沪（Dah Woo）酒店隔壁的中国匹头店，其门牌号为343号。
    由于该酒店与上述地点非常邻近，且可能是号码搞错了，决定去查看同一酒店的418房间。然而，经查发现，该房间已由酒店老板李润耕（Lee Sung Kung）于大约一年前租出，目前由他的两名亲属居住，分别是：李妙汀（Lee Nyoh Ting，音译），60岁，江苏江阴人，染料商；朱品彝（Tse Ping Yee，音译），46岁，无锡人，橡胶商。他们已在此居住了前述的时间。由于这些名字均与日本领事馆警察提供的名字不符，且地址不正确，搜查也未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品，这些看起来品行端正的人未被逮捕。

April 29, 39
7

Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie.

At 9 a.m. 23.4.39, D.S. Sugimoto of Crime
Branch Headquarters received information from Sgt.
Major Katodo of the Japanese Gendarmerie to the effect
that they had been successful in locating the male
Chinese named Siau Dee (小弟), who according to the
statement of Tai Ah Dong (戴阿董) had overheard
the conversation between himself and Zung Ah Kyung
(陳阿金) in Room 536 of the Far Eastern Hotel on
or about 26th. February, 1939, when they discussed the
plan to assassinate Mr. Chen Chuan (陳群), Minister
of the Interior to the Reformed Government.

At time of passing this information to D.S.
Sugimoto, Sgt. Major Katode requested that the under-
signed attend the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters for
purpose of questioning this man.

Having accepted this invitation the under-
signed accompanied by D.S.Sugimoto, proceeded to the
Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters, Bridge House, North
Szechuen Road and there questioned one named Tsung Sih
Liang (鍾錫良), alias Ah Sai (阿三), alias Siau
Dee (小弟), m/chauffeur, residing 131 Rue Jansire,
French Concession, and at present employed as a m/truck
driver for the Shanghai City Government, Civic Centre.

编号 S H D. 8297/39

C.1, 刑事处总部。

C.1 杂项 35/39
1939年4月29日
7

协助日本宪兵队。

1939年4月23日上午9时，刑事处总部的侦探杉本收到日本宪兵队加藤（Katodo，音译）曹长的通知，称他们已成功找到一名名为小弟（Siau Dee）的中国男子。据戴阿董（Tai Ah Dong）陈述，他于1939年2月26日左右在远东饭店536房间无意中听到了小弟与陈阿金（Zung Ah Kyung）之间的谈话，当时他们讨论了刺杀维新政府内政部长陈群（Chen Chuan）先生的计划。

在向侦探杉本传递此信息时，加藤曹长请求具名人前往日本宪兵队总部，目的是审讯此人。

接受邀请后，具名人偕同侦探杉本前往位于北四川路大桥公寓的日本宪兵队总部，并在那里审讯了一名名为钟锡良（Tsung Sih Liang），别名阿三（Ah Sai），别名小弟（Siau Dee）的男子，职业司机，居住在法租界贾西业路（Rue Jansire，音译）131号，目前受雇于上海市政府市中心区，担任卡车司机。

pages.en:
C.1 Misc.35/39

7/2

In replying to questions put to him, this
man corroborated the written statement made by him
to the Japanese Authorities, a copy of which is here-
with attached for information.

A perusal of this statement shows that this
man did overhear Tai Ah Dong discuss with Zung Ah Kyung
the plan for the suggested assassination of Mr. Chen
Chuen, but that he did not hear any mention made of Yee
Vung Ching (葉文清) nor had he ever met this man, which
although corroborating the statement of Tai Ah Dong to
a certain extent, yet does not appear to alter the
present position of Yee Vung Ching, who is at present
still detained in the Police Hospital.

John Laydal
D.S.I.
pages.zh:
C.1 杂项 35/39

7/2

在回答向他提出的问题时，此人证实了他向日本当局所作的书面陈述，副本随函附上以供参考。

查阅该陈述显示，此人确实无意中听到戴阿董与陈阿金讨论建议刺杀陈群（Chen Chuen，即陈群）先生的计划，但他没有听到提及叶文清（Yee Vung Ching），也从未见过此人。这虽然在一定程度上证实了戴阿董的陈述，但似乎并未改变叶文清目前的处境，叶文清目前仍被羁押在警察医院。

约翰·莱德尔（John Laydal，音译）
副督察长

Assistance to Japanese Military Police
Headquarters.

Reference to instructions of Commissioner of Police issued on the 28.3.39 re the handing over of the male Chinese Yee Vung Ching (姜文清) to the Japanese Gendarmerie for a period of two days, the undersigned, accompanied by D.S. Sugimoto, escorted this man to the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters located at Bridge House, North Szechuen Road, at 9.30 a.m. 29.3.39, where he was handed over to the custody of Sgt. Major Katodo, against his signed receipt (attached).

The conditions relating to the handing over having previously been explained to Lieut. Toita by D.I. Nakamura there was no further need to repeat this, however the undersigned through D.S. Sugimoto enquired from Sgt. Major Katodo whether or not he had been made familiar with these conditions and was answered in the affirmative.

During the ensuing conversation, Sgt. Major Katodo, through D.S. Sugimoto, requested the undersigned to first question their prisoner, Tai Ah Dong (戴阿堂) re the statement made by him to the Japanese Gendarmerie in Nanking on the 21.3.39, and on the undersigned agreeing

1939年4月1日
5

协助日本军警总部。

关于警察总监于1939年3月28日发出的指示，涉及将中国男子姜文清（Yee Vung Ching，此处中文名与上文不同，照录）移交给日本宪兵队两天一事，具名人偕同侦探杉本，于1939年3月29日上午9时30分将该男子护送至位于北四川路大桥公寓的日本宪兵队总部，并将其移交给加藤（Katodo）曹长保管，由其签署收据（附后）。

由于中村（Nakamura）侦探督察此前已向户田（Toita，音译）中尉解释了移交的相关条件，因此无需再次重复，但具名人通过侦探杉本询问加藤曹长是否熟悉这些条件，得到了肯定的答复。

在随后的谈话中，加藤曹长通过侦探杉本，请求具名人首先审讯他们的囚犯戴阿堂（Tai Ah Dong，此处中文名与上文略有不同，照录），内容是关于他于1939年3月21日在南京向日本宪兵队所作的陈述，在具名人同意

5/2

to do so, the S.M.P. prisoner Yee Vung Ching was removed
from the office and Tai Ah Dong brought in.
This man when questioned by the undersigned, made
a verbal statement to the effect that he first became
acquainted with Yee Vung Ching in June, 1933, whilst
the latter, then employed as a truck driver by Gordon
& Co. was delivering building material to a building
in the course of erection in the vicinity of his (Tai)
master's residence, and that after several such meetings
they became close friends. Continuing, Tai Ah Dong
explained that prior to the outbreak of the present
Sino-Japanese hostilities he purchased a motor car
licence No.1597 (later changed to 9967), and with same,
frequently touted for hire outside the Central Hotel.
After the outbreak of hostilities he sold his motor car
and returned to his native place, Yeu Yao (餘姚) in
Chekiang Province, where he remained for three months.
Returning to Shanghai, he remained unemployed
until June, 1938, when he visited Nanking, and along
with a friend named Yuen Tsin-jih (俞譚吉) commenced
trading in old motor car tyres, which they purchased in
Nanking and then resold in Shanghai. In carrying out
this business it was his usual practice to visit Shanghai
about twice every month and on such occasions he invariably called on Yee Vung Ching at his home, situated at
pages.zh:
5/2

这样做之后，工部局警务处的囚犯叶文清被带离办公室，戴阿董被带入。
此人在接受具名人审讯时，作了口头陈述，大意是他于1933年6月首次结识叶文清，当时后者受雇于戈登公司（Gordon & Co.）担任卡车司机，正在向他（戴）主人的住所附近一处正在建造的建筑运送建筑材料，经过几次这样的会面后，他们成为了密友。戴阿董继续解释说，在目前的中日敌对状态爆发之前，他购买了一辆汽车，牌照号为1597（后改为9967），并经常开着这辆车在中央饭店外揽客。敌对状态爆发后，他卖掉了汽车，回到了家乡浙江省余姚（Yeu Yao），在那里呆了三个月。
回到上海后，他一直失业，直到1938年6月，他前往南京，并与一位名为俞谭吉（Yuen Tsin-jih，音译）的朋友开始做旧汽车轮胎生意，他们在南京购买轮胎，然后在上海转售。在开展这项业务时，他通常每月去上海约两次，每次 invariably（总是）去叶文清位于……的家中拜访

pages.en:
5/3

159 Taku Road.
Recalling his last visit to Shanghai, Tai Ah Dong
explained that on or about the 6th. or 7th. January,
1939, he arrived in Shanghai, and after disposing of
five tyres he had brought with him, he took up residence
at Room 44 of the Nanking Lodging House, Avenue Edward
VII, and that the following morning at about 12 noon,
he visited the home of Yee Vung Ching at 159 Taku Road.
On this occasion he met Yee Vung Ching, his wife, mother,
and child, and at their request had lunch with them,
after which he left with Yee who, during the ensuing
conversation, requested him to meet him (Yee) at 8 p.m.
that evening in the Great World Amusement centre, Avenue
Edward VII. Continuing, he explained how he accepted
the invitation and at 8 p.m. that evening he kept the
appointment, meeting Yee Vung Ching on the 2nd. floor
of the Great World, where, after watching various
theatricals, they descended to the roadway and commenced
walking west along Avenue Edward VII. During this time
Yee Vung Ching mentioned to him that as he was always
in Nanking and had many friends amongst the chauffeurs
employed in the various ministries, it would be a
simple matter for him to obtain information concerning
the movements of the different ministers, particularly
pages.zh:
5/3

大沽路159号。
戴阿东（Tai Ah Dong）在回顾其上次上海之行时解释说，他于1939年1月6日或7日左右抵达上海，在处理完随身携带的五条轮胎后，入住爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）南京旅社44号房间。次日上午约12时，他前往大沽路159号叶荣庆（Yee Vung Ching，音译）的住所。此次他见到了叶荣庆及其妻子、母亲和孩子，并应其邀请与他们共进午餐。餐后他与叶一同离开，在随后的交谈中，叶要求他于当晚8点在爱多亚路的大世界游乐中心与他会面。戴继续陈述道，他接受了邀请，并于当晚8点赴约，在大世界二楼见到叶荣庆。在观看了一些戏剧演出后，他们下楼来到马路上，开始沿爱多亚路向西行走。在此期间，叶荣庆向他提及，由于自己常驻南京，且在各部受雇的司机中有许多朋友，因此获取各位部长的行踪信息，特别是

pages.en:
5/4

when they intended visiting Shanghai, and that if he
could obtain such information and pass it to him (Yee),
they would be rewarded to the extent of $10,000.00 or
$20,000.00. In replying to this suggestion, Tai Ah
Dong states that he agreed to the proposal, but only in
a light-hearted manner as he did not think Yee was in
earnest, and was merely joking. According to Tai no
further meeting or discussion in regard to the aforegoing
took place until on or about the 16th. February 1939,
when he was visited in Room 44 of the Nanking Lodging
House by Yee who, during the course of the conversation,
again brought up the matter of obtaining information
regarding Reformed Government officials in Nanking, and
mentioned that it would be an easy way of making a large
amount of money. Again Tai agreed and mentioned that
he had a friend named Zung Ah Kyung (陳阿金) who was
employed as a chauffeur to the Minister of the Interior
and that if he could approach this man, they might be
able to gain the necessary information.
The third occasion on which any mention was made
in regard to the aforegoing took place on the afternoon
of 22nd. February (3rd. day of Chinese New Year) when,
according to Tai, he, along with Yee Vung Ching and
another named Yang Kung Sung (楊根生), a business
associate, all met in Room 44 of the Nanking Lodging
pages.zh:
5/4

当他们打算访问上海时的行踪，对他来说易如反掌；如果他能获得此类信息并转交给他（叶），他们将获得10,000.00美元或20,000.00美元的酬金。戴阿东在回应这一提议时表示，他同意了该建议，但只是出于玩笑心态，因为他认为叶并非认真，仅仅是在开玩笑。据戴称，在此之后直到1939年2月16日左右，双方未再就上述事项进行会面或讨论。当日，叶来到南京旅社44号房间拜访他，在谈话过程中再次提起获取南京维新政府官员信息一事，并称这是赚取巨额钱财的简便途径。戴再次表示同意，并提到他有一位名叫陈阿金（Zung Ah Kyung）的朋友，在内政部担任部长司机，如果能接触此人，他们或许能获取所需信息。
第三次提及上述事项是在2月22日下午（农历正月初三），据戴称，他与叶荣庆以及另一位名为杨根生（Yang Kung Sung）的商业伙伴在南京旅社44号房间

pages.en:
5/5

House, and after some conversation, decided to visit
the Strand Cinema on Ningpo Road. All three proceeded
to this theatre but were unable to gain admission, hence
they next proceeded to the Lido Theatre on Peking Road,
but again failed to gain admission, owing to a full
house. All three then decided to return to the Nanking
Lodging House, where, a short time after their arrival
Yee expressed a desire to return home and left . Accord-
ing to Tai Ah Dong no discussion in regard to their
previous conversation took place on this occasion.
The last occasion on which he met Yee Vung Ching
was at about 8.30 p.m. 23.2.39 (5th. day of Chinese
New Year) when the latter called on him at Room 44
Nanking Lodging House and requested him to go out for
dinner. Owing to a previous dinner engagement Tai
expressed his inability to do so, and Yee left, prior
to which he again reminded him of his promise, and also
requested that he keep it secret.
In continuing, Tai Ah Dong related how that since
that time he had not seen Yee Vung Ching, but that at
about 8 p.m. on the 26th. February 1938 (8th. day of
Chinese New Year), when visiting a friend named Saung
(桑) at Room 536 of the Far Eastern Hotel, Yu Ya Ching
Road, he unexpectedly met Zung Ah Kyung in the elevator,
who, after exchanging greetings, enquired of him where
pages.zh:
5/5

会面，经过一番交谈后，决定前往宁波路上的斯特兰德电影院（Strand Cinema）。三人前往该影院，但未能入场，随后又前往北京路上的丽都大戏院（Lido Theatre），但因满座再次未能入场。于是三人决定返回南京旅社，抵达不久后，叶表示想回家便离开了。据戴阿东称，此次并未就之前的谈话内容进行任何讨论。
他最后一次见到叶荣庆是在1939年2月23日晚上8点30分左右（农历正月初五），当时叶到南京旅社44号房间拜访他，并邀他外出共进晚餐。因已有晚餐约会，戴表示无法前往，叶随即离开。在此之前，叶再次提醒他履行承诺，并要求他保守秘密。
戴阿东接着叙述，自那以后他便未再见过叶荣庆。但在1938年2月26日晚上8点左右（农历正月初八），当他去亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road）远东饭店536号房间拜访一位姓桑（Saung）的朋友时，在电梯里意外遇到了陈阿金。互相寒暄后，陈询问他要去哪里。

pages.en:
5/6

he was going. Tai replied that he intended visiting
a friend in Room 536 and invited Zung and his friend
who was then in his company to call at that room later.
After two hours Zung Ah Kyung and his friend called at
Room 536, and some time later, he, Tai, informed him
quietly about a certain friend (no name mentioned) who
had requested him to get information regarding the
movements of Reformed Government officials. Zung Ah Kyung
immediately informed him not to be stupid to attempt
such a thing and the matter was dropped there and then.
On or about March 11th. 1939, Tai returned to
Nanking and on arrival was informed that on the 8th.
March 1939, a chauffeur No.23 named Yung Sz (      )
of the Ministry of Home Affairs had called there stating
that Zung Ah Kyung would like to see him, as the minister's
wife had bought a new car and wanted a good chauffeur
and that Zung Ah Kyung wanted to recommend him for the
job. The following day Tai went to the ministry for the
purpose of seeing Zung, but was refused admission by the
sentries, and after three other attempts to see Zung,
all of which were abortive, he finally wrote him a
letter informing him of his return to Nanking and re-
questing an interview regarding the promised position of
chauffeur.
At about 9 a.m. 18.3.39, in response to this letter,
pages.zh:
5/6

戴回答说打算去536号房间拜访一位朋友，并邀请陈及其当时的同伴稍后也去该房间。两小时后，陈阿金及其朋友来到536号房间。过了一会儿，戴私下告诉他，有一位朋友（未提及姓名）曾请求他获取关于维新政府官员行踪的信息。陈阿金立即告诉他，试图做这种事是愚蠢的，此事便就此作罢。
1939年3月11日左右，戴返回南京，抵达后得知内政部一名编号为23号的司机雍某（Yung Sz，原文不清）曾于1939年3月8日到访，称陈阿金想见他，因为部长的夫人买了一辆新车，需要一名优秀的司机，陈阿金想推荐他担任此职。次日，戴前往部里欲见陈，但被哨兵拒绝入内。在另外三次试图见陈均告失败后，他最终给陈写了一封信，告知其已返回南京，并请求就此前许诺的司机职位进行面谈。
1939年3月18日上午9点左右，作为对这封信的回复，

pages.en:
5/7

Chauffeur No.23 again called at his address in Nanking
and requested him to accompany him back to the Ministry
where Zung Ah Kyung was waiting for him. Accordingly
Tai proceeded to the Ministry in a motor car driven
by Chauffeur No.23.

On arrival at the Ministry and on entering the
compound, Chauffeur No.23 asked him to wait a few
moments and that he would find where Zung had gone.
After waiting about one hour, a large motor car carrying
a Chinese female, and two male Chinese and a Japanese
dressed in foreign dress, came towards him from across
the compound and, stopping in front of him, the chauffeur
(unknown) asked him if he was the chauffeur from Shanghai.
On replying in the affirmative, this chauffeur told him
to jump in and that he would take him to see Zung Ah Kyung
He did so, and was driven to the Military Academy in
Nanking, where every one alighted and he was told to
wait beside the car. The others including the chauffeur
then entered the building and after an elapse of about
20 minutes the Chinese female and the chauffeur returned.
The latter then informed him that he had to take his
employer's wife out on urgent business, but that if he
(Tai) went upstairs and sat down for a little time he
would inform Zung Ah Kyung of his arrival. Continuing
his statement, explained how he, Tai complied with these
pages.zh:
5/7

23号司机再次来到他在南京的住处，请他陪同返回部里，陈阿金正在那里等他。于是，戴乘坐由23号司机驾驶的汽车前往部里。
抵达部里并进入大院后，23号司机让他稍等片刻，说他去寻找陈的去向。等待约一小时后，一辆载有一名中国女性、两名中国男性和一名身穿西式服装的日本人的大型汽车从大院对面驶来，停在他面前。该车司机（身份不明）问他是否是从上海来的司机。得到肯定答复后，该司机让他上车，说会带他去见陈阿金。戴照做了，随后被载至南京中央军校，众人下车，他被吩咐在车旁等候。其他人包括司机随后进入大楼。约20分钟后，那名中国女性和司机返回。后者随后告诉他，他必须送雇主夫人出去处理紧急事务，但如果戴上楼坐一会儿，他会通知陈阿金戴已到达。戴在继续陈述中解释了他如何遵从这些

pages.en:
5/8

instructions and entered a sitting room on the 2nd.
floor, where he sat down on a settle to await the
arrival of Zung. After about half an hour three Chinese
and a Japanese entered the room and began questioning
him regarding his arrival from Shanghai and whether or
not he had come alone, or was accompanied by any others.
On replying that he had arrived in Nanking on the 11.3.39
and that he was alone, he was next questioned as to where
the bombs and pistols which he had brought from Shanghai,
were being kept. Pleading ignorance to this, he was
immediately set upon and severely beaten, after which
he was held down over a chair and had water poured into
his nostrils, etc. Unable to stand the pain, he even-
tually admitted having a pistol, but on being released,
he withdrew this statement and told them truthfully that
he did not have any pistol, whereupon he was taken to
the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters and detained.
After three days of interrogation, during which he was
subjected to various forms of torture, he eventually
gave the story of how Yee Vung Ching had mentioned the
aforegoing to him, but added that he did not believe
Yee had any intention of carrying the plan out. As this
man was obviously in a bad state of nerves, he having
broken down and cried on two occasions during this
questioning, the undersigned informed him that he had
pages.zh:
5/8

指示，进入二楼的一间客厅，坐在长椅上等待陈的到来。约半小时后，三名中国人和一名日本人进入房间，开始讯问他是如何从上海抵达的，是独自前来还是有他人陪同。他回答说自己是1939年3月11日抵达南京，且是独自一人。随后他们又讯问他从上海带来的炸弹和手枪藏在哪里。他辩称对此一无所知，随即遭到猛烈殴打，之后被按在椅子上，往鼻孔里灌水等。因无法忍受疼痛，他最终承认拥有一把手枪，但在被释放后，他撤回了这一供词，如实告诉他们自己并没有手枪。随后他被带至日本宪兵队总部并遭拘留。
经过三天的审讯，期间遭受各种形式的酷刑，他最终讲述了叶荣庆曾向他提及上述事项的过程，但补充说他并不相信叶有意实施该计划。鉴于此人显然处于精神极度紧张的状态，在审讯过程中曾两次崩溃哭泣，笔录人告知他无需恐惧，只需如实说明叶荣庆是否确实要求他获取这些信息。他回答说，叶确实在上述日期提出过要求，但当时他认为叶只是在开玩笑，且在远东饭店与陈阿金会面后，他自己决定将此事彻底忘掉，返回南京后也无意再继续此事。

pages.en:
5/9

nothing to fear, but that to tell the truth in re
whether or not Yee Vung Ching had actually requested him
to get this information, and in replying he stated that
Yee had done so on the dates mentioned, but that at
the time he formed the opinion that Yee was merely
joking and after the interview with Zung Ah Kyung in the
Far Eastern Hotel he himself decided to forget the
whole thing and that on returning to Nanking he had
no intention of carrying the matter further.
Further questioned as to whether or not, at any
time during the discussions between himself and Yee
Vung Ching a third party had been present, he stated
that such was not the case, and that the only other
persons who knew of the suggested plan was Zung Ah Kyung
(陳阿金) and another named Siau Dee (小弟), a
chauffeur employed by Doo Yeu Sung (杜月笙) who had
been with Ah Kyung in room No.536 of the Far Eastern
Hotel, when he had mentioned the matter to the latter.
Questioned as to whom he suspected of having passed
the information to the Japanese Authorities, Tai Ah Dong
without hesitation mentioned Zung Ah Kyung whom he states
was previously employed by General Yang Hoo (楊虎), ex-
Shanghai Woosung Garrison Commander as a chauffeur and
who was the only other person, other than Yee Vung Ching
pages.zh:
5/9

当被进一步问及在他与叶荣庆的讨论过程中是否有第三方在场时，他表示并非如此，唯一知晓该提议计划的其他人是陈阿金和另一位名为小弟（Siau Dee）的人，小弟是杜月笙（Doo Yeu Sung）雇佣的司机，当他在远东饭店536号房间向陈阿金提及此事时，小弟正与陈在一起。
当被问及他怀疑是谁将信息泄露给日本当局时，戴阿东毫不犹豫地提到了陈阿金。他指出，陈此前曾任上海吴淞卫戍司令杨虎将军（General Yang Hoo）的司机，且除了叶荣庆和他自己之外，陈是唯一知晓获取上述信息这一提议计划的人。

pages.en:
5/10

and himself, who knew of the proposed plan to obtain
the information in question.
Taking into consideration the aforegoing facts,
the undersigned formed the opinion that there might
be some truth in what this man alleges against Yee
Vung Ching, but considering the source of the Japanese
information and to what extent this prisoner has un-
doubtedly been tortured, also his present situation,
this opinion was formed with reserve, and a request made
to question Yee Vung Ching on the statement as made by
this man, Tai Ah Dong.
This request was refused by Sgt. Major Katodo, who
explained that according to his instructions the under-
signed could be present at the questioning of this
prisoner but could not take part in the interrogation.
At 1 p.m. 29.3.39 the undersigned accompanied by
D.S. Sugimoto again visited the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters, Bridge House, and on this occasion were
permitted to sit in an adjoining room separated from
the office in which Yee Vung Ching was being interroga-
ted, by a wooden partition which was open, and through
which the prisoner and his interrogators could be seen
and heard quite clearly. This interrogation lasted
until 4.30 p.m. and during the course of same Yee Vung
pages.zh:
5/10

考虑到上述事实，笔录人认为戴对叶荣庆的指控可能有一定真实性，但鉴于日本方面情报的来源，以及这名囚犯无疑遭受了何种程度的酷刑，加之其目前的处境，这一意见是持保留态度形成的，并请求就戴阿东所作的陈述对叶荣庆进行讯问。
这一请求被加藤军曹（Sgt. Major Katodo）拒绝，他解释说，根据他的指令，笔录人可以出席对该囚犯的讯问，但不能参与审讯。
1939年3月29日下午1点，笔录人在杉本侦探（D.S. Sugimoto）的陪同下再次访问了位于百老汇大厦（Bridge House）的日本宪兵队总部。此次，他们获准坐在一间相邻的房间内，该房间与讯问叶荣庆的办公室之间隔着一道敞开的木板墙，透过隔板可以清晰地看到和听到囚犯及其审讯者。这次讯问持续到下午4点30分，在此期间，叶

pages.en:
5/11

Ching made a complete denial of the allegations made
against him by Tai Ah Dong and emphatically stuck to
his statement as made to the S.M.Police on the 19.3.39.
On one occasion only, during the whole of this interro-
gation, did the undersigned witness any violence being
used and this took place towards the end, when Sgt. Major
Katodo was seen to kick the prisoner on the shins and
then slap him across the face with his open hand, however
as it was not repeated no protest was made, and on the
interrogation ending the undersigned and D.S. Sugimoto
returned to Crime Branch Headquarters, where the afore-
going was reported to C.D.I. Grubb in charge C.1.

At 10 a.m. 30.3.39, the undersigned again attended
the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters in company of D.S.
Sugimoto, and on arrival there witnessed the re-question-
ing of Tai Ah Dong by Sgt. Major Katodo, who at this time
mentioned to the undersigned, through D.S. Sugimoto, that
the case appeared to be at a dead end, inasmuch that Tai
Ah Dong still persisted in his statement whilst Yee Vung
Ching continued to register a complete denial, and as
there was no other witness available, the only other
channel of investigation open, would be to try and as
far as possible, check Tai Ah Dong's statement in regard
to his movements etc., during the time that he alleged
pages.zh:
5/11

荣庆完全否认了戴阿东对他的指控，并坚决坚持其于1939年3月19日向工部局警务处（S.M.Police）所作的陈述。在整个讯问过程中，笔录人仅目睹过一次暴力行为，这发生在接近尾声时，只见加藤军曹踢了囚犯的小腿，并张开手掌扇了其耳光。然而，由于该行为未重复发生，故未提出抗议。讯问结束后，笔录人和杉本侦探返回刑事调查处总部，将上述情况报告给负责C1科的格鲁布首席侦探督察（C.D.I. Grubb）。
1939年3月30日上午10点，笔录人再次与杉本侦探一同前往日本宪兵队总部，抵达时目睹了加藤军曹对戴阿东的再次讯问。此时，加藤通过杉本侦探向笔录人提及，案件似乎陷入了僵局，因为戴阿东仍坚持其陈述，而叶荣庆继续完全否认，且没有其他证人可用，因此唯一开放的调查途径将是尽可能核实戴阿东关于其在所谓

pages.en:
5/12

that Yee Vung Ching requested him to try and gain th
information in question. The undersigned agreed to
assist in this matter and Sgt. Major Katodo then
explained that he would detail Sgt. Major Hikiyi for
this job, and that the latter would call at Police
Headquarters at 2 p.m. 30.3.39.

At 2.30 p.m. 30.3.39 Sgt. Major Hikiyi called a
Crime Branch Headquarters and requested assistance t
first visit 159 Taku Road, the home of Yee Vung Chin
and secondly to visit 42 Peiho Road, the home of one
Yang Kung Sung who according to Tai Ah Dong had acco
panied him and Yee to the cinema on the 21.3.39 (the
day of Chinese New Year) which Yee denied during his
interrogation.

At 2.45 p.m. 30.3.39, the undersigned accompanie
by L.S. Sugimoto and A/D.I. Chu Shou Ling (朱寿龄)
escorted Sgt. Major Hikiyi to 159 Taku Road, where th
undermentioned persons were questioned:-

(1) Yee Kau Sz (葉高氏), age 70, widow, moth
of Yee Vung Ching.
(2) Yee Loh Sz (葉罗氏), age 38, wife of Yee
Vung Ching.
(3) Yee Bei Nyi (葉培基), age 12, son of Yee
Ching.

These three persons were questioned regarding th
knowledge of Tai Ah Dong and all admitted that he wa
pages.zh:
5/12

称叶荣庆（Yee Vung Ching）请求他设法获取上述情报。签署人同意在此事上提供协助，随后警佐长 Katodo 解释说，他将指派警佐长 Hikiyi 负责此项工作，后者将于 1939 年 3 月 30 日下午 2 时前往警察总局报到。

1939 年 3 月 30 日下午 2 时 30 分，警佐长 Hikiyi 来到刑事科总部，请求协助首先前往大沽路 159 号，即叶荣庆（Yee Vung Ching）的住所，其次前往北河路 42 号，即杨根生（Yang Kung Sung）的住所。据戴阿东（Tai Ah Dong）称，杨曾于 1939 年 3 月 21 日（农历新年当日）陪同他和叶前往电影院，而叶在受审时对此予以否认。

1939 年 3 月 30 日下午 2 时 45 分，签署人在巡佐 Sugimoto 和代理探员朱寿龄（Chu Shou Ling）的陪同下，护送警佐长 Hikiyi 前往大沽路 159 号，并对下列人员进行了讯问：-

(1) 葉高氏（Yee Kau Sz），70 岁，寡妇，叶荣庆之母。
(2) 葉罗氏（Yee Loh Sz），38 岁，叶荣庆之妻。
(3) 葉培基（Yee Bei Nyi），12 岁，叶荣庆之子。

就这三个人对戴阿东的了解情况进行了讯问，三人均承认他是

pages.en:
5/13

friend of Yee Vung Ching who traded in second-hand motor
car tyres between Nanking and Shanghai, and who when
in Shanghai usually called on Yee. Questioned as to
when they last saw Tai Ah Dong all at first made conflic-
ting statements, the mother stating that she could not
remember, the wife saying that it was sometime between
the 6th. or 7th. moon last year (June - July or August,
1938), whilst the son mentioned that Tai Ah Dong had
called on his grandmother's birthday, 22nd. day of 11th.
moon (16.1.39), and had partaken of lunch with the
family. After some deliberation all three then recalled
that at about 12 noon on the 16.1.39, Tai Ah Dong had
called at 159 Taku Road and had remained there for
lunch, leaving again at about 1 p.m. Questioned as to
whether Yee Vung Ching had been present, they admitted
that he had arrived home at about 12.30 p.m. that day
and after lunch, during the course of which, he conversed
with Tai Ah Dong on every day topics, he left again at
about 1.30 p.m., half an hour after Tai had gone. They
were next questioned regarding, the every day life of
Yee Vung Ching, and in reply stated that he usually left
for work at about 7.30 a.m., returned at 12.30 p.m. for
lunch, leaving again at 1.30 p.m. and returning at 6 or
7 p.m., also that during the past three months owing to
the sickness of his aging mother he had very rarely gone
pages.zh:
5/13

叶荣庆的朋友，在南京和上海之间从事二手汽车轮胎贸易，且在上海期间通常会拜访叶家。当被问及最后一次见到戴阿东的时间时，三人起初陈述不一，母亲称记不清了，妻子称是去年农历六月或七月间（即 1938 年 6 月至 7 月或 8 月），而儿子则提到戴阿东曾在祖母生日那天，即农历十一月二十二日（1939 年 1 月 16 日）来访，并与家人共进午餐。经过一番回想，三人随后回忆起，1939 年 1 月 16 日中午 12 时许，戴阿东曾到访大沽路 159 号并留下吃午饭，约下午 1 时离开。当被问及叶荣庆当时是否在场时，他们承认叶于当天中午 12 时 30 分左右回家，午饭后，其间他与戴阿东聊了些日常话题，于下午 1 时 30 分左右再次离家，即在戴离开半小时后。接着就叶荣庆的日常生活对他们进行讯问，他们回答说，他通常早上 7 时 30 分左右出门上班，中午 12 时 30 分回来吃午饭，下午 1 时 30 分再次离开，晚上 6 点或 7 点返回；还提到，在过去三个月里，由于年迈的母亲生病，他很少在下班后外出

pages.en:
5/14

out in the evenings after work, and that if he did,
he invariably informed them where he was going, par-
ticularly if he intended visiting a cinema, as it was
his usual practice to obtain the money for such amuse-
ment from his mother. Written statements as taken
from these persons are herewith attached for information.
A visit was next paid to 42 Peiho Road, offices
of the Chung Yuen (中原) Transportation Company,
wherein one named Yang Kung Sung (楊根生) is employed
as a broker, however on enquiries being made for this
man, it was learned that he was absent on business. In
view of this a note requesting him to call at police
headquarters on the morning of the 31.3.39 was left and
the party returned to Crime Branch Headquarters.
At 9.30 a.m. 31.3.39, Sgt. Major Hikiyi brought to
Crime Branch Headquarters the prisoner Yee Vung Ching
and from his general appearance it was very obvious that
he had been subject to a great deal of man handling. On
being removed to the Chinese detective office and
immediately out of the presence of Sgt. Major Hikiyi,
this prisoner broke down and complained of the acute
pains in his legs, which when examined by the undersigned
were found to be a mass of bruises and abrasions, also
he had a slight bruise over the left eye. Questioned
as to how he had come about these wounds, he stated
pages.zh:
5/14

如果外出，他总会告知家人去向，特别是如果打算去看电影，因为他用于此类娱乐的钱通常是从母亲那里得来的。从这些人处取得的书面陈述附后供参考。
随后前往北河路 42 号，即中原（Chung Yuen）运输公司的办事处，一名叫杨根生（Yang Kung Sung）的人受雇为该行经纪人，但在查询此人时，得知他因公外出。鉴于此，留下一张便条，请他于 1939 年 3 月 31 日上午前往警察总局，随后一行人返回刑事科总部。
1939 年 3 月 31 日上午 9 时 30 分，警佐长 Hikiyi 将犯人叶荣庆带至刑事科总部，从其总体外表来看，很明显他遭受了大量的粗暴对待。当被带至华捕探员办公室并立即避开警佐长 Hikiyi 的视线后，这名犯人崩溃了，抱怨腿部剧烈疼痛，经签署人检查，发现腿部满是瘀伤和擦伤，左眼上方也有轻微瘀伤。当被问及这些伤痕是如何造成时，他声称

pages.en:
5/15

that most of such had been inflicted by Japanese members
of the Gendarmerie, who after the undersigned had returned
to Crime Branch Headquarters, had further questioned him
regarding the allegation made by Mr. A. Wong.

Owing to the serious nature of this man's injuries
C.D.I. Grubb was informed and he in turn informed D.I.
Nakamura, who along with C.D.I. Grubb, personally in-
terviewed this prisoner and heard his story of how he
had been tortured and further questioned during the
absence of the undersigned.

After this examination and interview and on instru-
ctions of D.C. Crime this man was taken to the Police
Hospital, where he was immediately recognised by certain
members of the staff as Mr. Gauge's chauffeur, who at
frequent intervals drove Mrs Warren, Matron of the
Hospital.

On being examined by Drs. Liu and Siau, this man
was ordered to be detained in Hospital, pending a more
thorough examination, after which a detailed medical
certificate would be forwarded to the undersigned.

Returning to Crime Branch Headquarters, the under-
signed in the presence of D.S. Sugimoto and Sgt. Major
Hikiyi questioned the witness Yung Kung Sung who made
the attached written statement in which he admits that
on the 3rd. or 4th. day of the Chinese New Year, 22/22
pages.zh:
5/15

大部分是由宪兵队的日本成员造成的，他们在签署人返回刑事科总部后，就 A. Wong 先生提出的指控对他进行了进一步讯问。

鉴于此人伤势严重，已通知华捕探员长 Grubb，他随即通知了日捕探员长 Nakamura，Nakamura 与华捕探员长 Grubb 一起亲自讯问了这名犯人，并听取了他关于在签署人不在场期间如何遭受酷刑和进一步讯问的陈述。

在这次检查和讯问之后，根据副刑事科长（D.C. Crime）的指示，此人被送往警察医院，医院某些工作人员立即认出他是 Gauge 先生的司机，该司机经常驾驶医院女护士长 Warren 夫人的专车。

经刘医生（Dr. Liu）和萧医生（Dr. Siau）检查后，命令将此人在医院扣留，以待更彻底的检查，之后将向签署人提交详细的医疗证明。

返回刑事科总部后，签署人在巡佐 Sugimoto 和警佐长 Hikiyi 在场的情况下，讯问了证人杨根生（Yung Kung Sung，原文如此，前文为 Yang Kung Sung），后者作出了附后的书面陈述，承认在 1939 年 2 月 22 日（农历新年初三或初四）

pages.en:
5/16

February, 1939, he accompanied by Yee Vung Ching visited
Tai Ah Dong in Room 44 of the Nanking Lodging House,
after which they made futile attempts to gain admission
to the Lido and Strand Theatres. Continuing this man
explains how they returned to the Nanking Lodging House
and later how he and Yee Vung Ching returned to the
latter's home, where he remained for dinner, after which
he returned to his own home at 42 Peiho Road.

In view of this man's statement, which to a certain
extent corroborates that of Tai Ah Dong's, he was ques-
tioned as to whether or not he had heard any discussion
relating to the obtaining of information re the movements
of officials of the Reformed Government and in reply he
stated he had not.

At 11.30 a.m. 31.3.39, on the instructions of D.C.
Crime, the undersigned interviewed Mr. Gange at his
office, Gordon & Co., 185 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, and as a
result obtained from him, (later by chit coolie) the
attached statement, in which he outlines the character
of Yee Vung Ching (奚文清) as is known to him.

At 10 a.m. 1.4.39 a telephone message was received
from the Police Hospital Authorities regarding an escort
for Yee Vung Ching who was being sent to the Country
Hospital for ex-Ray. This was complied with, Sinsa
Station rendering the necessary assistance.

John Coupland
D.S.I.
pages.zh:
5/16

他陪同叶荣庆在南京旅社 44 号房间拜访了戴阿东，随后他们试图进入丽都大戏院（Lido Theatre）和斯特兰德大戏院（Strand Theatre）但未果。接着，此人解释了他们如何返回南京旅社，以及后来他和叶荣庆如何回到叶家，他在那里吃了晚饭，之后返回自己位于北河路 42 号的家中。

鉴于此人的陈述在一定程度上佐证了戴阿东的说法，对他进行了讯问，问他是否听到过任何关于获取维新政府官员行踪情报的讨论，他回答说没有。

1939 年 3 月 31 日上午 11 时 30 分，根据副刑事科长（D.C. Crime）的指示，签署人在其办公室——圆明园路 185 号 Gordon & Co. 公司——会见了 Gange 先生，并由此从他那里获得了（后来通过信差送来）附后的陈述，其中概述了他所了解的叶荣清（奚文清）的品行。

1939 年 4 月 1 日上午 10 时，收到警察医院当局关于为叶荣庆提供押送人员的电话留言，叶将被送往乡村医院（Country Hospital）进行 X 光检查。此事已照办，新闸捕房（Sinsa Station）提供了必要的协助。

John Coupland
首席巡佐督察（D.S.I.）

pages.en:
C.l. Misc. 35/39
Headquarters
Crime Branch
April 1,
39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE (TEMPORARY
HANDING OVER OF YEE VUNG CHING (        ).

In accordance with instructions from D. C.
(Crime) on March 28, 1939, I informed Lieut. Toita of
the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters of the necessity
of conforming to the following arrangements concerning
the loan of Yee Vung Ching :-

" Yee Vung Ching will be loaned for a period
of 2 days only to Gendarmerie Headquarters, on the
understanding that a Foreign and Japanese detective
shall be present during the interrogation that takes
place. He is in the employ of a reputable foreigner
of standing, and has been employed in this capacity
for many years, and that the interrogation and
treatment of this chauffeur must be carried out on
strictly legal lines and in conformity to the process
of the law. Arrangements should be made so that the
interrogation takes place immediately Yee Vung Ching
is handed over and a receipt in this connection should
be given by the Japanese Authorities."

Further, I intimated to the officer that Mr.
Gange, the employer of Yee Vung Ching, was desirous of
engaging a lawyer for him.

D. C. (Crime)
D. I.
pages.zh:
C.l. Misc. 35/39
总部
刑事科
1939 年
4 月 1 日

协助日本宪兵队（临时移交叶荣庆（        ））。

根据 1939 年 3 月 28 日副刑事科长（D. C. (Crime)）的指示，我通知日本宪兵队总部的 Toita 中尉，必须遵守以下关于借用叶荣庆的安排：-

“叶荣庆仅借给宪兵队总部使用 2 天，前提是讯问期间须有一名外籍探员和一名日籍探员在场。他受雇于一位有声望的外国人，并已以此身份工作多年，对该司机的讯问和处理必须严格依法进行，符合法律程序。应作出安排，以便在叶荣庆移交后立即进行讯问，并由日本当局就此出具收据。”

此外，我向该军官表示，叶荣庆的雇主 Gange 先生希望为他聘请律师。

副刑事科长（犯罪）
探员长

pages.en:
Y __ __ ( __ ), 70, Female,
__ tung, / __ . __ . 172,
C.1 31.3.39 Yo

I am the mother of Yee Vung Ching. I am now 70 years
old. My health is very poor and most of my time is spent in
bed.
On 22.11.38, the occasion of my 70th. birthday, my son,
Yee Vung Ching, bought some foodstuff and gave small party
in my honour, inviting several friends to dinner. I do not
know the names of the friends who attended the party.
My son has always been very good to me. He is now
employed as chauffeur by foreigner. He usually hands to
me the money he earns every month to run various domestic
expenses.
During the Chinese New Year, I was very ill. Yee had
several days holiday, and instead of going to various places
to enjoy himself, he stayed by my side all the time, waiting
upon me. He went back to duty on 23.2.39.
This is the truth.

YEE SAU B.
pages.zh:
Y __ __ ( __ )，70 岁，女性，
__ 东，/ __ . __ . 172，
C.1 1939 年 3 月 31 日 Yo

我是叶荣庆的母亲。我现在 70 岁。我的健康状况很差，大部分时间都卧床不起。
1938 年 11 月 22 日，正值我 70 岁生日，我的儿子叶荣庆买了一些食品，为我举办了一个小型聚会，邀请了几位朋友共进晚餐。我不知道参加聚会的朋友的姓名。
我的儿子一直对我很好。他现在受雇于一名外国人担任司机。他通常每月将赚来的钱交给我，用于支付各种家庭开支。
春节期间，我病得很重。叶有几天假期，他没有去各处游玩，而是一直守在我身边侍奉我。他于 1939 年 2 月 23 日回去上班。
属实。

叶曹氏（YEE SAU B.）

pages.en:
Yee Loo Sz (奚 羅 氏)
Tientsin                                      C.J.S. 290
C.B.H.Q.  C.1        1/4/39          un: slated
                                         ////////       Clerk Hsia

My name is Yee Loo Sz, age 32, native of Tientsin,
married, residing at No.159 Taku Road.
    I married one named Yee Vung Ching in Tientsin about
12 years ago, and I came to Shanghai in the autumn of the
year 1927.
    On the 18th. January, 1939 (22nd. day, 11th. Moon, Lunar
Year) was my mother-in-law's (Yee Sau Sz 奚 曹 氏) birth-day.
At about 11 a.m. on the same day, Tai Ah Dong (戴阿東),
a friend of my husband, Yee Vung Ching (奚榮慶) came to my
home for amusement whilst I was engaged in cooking macaroni,
I requested him to remain to have some macaroni. At about
12.30 p.m. my husband, Yee Vung Ching returned for meal. When
they met they held a conversation relating to daily life.
After partaking of macaroni, Tai Ah Dong left at 1 p.m. but
my husband Yee Vung Ching went to his Foreign master's house
for the purpose of driving the motor car at about 1.30 p.m.
    On the 19th. and 20th. February, 1939 (1st.& 2nd.day of
the 1st. Moon, Chinese New Year) was a wet day so my husband
remained at home. The following day, 21.2.39 (3rd. day of the
Chinese New Year) he played Mah Jong together with one of the
tenants, Tsang Fah (張發) and Tsong Woo (宗武) at home.
On the 22.3.39 they continued playing Mah Jong and did not
leave the premises. During the period of October, 1938 and
22nd. March, 1939, my mother-in-law was very sick, so my
husband stayed at home all the time during the Chinese New
Year holidays. He resumed work on the 23.3.39. Usually, he
went out to work in the early morning and returned in the
pages.zh:
叶罗氏（Yee Loo Sz / 奚 羅 氏）
天津                                      C.J.S. 290
刑事科总部  C.1        1939 年 4 月 1 日          未注明
                                         ////////       书记员 Hsia

我叫叶罗氏，32 岁，天津人，已婚，住大沽路 159 号。
    大约 12 年前，我在天津嫁给一个叫叶荣庆的人，我于 1927 年秋天来到上海。
    1939 年 1 月 18 日（农历十一月二十二日）是我婆婆（叶曹氏 奚 曹 氏）的生日。当天上午 11 点左右，我丈夫叶荣庆（奚榮慶）的朋友戴阿东（Tai Ah Dong）来我家消遣，当时我正在煮通心粉，我请他留下来吃点通心粉。中午 12 时 30 分左右，我丈夫叶荣庆回来吃饭。他们见面后就日常生活进行了交谈。吃完通心粉后，戴阿东于下午 1 时离开，但我丈夫叶荣庆于下午 1 时 30 分左右前往其外国主人家去开汽车。
    1939 年 2 月 19 日和 20 日（农历正月初一和初二，春节）是雨天，所以我丈夫待在家里。第二天，1939 年 2 月 21 日（农历正月初三，春节第三天），他在家与一名房客张发（Tsang Fah）和宗武（Tsong Woo）一起打麻将。
    3 月 22 日他们继续打麻将，没有离开住所。在 1938 年 10 月至 1939 年 3 月 22 日期间，我婆婆病得很重，所以我丈夫在春节假期期间一直待在家里。他于 1939 年 3 月 23 日恢复工作。通常，他清晨出去工作，傍晚回来，

pages.en:
(2)

evening, sometimes he obtained 10 or 20 cents from his mother
to see moving pictures. He always explained to me or my
mother-in-law before he went to the theatre.
This is a true statement.

Signed:- Yee Loo Sz
pages.zh:
(2)

有时他会从母亲那里拿 10 或 20 分钱去看电影。他在去剧院之前总是向我或我婆婆说明。
此陈述属实。

签名:- 叶罗氏

pages.en:
YEE BEI KYI ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), 12, Student,
Pootung, C.D.S. 172,
C.1 31.3.1939 Yao.

My name is Yee Bei Kyi, aged 12, native of Pootung.
Owing to financial difficulties, I left school this
Spring and stayed at home, 159 Taku Road, doing nothing.
I was born in Tientsin and came to Shanghai together with
my parents at the age of 4. At first we stayed in an address
on Gt. Western Road, wherefrom we subsequently moved to the
above address, where we have been living since.
There are four persons in our house, i.e. my grandma,
father, mother and myself. All of us lived on the expense
of my father, who was a chauffeur in a foreign household.
During the Chinese New Year, my father was given four
days holiday (19/20/21/22.2.39), but as everyday rained heavily
my father stayed at home all the time, except visiting the
neighbour's house twice for mahjong games. He went back to
duty on the 5th. New Year Day (23.2.39).
Last year, on 22.11.38, the occasion of grandma's birth-
day, my father gave a small party at home. Several friends,
Tai h Dong et al attended. This is the truth.

Signed : YEE BEI KYI
pages.zh:
叶培基（YEE BEI KYI / 〔此处转录不清〕），12 岁，学生，
浦东，C.D.S. 172，
C.1 1939 年 3 月 31 日 Yao.

我叫叶培基，12 岁，浦东人。
由于经济困难，我今年春天辍学，待在大沽路 159 号的家里，无所事事。
我出生在天津，4 岁时随父母来到上海。起初我们住在西摩路（Gt. Western Road）的一个地址，随后搬到了上述地址，并一直居住至今。
我家有四口人，即我的祖母、父亲、母亲和我。全家靠我父亲的收入生活，他在一个外国家庭当司机。
春节期间，父亲放了四天假（1939 年 2 月 19/20/21/22 日），但由于每天雨下得很大，父亲一直待在家里，除了两次去邻居家打麻将。他在春节第五天（1939 年 2 月 23 日）回去上班。
去年，1938 年 11 月 22 日，正值祖母生日，父亲在家举办了一个小型聚会。几位朋友，戴阿东等人参加了。属实。

签名 : 叶培基

YANG KUNG SUNG (杨公颂), 30, S/Clerk,
Soochow, -- Self,
C.1 31. 3.1939. Yao

I am employed as a clerk i/c of cargo of affairs at
the Chung Yuen Transportation Co., 42 Peiho Road.

Five years ago, when my nephew Ching Kwei Sung and I were
visiting the Great World Amusement Park, I was introduced by the
Former to Yee Vung Ching, and since then Yee became a regular
visitor at my house. During June or July, 1938, Yee introduced
me to his friend, Tai Ah Dong, with whom I became very friendly
afterwards.

On or about the 3rd. or 4th. day of the Chinese New
Year (21/22.2.39), I visited Yee's house to offer the season's
greetings. I was received by Yee Zau Sz (Yee's mother), Yee
Loo Sz (Yee's wife), Yee Bei Kyi (Yee's junior) and Yee Vung
Ching himself. After tiffin, Yee Vung Ching suggested that I
accompany him to the Nanking Lodging House, near the Nanking
Theatre, to see Tai Ah Dong. I agreed, and the two of us went
the Ah Li's room, where we stayed for about 2 hours, chatting
on various subjects. Soon, we left the house for the Strand
Theatre, but on arrival, we found the house already full. We
were eager to see a picture, so we went to the Rialto Theatre.
But it was also full. We had nothing to do, but to stroll home
(the Nanking Lodging House)
ward, Yee buying several oranges on the way. On arrival at
Tai's room, it was already about time for dinner. Yee then
suggested all of us going to his house for the meal. Tai had
a previous engagement and declined his invitation, so Yee and
I left him and came to Yee's home, where I had dinner. I left
Yee's house at about 9 p.m. and went back to the Chung Yuen Co.

This is the truth.

YANG KUNG SUNG.
pages.zh:
杨公颂（YANG KUNG SUNG），30岁，高级职员，
苏州人，——本人陈述，
C.1 1939年3月31日。姚

我受雇于北河路42号中原运输公司（Chung Yuen Transportation Co.），担任负责货物事务的职员。

五年前，当我的侄子郑桂松（Ching Kwei Sung）和我游览大世界游乐场时，经他介绍，我认识了叶荣清（Yee Vung Ching），此后叶便成了我家的常客。1938年6月或7月间，叶将我介绍给他的朋友戴阿堂（Tai Ah Dong），此后我与戴交情甚笃。

在农历新年初三或初四左右（1939年2月21/22日），我前往叶家拜年。接待我的是叶邹氏（叶母）、叶鲁氏（叶妻）、叶贝姬（叶之晚辈）以及叶荣清本人。午饭后，叶荣清建议我陪他去南京大戏院附近的南京旅社（Nanking Lodging House）去见戴阿堂。我同意了，于是我们两人去了阿李（Ah Li）的房间，在那里逗留了约两个小时，闲聊各种话题。不久，我们离开那里前往斯特兰德大戏院（Strand Theatre），但到达后发现客满。我们急于看电影，于是又去了里亚尔托大戏院（Rialto Theatre）。但那里也客满。我们无事可做，只好漫步回（南京旅社）方向，途中叶买了几只橘子。到达戴的房间时，已近晚餐时间。叶随后建议我们大家去他家吃饭。戴因已有约会而谢绝了邀请，于是叶和我告别了他，来到叶家，我在那里用了晚餐。晚上9点左右，我离开叶家，返回中原公司。

以上属实。

杨公颂。

D. C. (Special Branch).

S. B. REGISTRY
No. 8. D. 8799/37
Date March 27, 39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE AUTHORITIES -
ARREST OF YEE VUNG CHING (葉榮清).

D.I. NAKAMURA                                C.D.I. GRUBB.

27.3.39.
At 3 p.m. D.I. Nakamura telephoned to Lieut.
Toita, asking him to bring Tai Ah Dong, who was brought
to Shanghai from Nanking, to C.I for confrontation
with Yee Vung Ching. Lieut. Toita is of the opinion
that it is necessary to make discreet enquiries
regarding Yee Vung Ching as he is considered an
important suspect in the case of the conspiracy to
murder a high official of the Reformed Government and
not just an ordinary guerilla suspect. Accordingly,
he does not therefore, agree for the two men to be
confronted with each other at the present stage, because
he fears that it may completely obstruct further
investigations.

As Tai Ah Dong clearly stated that Yee Vung
Ching was connected with the case, Lieut. Toita wishes
to ask for the immediate handing over of Yee, however,
in case of being refused, he may be handed over on
loan. He further stated that at the time of the
interrogation of Yee at his office, the presence of
foreign and Japanese detectives would be welcome.

Continuing, he said that in such an important
case as this, speedy enquiries would be necessary,
therefore, he hoped that his request be immediately
complied with.

（批：JBR
P.A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)
28/3.）

（签名：C G / 3.）
Recd 28/3

（签名：Nakamura）
D. I.

特别处登记簿
编号：D. 8799/37
日期：1939年3月27日。

协助日本当局——
逮捕叶荣清（葉榮清）。

警司 中村                                首席侦探督察 格鲁布。

1939年3月27日。
下午3时，警司中村致电丰田中尉（Lieut. Toita），请他将戴阿堂从南京带至上海，到刑事侦缉处与叶荣清对质。丰田中尉认为，有必要对叶荣清进行谨慎的调查，因为他被视为一起阴谋谋杀维新政府高官案件的重要嫌疑人，而不仅仅是一名普通的游击队嫌疑犯。因此，他不同意在目前阶段让两人互相面对，因为他担心这可能会完全阻碍进一步的调查。

由于戴阿堂明确指称叶荣清与此案有关，丰田中尉希望要求立即移交叶，但是，如果遭到拒绝，也可以暂借移交。他还表示，在其办公室审讯叶时，欢迎外国和日本侦探在场。

他接着说，在此类重要案件中，迅速调查是必要的，因此，他希望他的请求能立即得到遵行。

（批注：JBR
致副总监（特别处）私人助理
3月28日）

（签名：C G / 3.）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. I. REGISTRY
C. I.
No 35/39.
Date 26th March 39.
CHINA S. B. D.
Date 26th March 39.

Assistance to Japanese Military Police Headquarters.

D.S.I. Crighton
C.D.I. Grubb.

In reference to arrest of one named YEE VUNG
CHING ( 葉文清 ) M/Chauffeur, residing 159 Taku road, on the
morning of the 19.3.39. , the attached request for his handing
over was received from the Headquarters of the Japanese Gend-
armerie on the 25.3.39., along with a copy of the Statement
taken from the prisoner TAI AH DONG ( 戴阿堂 ), who, according
to this request has been brought to Shanghai from Nanking, and
is at present detained in the Headquarters of the Japanese
Gendarmerie.

Attached herewith is a translation of the above,
statement, which when read over to YEE VUNG CHING ( 葉文清 )
brought an emphatic denial that he had ever uttered such suggest-
ions to TAI AH DONG ( 戴阿堂 ).

In view of above, and as the evidence, to hand
does not appear to carry much weight, it being a case of one mans
word against another, the undersigned would respectfully suggest,
that provided TAI AH DONG ( 戴阿堂 ) is still in Shanghai,
the Japanese Gendarmerie, be requested to bring him to this office
where he could be confronted with Yee Vung Ching ( 葉文清 )
and further questioned regarding his allegations.

John Coughlin
D. S. I.

（批：16）
（批：Cost 1/3）
（批：S.I. / D.B.P. / 27/3.）

副侦探督察 克莱顿
首席侦探督察 格鲁布。

关于1939年3月19日上午逮捕一名名为叶文清（YEE VUNG CHING，葉文清）的男子（职业：司机，住址：大沽路159号）一事，日本宪兵司令部于1939年3月25日收到了附带的移交请求，并附有一份从囚犯戴阿堂（TAI AH DONG，戴阿堂）处取得的供词副本，根据该请求，戴已被从南京带至上海，目前被拘押在日本宪兵司令部。

随函附上上述供词的译文，当向叶文清（葉文清）宣读时，他坚决否认曾向戴阿堂（戴阿堂）提出过此类建议。

鉴于上述情况，且现有证据似乎分量不足，因为这属于一人之言对抗另一人之言的情况，签署人谨建议，只要戴阿堂（戴阿堂）仍在上海，应请求日本宪兵队将其带至本办事处，以便与叶文清（葉文清）对质，并就其指控进一步讯问。

约翰·科格林
副侦探督察
