TAI AH DONG (戴阿堂) alias TAI CHING SIANG
(戴慶祥), age 26 years,
Chih-men, Yue-yao, Chekiang XX Sqt. Major H. Shintaka
Jap. Gend. H.Q. Provost
at Nanking 21-3-39 Zung Yih Dah (陳一達)
& translated by J.D.C. Shimidzu, S.M.P.

Address : c/o Yuen Tsin-jih (chauffeur), No. 45, Er Dian Hsian,
Koo Lao, Nanking. (南京鼓樓二條巷四十五號俞譜吉轉 ).

Occupation : Dealer in second-hand motor car tyres.

Domicile : Chih-men, Yue-yao Hsien, Chekiang (浙江餘姚千門 ).
----------------------------------------

On March 21, 1939 the aforementioned Chinese made the
following voluntary statement at the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters :-

My domicile, native place, present address, profession,
name and age are same as those stated above.

When I was 7 years old I entered the Dih Moon Primary
School (迪蒙小學校) at Old West Gate (老西門 ), Shanghai and
graduated the same at the age of 14 years.

When I was 15 years of age, I joined as an apprentice
in the Doong Tse Clock Factory (同志製鐘廠) at Ming Dao Road
(道明路 ), Shanghai, where I worked for 2 years but had to
leave owing to the factory being closed due to business
depression.

Then I joined the Central Motor Car Studying Society
at Rue de Albert, in Shanghai and after receiving the provisional
licence for driving motor-cars at the age of 20, I worked as a
chauffeur in the employ of a Chinese lawyer named Tse Dien Ching
(朱殿卿); at No. 4 San Shing Foong (三星坊 ), Doo Zung Woo Road
(杜神父路), French Concession.

Whilst working three years in the above place, I saved
nearly $300.00 so I started the business of my own after buying
a second-hand motor-car.

In the 7th Moon (Lunar Calendar), 1937, I sold the
pages.zh:
戴阿堂（TAI AH DONG），别名戴庆祥（TAI CHING SIANG），26岁，
浙江余姚芝门 XX 小队队长 H. Shintaka
日本宪兵司令部 纠察长
于南京 1939年3月21日 陈一达（Zung Yih Dah）
由上海公共租界警务处 J.D.C. Shimidzu 翻译

地址：南京鼓楼二条巷四十五号，由俞谱吉（司机）转交。

职业：二手汽车轮胎经销商。

籍贯：浙江余姚县芝门（浙江餘姚千門）。
---

1939年3月21日，上述华人在日本宪兵司令部作出如下自愿陈述：

我的籍贯、出生地、现住址、职业、姓名和年龄均如上所述。

我7岁时进入上海老西门的迪蒙小学校，14岁时毕业。

15岁时，我在上海道明路的同志制钟厂当学徒，在那里工作了两年，但因生意萧条导致工厂关闭而不得不离开。

随后，我加入上海亚尔培路（Rue de Albert）的中央汽车学习社，20岁获得汽车驾驶临时执照后，我在法租界杜神父路三星坊3号受雇于一位名叫朱殿卿（Tse Dien Ching）的中国律师，担任司机。

在上述地方工作三年期间，我积蓄了近300美元，于是买了一辆二手车，开始自己做生意。

1937年农历七月，我卖掉了

pages.en:
- 2 -
motor-car and tried to find some employment but failed to do so
owing to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.
Therefore, I returned to my native place and spent
about 3 months. After returning to Shanghai I entered the Ling
Zau Chinese Opera Club, No. 8 Tong Woo Li, Sie Zaung Road
(Thibet Road) but passed the day without doing anything until
June last.
In the middle of June last year, I visited my friend
named Yuen Tsin-jih (俞譜吉 ), residing at No. 6 Pootoo Road,
Nanking, to find some job through his recommendation but
without any success and spent one month at his house. Later
I managed to run a business dealing in old tyres of motor
vehicles which is continued until now.
My business is to purchase old motor-car tyres in
the city of Nanking and to dispose of them in Shanghai.
For this purpose, once or twice a month I used to
visit Shanghai where I stay about a week or so in order to
sell the old tyres.
The tyres had been sold through the hand of one
named Tsang Foh Ziang (          ) of Yah Shing Motor Car
Repairing Co. (          ), at No. 14, Yoh Chun (          ),
Pei-hai Road (          ), International Settlement.
The proceeds from the sale of these tyres after
deducting the lodging charges, the railway fares, etc.,
amounted to approximately $40.00 per mensem so that I did not
find any difficulties in my living but I often had a hard
time of it because of my fondness for gambling.
pages.zh:
- 2 -
汽车，试图找些工作，但由于中日战事爆发而未能如愿。
因此，我回到家乡，度过了大约三个月。回到上海后，我进入了西藏路同武里8号的灵奏国剧社，但直到去年六月一直无所事事。
去年六月中旬，我拜访了住在南京普陀路6号的朋友俞谱吉（Yuen Tsin-jih），希望通过他的推荐找份工作，但未成功，在他家住了一个月。后来，我设法经营起买卖旧汽车轮胎的生意，一直持续到现在。
我的业务是在南京市购买旧汽车轮胎，并在上海出售。
为此，我每月去上海一两次，停留约一周左右，以便出售旧轮胎。
轮胎是通过国际公共租界北海路14号耀春（音译）亚兴汽车修理公司（音译）的曾佛祥（Tsang Foh Ziang，原文空白）之手售出的。
出售这些轮胎的收入，扣除住宿费和铁路运费等，每月约为40美元，因此我的生活并不困难，但由于我好赌，常常日子过得紧巴巴的。

pages.en:
- 3 -

The place where I had stayed during my visits to
Shanghai were the Nanking Hotel, Avenue Edward VII, French
Concession, and An Soung Hotel (        ) at Rue Palikao,
French Concession.

My parents and elder sister are working in the
native place as farmers and the eldest sister was married to
one named Kying Kao Liang (金國樑), a chauffeur, residing at
57 Avenue Joffre, French Concession.

Now I wish to state how I was requested by one named
Yi Vung Ching (奚文欽), a chauffeur employed by the Koo Fah
Li Co., a British concern, 185 Yuen Ming Yuen Road (Gordon
& Co.), who is residing on the 3rd floor of Shing Zung Ziang
Shop (興生祥號), 159 Taku Road, to watch the movements of
officials of the Reformed Government and the Nanking City
Government.

Whilst I was staying at the Nanking Hotel, Avenue
Edward VII, French Concession, I, on the morning of 16th or
17th November last, visited Yi Vung Ching, 3rd floor of the
Shing Sung Ziang Shop, 159 Taku Road, and after tiffin as I
was just going to leave, Yi Vung Ching asked me to go to the
Great World in the French Concession. So I promised him to go
and I went there at about 8 p.m. After waiting for him a short
time, Yi Vung Ching came and we together was a theatrical
performance until about 11 p.m. when we left.

After a walking along Avenue Edward VII about 100
metres from the Great World and when I was parting from him
Yi Vung Ching told me that as I was living in Nanking, it would
pages.zh:
- 3 -

我在上海访问期间居住的地方是法租界爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的南京饭店，以及法租界白克路（Rue Palikao）的安松旅馆（An Soung Hotel，原文空白）。

我的父母和姐姐在家乡务农，大姐嫁给了金国樑（Kying Kao Liang），他是一名司机，住在法租界霞飞路57号。

现在我想陈述我是如何受到一名叫奚文钦（Yi Vung Ching）的人的请求的，他是英国公司固发利公司（Koo Fah Li Co.，戈登公司 Gordon & Co.）的司机，住在圆明园路185号，现居大沽路159号兴生祥号三楼，他要求我监视维新政府和南京市政府官员的动向。

当我住在法租界爱多亚路的南京饭店时，去年11月16日或17日上午，我拜访了住在大沽路159号兴生祥号三楼的奚文钦，午饭后我正准备离开，奚文钦让我去法租界的大世界。于是我答应了他，并在晚上8点左右去了那里。等了他一小会儿，奚文钦来了，我们一起看了一场戏剧表演，直到晚上11点左右才离开。

沿着爱多亚路从大世界走了大约100米，当我与他分手时，奚文钦告诉我，因为我住在南京，所以

pages.en:
- 4 -
be very easy for me to trace the movements of the high
officials of the Reformed and City Governments and accordingly
to watch them carefully. He wanted me to shadow them whenever
they planned to visit Shanghai on some business and to report
to him where they were staying in Shanghai.
Yi Vung Ching further stated that he would arrange
for the assassination of those persons and that it would be a
very good chance for me to rise in the world. He persuaded me
to comply with his request for it was not a difficult job at all
When the hostilities broke out I was staying in
Shanghai and saw many Chinese being killed and houses burned
by Japanese soldiers so I harboured a grudge against them.
I thought as a means of revenge the work would be splendid
but I hesitated to give a definite answer at that time to
Yi Vung Ching. I simply said to him, "Is that so?" and then
we parted. As I have already stated I was inclined to carry
it out.
On December 28, 1938, whilst I was staying at the
Nanking Hotel on business Yi Vung Ching came to the hotel at
about 8 p.m. on the same date and informed me that in addition
to what had already been mentioned if I could tell him the
places where leading officials of the Reformed Government and
the Nanking City Government were staying in Shanghai, a reward
of $8,000.00 to $10,000.00 would be given me and I would be
recommended to Chiang Kai Sheh (蒋介石). He further said
that in that case I would be well treated and could also join
the Lan San Dan (蓝衫党) (Blue Shirts) which was organized
pages.zh:
- 4 -
对我来说，追踪维新政府和市政府高官的动非常容易，因此要我仔细监视他们。他希望我在他们计划因公务访问上海时跟踪他们，并向他报告他们在上海的住处。
奚文钦进一步表示，他会安排暗杀这些人，这对我来说是一个很好的升迁机会。他劝我答应他的请求，因为这项工作一点也不难。
战事爆发时，我正住在上海，目睹许多中国人被日本士兵杀害，房屋被烧毁，因此我对他们怀恨在心。我想，作为一种报复手段，这项工作会很棒，但我当时犹豫不决，没有给奚文钦明确的答复。我只是对他说，“是这样吗？”然后我们就分开了。如前所述，我倾向于执行此事。
1938年12月28日，当我因公住在南京饭店时，奚文钦于当晚8点左右来到酒店，告诉我，除了前面提到的内容外，如果我能告诉他维新政府和南京市政府主要官员在上海的住处，将给我8,000至10,000美元的报酬，并将把我推荐给蒋介石（Chiang Kai Sheh）。他还说，在这种情况下，我会受到优待，还可以加入蓝衣社（Lan San Dan，蓝衫党），该组织是由

pages.en:
- 5 -

with the object of assassinating the notables of the Reformed
and Nanking City Governments. He told me as I could receive an
allowance of $40.00 per month and to bring my photograph.

Upon hearing of this request I promised Yi Vung Ching
to try as I thought it would be a delightful matter to accept.

I told him that a friend of mine named Zung Ah Kying
(      ) was employed by the Minister of Home Affairs of
the Reformed Government as a chauffeur so if we could win Zung
over, we might be able to assassinate the Minister. Then Yi
Vung Ching strongly encouraged me to carry it out. I hoped to
get into touch with Zung to win him over but owing to business
circumstances I could not return to Nanking until the 21st of
January, so I did not meet Zung.

At about 7.30 p.m. on 5-1-39 (the Lunar Calendar)
whilst I was staying in the Nanking Hotel, Yi Vung Ching came
to the hotel and asked me to take supper with him but I refused
it. Then he told me not to forget the matter which he had
asked me the other day and left.

On 8-1-39 (the Lunar Calendar) when I visited the Far
Eastern Hotel to see my acquaintance named Soung ( 宋 ), I met
Zung Ah Kying unexpectedly in the lift of that hotel.

At that time (about 8 p.m.) Zung was accompanied by his
brother, who was formerly known to me.

Zung said to me, "When have you come here?" I replied,
"I came here on 27-12-38 (Lunar Calendar) on business, and now
going to Room No. 536 in this hotel." Zung told me that he
would come later. Zung got out of the lift on the 4th floor
pages.zh:
- 5 -

其目的是刺杀维新政府和南京市政府的要员。他告诉我，我每月可领取40.00美元的津贴，并让我带上照片。

听到这一请求后，我向叶文清（Yi Vung Ching）承诺会尽力尝试，因为我认为接受此事将是一件令人愉快的事。

我告诉他，我有一位名叫钟阿金（Zung Ah Kying）(音译)的朋友受雇于维新政府内政部长，担任司机，因此如果我们能争取钟加入，我们或许能够刺杀该部长。随后，叶文清极力鼓励我实施此计划。我希望能与钟取得联系以争取他，但由于事务原因，我直到1月21日才能返回南京，因此我未能见到钟。

1939年1月5日（农历）晚上约7点30分，当我住在南京饭店时，叶文清来到饭店，邀请我与他共进晚餐，但我拒绝了。随后，他提醒我不要忘记前几天他委托我的那件事，然后离开了。

1939年1月8日（农历），当我去远东饭店拜访一位姓宋（Soung）的熟人时，我在该饭店的电梯里意外遇到了钟阿金。

当时（约晚上8点），钟由他的弟弟陪同，这位弟弟我以前也认识。

钟对我说：“你什么时候来的？”我回答说：“我于1938年12月27日（农历）因公务来到这里，现在要去这家饭店的536号房间。”钟告诉我他稍后会来。钟在四楼走出电梯

pages.en:
- 6 -

and I on the 5th.

Two hours later, whilst I was gambling with Soung
in his room Zung and his brother came in.

I was delighted to see them for I had promised the
matter to Yi Vung Ching. After talking for 30 minutes amongst
four of us, I said to Zung Ah Kying as follows :- "I have been
informed from Yi Vung Ching to watch the movements of the high
officials of the Reformed Government and to report the places
where they are going to stay in Shanghai, for which a reward of
$10,000.00 will be issued. The assassination will be carried
out by them. (Yi Vung Ching's name was not mentioned but simply
said "them"). If we were successful they will recommend us to
Chiang Kai Sheh so there is a chance for us to rise in the
world." Zung Ah Kying said, "It is a very difficult job to be
accomplished so it is better to have fun by calling girls."

I was disappointed on finding out that Zung Ah Kying
was not interested in the case, so I tried to call the girls
from An Loh Da Bath House (安樂池浴場) by telephone but they
had already been engaged by others. Then Zung Ah Kying
together with his brother left the hotel.

During our conversations as Soung was staying a short
distance away from us and further as he was dull-headed I do
not think that he understood what we were talking about. Zung
Ah Kying's brother was also listening the conversation, but I
do not think that neither Zung nor his brother became aware of
the fact that I was doing such kind of work. After that, I
did not tell anything openly to Zung, fearing that he might
pages.zh:
- 6 -

而我则在五楼。

两小时后，当我正在宋的房间里与他赌博时，钟和他的弟弟走了进来。

见到他们我很高兴，因为我已向叶文清承诺了那件事。在我们四人交谈了30分钟后，我对钟阿金说如下内容：“我从叶文清那里得知，要监视维新政府高官的行踪，并报告他们在上海将下榻的地点，为此将发放10,000.00美元的赏金。刺杀行动将由他们执行。（未提及叶文清的名字，仅说‘他们’）。如果我们成功，他们将把我们推荐给蒋介石，这样我们就有机会飞黄腾达。”钟阿金说：“这是一项很难完成的工作，不如叫妓女来取乐更好。”

我发现钟阿金对此案不感兴趣，感到失望，于是我试图通过电话从安乐池浴场（An Loh Da Bath House）叫妓女，但她们已被他人预订。随后，钟阿金与其弟离开了饭店。

在我们的谈话过程中，由于宋住得离我们有一段距离，而且他头脑迟钝，我认为他并不理解我们在谈论什么。钟阿金的弟弟也在旁听谈话，但我认为钟及其弟弟均未意识到我正在从事此类工作。此后，我没有再向钟公开透露任何信息，唯恐他可能

pages.en:
- 7 -

become suspicious. However, I thought it would be wise to
disclose to him of our plan gradually of our next meetings.
I returned to Nanking on March 11 and was told by the
inmate named Van Kung ( ) that on or about March 8th, a
chauffeur No. 23 (name unknown) of the Minister of Home
Affairs, visited his house as Zung's messenger. The Minister's
wife bought a motor-car and as she was looking for a good
chauffeur, Zung tried to introduce me as a chauffeur. When I
heard this story I was delighted for the time had come to
approach a high official which I promised to Yi Vung Ching, but
I did not feel myself so much interested as at the time when
Yi Vung Ching first told me to watch the movements of the high
officials of the Reformed Government. It is because if I
became a chauffeur, I can get a salary and nothing to worry
about my living, and because the work is very difficult as I
have already told to Zung at the Eastern Hotel. But at the
time when I become a chauffeur of the Minister of Home Affairs,
it is the best chance and easy to detect the movements of the
Minister, so that I can get a reward. When I visited Zung at
the office of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the following
day, the watchman told me that Zung was ill in bed at the
quarters of the Chief of the Home Affairs. Next day I visited
Zung again at the quarters but he was absent. I called at
Zung's quarters again on the third day, but it proved abortive.
Then I sent a letter to him, thinking that it would be useless
to visit him. The letter reads as follows :-
" I returned to Nanking on March 11th, and I was
pages.zh:
- 7 -

产生怀疑。然而，我认为在下次会面时逐步向他透露我们的计划是明智之举。
我于3月11日返回南京，并从一名叫范公（Van Kung）(音译)的住客处得知，大约在3月8日，内政部长的第23号司机（姓名不详）作为钟的信使访问了他的住所。部长的夫人购买了一辆汽车，由于她正在寻找一名优秀的司机，钟试图推荐我担任司机。听到这个消息我很高兴，因为向我向叶文清承诺的接近高官的时机已经到来，但我此时对此事的兴趣不如叶文清最初让我监视维新政府高官行踪时那样浓厚。这是因为如果我成为司机，我可以获得薪水，无需为生计担忧，而且正如我已在远东饭店告诉钟的那样，这项工作非常困难。但是，当我成为内政部长的司机时，这是最佳机会，也易于侦测部长的行踪，从而使我能够获得赏金。第二天我去内政部办公室拜访钟时，门卫告诉我，钟因病躺在内务主管的宿舍里。第二天我又去宿舍拜访钟，但他不在。第三天我再次前往钟的宿舍，但仍未果。随后我给他写了一封信，心想再去拜访他也是徒劳。信件内容如下：
“我于3月11日返回南京，并从唐寿根（Dong Zeu Kung）处得知

pages.en:
- 8 -

given to understand by Dong Zeu Kung (唐寿根) that
you were willing to introduce me as a chauffeur.
So I called at your quarters on 12th, 13th and 14th
of March, but failed to see you. If you have the
kindness to recommend me as a chauffeur please come
to my residence and see me. "

At about 9 a.m. 18-3-39, chauffeur No. 23 of the
Ministry of Home Affairs came to my residence on behalf of
Zung. He told me that Zung was waiting for me at his quarters
at about 10 a.m. on that day. Then I asked him to take me for
the watchman might refuse my admittance. The chauffeur agreed
and took me to the quarters, where I was arrested.

I have been acquainted with Zung for 3 or 4 years.
I was first introduced to him by Tau Ah Ling (邵阿林), a
chauffeur of Kying Kyeu Ling (金九林), the Chief Officer of
the French Police in Shanghai, residing at Boo Kao Li (步高里),
Rue Albert. I requested him three times in October, November
and December (Lunar Calendar) to recommend me to some firms as
a chauffeur.

I will now state how I became acquainted with Yi Vung
Ching. In June 1933, whilst I was in the employ of a lawyer
named Ts Dien Ching (朱殿卿), No. 4 San Shing Foong (三星坊),
Doo Zung Woo Road (杜神父路), French Concession, as a chauffeur,
I went with my friend named Ah San (阿三), a chauffeur of
Tseng (曾), residing at House No. 6 in the same alleyway, to
Koo Fah Li Co. (顾发利洋行), British Firm, in Taku Road, where
I was introduced to Yi Vung Ching by Ah San. Since then wo
pages.zh:
- 8 -

你愿意推荐我担任司机。
因此，我于3月12日、13日和14日前往你的宿舍，但未能见到你。如果你好意推荐我担任司机，请到我住处来见我。”

1939年3月18日上午约9点，内政部的第23号司机代表钟来到我的住处。他告诉我，钟当天上午约10点在他的宿舍等我。于是我请他带我去，因为门卫可能会拒绝我进入。司机同意了，并带我去了宿舍，在那里我被捕。

我认识钟已有三四年。最初是由邵阿林（Tau Ah Ling）介绍给我的，邵阿林是上海法租界警务处总监金九林（Kying Kyeu Ling）的司机，居住在阿尔贝路（Rue Albert）步高里（Boo Kao Li）。我在农历十月、十一月和十二月曾三次请求他推荐我到一些公司担任司机。

现将我如何结识叶文清的情况陈述如下。1933年6月，我在法租界杜神父路（Doo Zung Woo Road）三星坊（San Shing Foong）4号受雇于一名叫朱殿卿（Ts Dien Ching）的律师，担任司机。我与我的朋友阿三（Ah San）一同前往大沽路（Taku Road）的顾发利洋行（Koo Fah Li Co.，英国商行），阿三是曾（Tseng）先生的司机，住在同一条弄堂的6号。在那里，阿三将我介绍给叶文清。自此以后，我们

pages.en:
- 9 -

became close friends.
At about 6.30 p.m. 13-3-39, I attended the Dong Shing Tse (龍兴池) Bath House, at No. 16 Hupeh Road, to take a bath and whilst I was taking a rest on the seat No. 5 of the Special Waiting Room, my friend named Zee Zung Hwa (徐永華) came in at about 7 p.m. and took my next seat (No. 6). He told me that he had visited my residence and was informed where I was. He whispered to me, for there were about 5 or 6 other persons sitting in the waiting room, that I was watching the movements of the high officers of the Reformed Government and the Municipal Administration and reporting to Yi Vung Ching after locating their residences. He and Zung Koh Ziang (陳國祥) were undertaking a similar work, so if I had occasion to come to Shanghai shadowing the movements of high officers they wanted me to act in concert with them, and to report the matter to Yi Vung Ching.
When I heard of this I was inclined to believe that Zee Zung Hwa and Zung Koh Ziang were asked by Yi Vung Ching to do the same work. I simply replied them to do so but did not ask them anything particularly.
Zee Zung Hwa and Zung Koh Ziang are at present employed by the Japan Transportation Co. (日帝通運会社) as chauffeurs and are residing at 55 Pau Tah Ka (宝泰街), Nanking.
I became acquainted with Zee Zung Hwa in last June, being introduced by my friend, Tong Zeu Kung (唐春根), and Zung Koh Ziang in January last year, when we gambled together in Room No. 536, Eastern Hotel, in Shanghai, but I did not continue my
pages.zh:
- 9 -

成为了密友。
1939年3月13日下午约6点30分，我前往湖北路16号的龙兴池（Dong Shing Tse）浴室洗澡，当我在特别等候室的5号座位上休息时，我的朋友徐永华（Zee Zung Hwa）于晚上约7点进来，坐在我旁边的座位（6号）。他告诉我，他曾去过我的住处，并被告知了我的去向。由于等候室里还坐着大约五六个人，他低声对我说，我正在监视维新政府和市政当局高官的行踪，在确定他们的住所后向叶文清报告。他和陈国祥（Zung Koh Ziang）也在从事类似的工作，因此如果我有机会来上海监视高官的行踪，他们希望我与他们协同行动，并将此事报告给叶文清。
听到这些后，我倾向于相信徐永华和陈国祥是受叶文清指派做同样的工作。我只是回答让他们去做，并没有特别询问他们什么。
徐永华和陈国祥目前受雇于日帝通运会社（Japan Transportation Co.）担任司机，居住在南京宝泰街（Pau Tah Ka）55号。
我是去年六月通过我的朋友唐春根（Tong Zeu Kung）的介绍结识徐永华的，而结识陈国祥则是在去年一月，当时我们在上海远东饭店536号房间一起赌博，但我并未继续与他们保持

pages.en:
- 10 -
friendship with them.
I will state that I know about the connection between
Zee Zung Hwa, Zung Koh Ziang and Yi Yung Ching.
During the latter part of last June I visited Shanghai
on business and whilst I was staying in the Nanking Hotel Zee
Zung Hwa called on me. Later Yi Yung Ching came and I
introduced both of them.
Since that time Zee Zung Hwa and Yi Yung Ching used to
meet and seemed to be on good terms.
Zung Koh Ziang met Yi Yung Ching in my room, the
Nanking Hotel, during August and September last year.
Zee Zung Hwa is the close friend of Zung Koh Ziang.
QUESTION :- "Have you anything else to say?"
ANSWER :- "It is all what I have to state regarding this
case. I am prepared to face punishment for the
wrongs which I have done."
Signed & Thumbprinted : TAI AH DONG (戴阿堂).
pages.zh:
- 10 -
友谊。
我将陈述我所了解的徐永华、陈国祥与叶文清（Yi Yung Ching）之间的关系。
去年六月下旬，我因公务前往上海，住在南京饭店期间，徐永华来拜访我。后来叶文清也来了，我将他们两人作了介绍。
自那时起，徐永华和叶文清经常见面，似乎关系良好。
去年八月和九月，陈国祥在南京饭店我的房间里见到了叶文清。
徐永华是陈国祥的密友。
问：“你还有什么要说的吗？”
答：“关于此案，我要陈述的就是这些。我准备为我所犯下的过错接受惩罚。”
签名并按指印：戴阿堂（TAI AH DONG）。

pages.en:
M. C. C. B.
March 20, 39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE TO ARREST
A MALE CHINESE AT 159 TAKU ROAD.

C.D.I. CRUBB

The instructions of the D.C. (Crime) to
the effect that the chauffeur, Yee Yung Ching (葉文清),
arrested at 159 Taku Road, on March 13, would be
released on March 20, unless evidence was produced
against him, were conveyed to D.S.I. Umemoto to the
Japanese Gendarmerie at 9.45a.m. March 20.
Sgt. Major Katoda replied that as the
request for the man's arrest was made by the Gendarmerie
in Nanking, he would have to communicate by telephone
with Nanking.
At 11.35 a.m. March 20, D.S.I. Umemoto
received a telephone message from Sgt. Major Katoda,
stating that he had received a reply from Nanking to the
effect that several more arrests had been made there
and pending further information from that source, he
requested that Yee Yung Ching be detained.

C.D.I.
pages.zh:
M. C. C. B.
1939年3月20日。

协助日本宪兵队在大沽路159号逮捕一名中国男子。

C.D.I. CRUBB

刑事副主任（Crime）的指示指出，除非提出针对3月13日在大沽路159号被捕的司机叶文清（Yee Yung Ching）的证据，否则他将于3月20日获释，该指示已于3月20日上午9点45分传达给日本宪兵队的Umemoto警部补。
Katoda军曹回复称，由于逮捕该人的请求是由南京宪兵队提出的，他必须通过电话与南京方面联系。
1939年3月20日上午11点35分，Umemoto警部补收到Katoda军曹的电话留言，称他已收到南京方面的回复，大意是那里又逮捕了数人，在等待来自该方面的进一步消息期间，他要求拘留叶文清。

C.D.I.

pages.en:
HEADQUARTERS CRIME BRANCH
C. I. M. CRIMES FILE
No. 35/39
Date March 19, 39

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. P. REGISTRY
No. S. P. D. 827721
H. O. J. B.
Date ____
March 19, 39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE.

D.S.I. CRIGHTON                                C.D.I. GRUBB.

At 9 p.m. 18.3.39 Sgt. Major Katoda of
the Japanese Military Police communicated with D.S.I.
Umonoto of the S.P.O. requesting assistance for 6 a.m.
19.3.39 to arrest one named, YEE VUNG CHING (奚文卿),
a chauffeur, residing in the upstairs room of a
D. C. (Special Branch) Chinese tailor shop at 159 Taku Road.

FILE
（批：26）

Sgt.Major Katoda explained that at 3 p.m.
18.3.39 he had received a telephone call from the
headquarters of the Nanking Japanese Gendarmerie,
requesting him to arrest the aforesaid man for being
concerned in the planning of an attempt to be made on
the life of CHEN CHUEN (陳群), Minister of the
Interior of the "Reformed Government".

The usual formalities having been complied
with, the desired assistance was rendered at 6:10 a.m.
19.3.39, when a party of S.M.Police, consisting of the
undersigned, D.S.Fowler, D.S.Sugimoto, J.D.C.Yamahara,
D.I.Chu Shou Ling, C.D.S.'s 129, 172 and 304, accompanied
Sgt.Major Katoda and three other Japanese, proceeded
to the Hsing Sung Ziang Tailor Shop (興生祥), 159
Taku Road, and on the third floor, took into custody
one named, YEE VUNG CHING (奚文卿), age 32, native
of Pootung, M/Chauffeur, residing therein, also seized
（批：化） nine documents, two visiting cards, four photographs
and one Tientsin driving licence. (List attached).

Returning to Crime Branch Headquarters, the
undersigned further questioned Sgt.Major Katoda re the

上海公共租界工部局警务处

1939年3月19日。

协助日本军方警察。

D.S.I. CRIGHTON                                C.D.I. GRUBB.

1939年3月18日晚上9点，日本军方警察的Katoda军曹与特别处（S.P.O.）的Umonoto警部补联系，请求协助于1939年3月19日上午6点逮捕一名叫奚文卿（YEE VUNG CHING）的男子，此人系司机，居住在大沽路159号一家华人裁缝店（属特别处管辖）的楼上房间。

档案
（批：26）

Katoda军曹解释说，1939年3月18日下午3点，他接到南京日本宪兵队总部的电话，要求他逮捕上述男子，因其涉嫌策划企图杀害“维新政府”内政部长陈群（CHEN CHUEN）。

在完成常规手续后，所需的协助于1939年3月19日上午6点10分提供，当时由以下人员组成的上海公共租界警务处小组：签署人本人、Fowler副督察、Sugimoto副督察、Yamahara日籍侦探长、朱守令（Chu Shou Ling）侦探，以及编号为129、172和304的华人巡长，陪同Katoda军曹和其他三名日本人，前往大沽路159号的兴生祥（Hsing Sung Ziang）裁缝店，并在三楼拘捕了一名叫奚文卿（YEE VUNG CHING）的男子，年龄32岁，浦东人，职业为机动司机，居住于此；同时查获
（批：化）九份文件、两张名片、四张照片和一张天津驾驶执照。（附清单）。

返回刑事科总部后，签署人就相关情况进一步讯问了Katoda军曹

pages.en:
- 2 -

information supplied him in connection with the
arrested man, and as a result, was informed by that
officer that at 3 p.m. 18.3.39, he had received a
telephone communication from the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters in Nanking, stating that they had arrested
one named, TAI AH DONG (戴亞堂), in connection with
the planning of an attempt to be made on the life of
CHEN CHUEN (陳群), Minister of the Interior of
China for the "Reformed Government", and that this
man on being questioned, had implicated the arrested
man as being a principal, who, if the assassination
of Chen Chuen was successful, would pay him $150,000.00
Sgt.Major Katoda further explained that this
communication had been very brief, and that he expected
to have further details later.
The arrested man on being questioned, made a
voluntary written statement (attached) in which, he
relates his connections with Tai Ah Dong, and as can
be seen from same, there appears to be nothing of a
detrimental nature against him. However, until such
time as further particulars regarding the case are
obtained from Nanking, Sgt.Major Katoda requests that
he be detained.
Attached herewith is a list of the seized
documents, which when translated, tend to support the
arrested man's statement, that his connections with
Tai Ah Dong were purely business and not political.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

向他提供的关于被捕男子的信息，并因此从该警官处获悉，1939年3月18日下午3时，他接到南京日本宪兵司令部的电话通讯，称他们逮捕了一名名为戴亞堂（TAI AH DONG）的男子，该人涉嫌策划刺杀“维新政府”内政部长陳群（CHEN CHUEN），且此人在受审时供出被捕男子为主犯，若刺杀陈群成功，将支付其150,000.00美元。
加藤（Katoda）警佐进一步解释称，该通讯非常简短，他预计稍后会有更多细节。
被捕男子在受审时作出了一份自愿书面陈述（附后），其中叙述了他与戴亞堂的关系，从中可以看出，似乎没有任何对他不利的内容。然而，在从南京获得关于此案的更多详情之前，加藤警佐要求将其拘留。
随函附上查获文件清单，经翻译后，这些文件倾向于支持被捕男子的陈述，即他与戴亞堂的关系纯属商业性质，而非政治性质。

pages.en:
- 3 -

As can be seen from the suspect's statement,
he has been employed in Shanghai for the past seven
years with Gordon & Co. Ltd., 185 Yuen Ming Yuen Road,
first as a truck driver and later as a chauffeur to
Mr. F.B.Gange, General Manager of the said company.
The statement of the suspect is now being
checked and will be made the subject of a further
report.
At 11 a.m. 19.3.39 Mr. F. B. Gange called
at this office enquiring regarding the arrest of his
chauffeur, whom he claimed to be a man of very high
character and not likely to be mixed up in any criminal
activities. The circumstances surrounding his arrest
were briefly explained to Mr. Gange, who prior to
taking his leave, stated that he intended writing to
the Commissioner of Police in reference to this arrest.

John McPhar
D. S. I.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

从嫌疑人的陈述中可以看出，他在过去七年里受雇于上海圆明园路185号的Gordon & Co. Ltd.（高登有限公司），起初担任卡车司机，后来担任该公司总经理F.B.Gange先生的私人司机。
目前正对嫌疑人的陈述进行核实，并将作为进一步报告的主题。
1939年3月19日上午11时，F. B. Gange先生来到本办事处，询问其司机被捕一事，他声称该人品性极高，不太可能卷入任何犯罪活动。向Gange先生简要解释了其被捕的相关情况，Gange先生在离开前表示，打算就此次逮捕致信警务处处长。

John McPhar
副督察（D. S. I.）

pages.en:
YEE VUNG CHING ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), 32, M/Chauffeur,
Pootung, D.I. Chu Shou Ling,
C.1 19.3.39 Yao Dinsin.

My name is YEE VUNG CHING, alias Yee Vung Tsing ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ),
alias Ah Dee ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), aged 32, native of Pootung, married/
Chauffeur, and residing in an upstairs room at 159 Taku Road.

My father was a sack merchant, who died when I was 13
years of age. When I was 7 years old, I studied in a small
village school for 3 years. After the death of my father, I
was sent to a village mason to be taught in masonry for two
years. At the age of 14, when I was still an apprentice in
that profession, I accidentally fell down from the building
works, which prevented me from becoming a mason. I had a
sister who was married to Wu Pau Gee, proprietor of a motor car
repair shop in Tientsin. My sister died 5 years ago.

After I left the mason's house, I was sent to the
Nang Hai Motor Car Repairing Hong in Tientsin, where my brother-
in-law taught me how to drive a car. This was at the age of 15
1922. Four years later, I became qualified as a motor car
driver, and after staying at the above repair shop for one more
year, I was recommended by a friend to be the chauffeur of Mr.
Zung Hang Tsung, General Manager of the Ih Tsing Realty Co.
located at the Japanese Concession in Tientsin. Four years
later, I was compelled to quit the job and come to Shanghai,
owing to the serious illness of my sister. In Shanghai, after
two months without anything to do, I finally succeeded in becoming
a truck driver with the Gordon & Co. Ltd. through the recommen-
dation of a friend, Faung Ah Leh. Two years later, I was
promoted to be Mr. Gange's chauffeur. Mr. Gange is the manager
of Gordon & Co. Ltd. with whom I am still working. I receive
pages.zh:
YEE VUNG CHING（〔此处转录不清〕），32岁，男/司机，浦东，督察朱守灵（Chu Shou Ling），
C.1 1939年3月19日 姚丁新（Yao Dinsin）。

我叫YEE VUNG CHING，别名Yee Vung Tsing（〔此处转录不清〕），别名阿弟（Ah Dee）（〔此处转录不清〕），32岁，浦东人，已婚/司机，居住在大沽路159号楼上房间。

我父亲是一名麻袋商人，在我13岁时去世。我7岁时，在一所乡村小学读了3年书。父亲去世后，我被送到村里的一名石匠那里学习石工两年。14岁时，我仍在那一行当学徒，不慎从建筑工地摔下，导致我无法成为石匠。我有一个姐姐，嫁给了天津一家汽车修理店的老板吴宝吉（Wu Pau Gee）。我姐姐5年前去世。

离开石匠家后，我被送到天津的南海汽车修理行（Nang Hai Motor Car Repairing Hong），在那里我的姐夫教我如何驾驶汽车。那是1922年，我15岁。四年后，我取得了汽车驾驶员资格，在上述修理店又待了一年后，经朋友推荐，成为位于天津日租界的益清地产公司（Ih Tsing Realty Co.）总经理宗恒宗（Zung Hang Tsung）先生的司机。四年后，由于姐姐病重，我被迫辞职来到上海。在上海闲赋两个月后，经朋友方阿乐（Faung Ah Leh）推荐，我终于在Gordon & Co. Ltd.（高登有限公司）当上了卡车司机。两年后，我晋升为Gange先生的司机。Gange先生是Gordon & Co. Ltd.的经理，我至今仍为其工作。我的月薪为

pages.en:
- 2 -

$40 per month as salary in addition to an allowance of $5.
During the period as a truck driver, I made the
acquaintance of Tai Ah Dong, a chauffeur employed by Lawyer
Tsu Dien Ching, who used to visit the 2nd. S.S.D.Court in
French Concession, every day. At that time the Gordon & Co.
was erecting a building in the vicinity of the 2nd. S.S.D.Court
and, being a truck driver, it was my duty to drive to the
building grounds to supply building materials etc. Tai Ah
Dong and I used to meet several times a day, and thus became
known to each other. Several months later, after the building
was completed, we seldom see each other, unless on some
occasions when his car and mine came to pass each other.
One day in 1935, I happened to meet Tai near the gate
of the Central Theatre, Pakhoi and Yunnan Road corner. There
he informed me that he and a friend had purchased a car which
was for hire purposes. About a year later, when I met him
again near the Central Theatre, I learned that the partnership
between his friend and himself had come to an end and that he
alone had owned a car with the Central Theatre as the centre of
his hire business.
At the commencement of hostilities in August, 1937,
I learned that Tai had returned to his native town in Zanzhing,
having evaded payments of debt. During November of that year,
Tai came back to Shanghai and paid a visit to my house. I was
ill at the time, and I was glad to see him as I needed him to
be my substitute for my master car, which he did for half a
month. During the period when he was my substitute, he was
pages.zh:
- 2 -

40美元，另有5美元津贴。
在担任卡车司机期间，我结识了戴亞堂，他是律师徐殿青（Tsu Dien Ching）雇佣的司机，每天往返于法租界第二特区法院。当时Gordon & Co.正在第二特区法院附近建造一栋楼房，作为一名卡车司机，我的职责是开车到建筑工地运送建筑材料等。戴亞堂和我每天见面数次，从而相互认识。几个月后，大楼完工，我们很少见面，除非偶尔他的车和我的车相遇。
1935年的一天，我碰巧在北海路与云南路转角的大光明电影院门口遇到戴。他告诉我，他和一个朋友买了一辆车用于出租。大约一年后，当我再次在大光明电影院附近遇到他时，我得知他与朋友的合伙关系已经结束，他独自拥有一辆车，并以大光明电影院为中心开展出租业务。
1937年8月战事开始时，我得知戴因逃避债务回到了浙江老家。同年11月，戴回到上海并到我家拜访。当时我生病了，很高兴见到他，因为我需要他替我开主人的车，他替了半个月。在他代班期间，他在

pages.en:
- 3 -

registered with the S.M.P. Traffic Office as a chauffeur in the
employ of the Gordon & Co. However, after I was recovered, he
failed to surrender his driving permit to the Traffic Office for
cancellation. He kept it purposely, for fear that it would be
suspended after six months without employment.
In April, 1938, I learned that he had become a
dealer in tires. He used to travel between Shanghai and
Nanking, taking with him a number of either new or used tires.
In Shanghai, he used to sell them to the Foh Siang Truck Co.
on Canton Road near the Race Course, where he could obtain loans
immediately on arrival and settle up accounts just before he
left. In this city, he had no fixed abode, using hotels and
lodging houses as quarters. I was informed of his whereabouts
usually by telephone. His favourite place of abode was the
An Laung Lodging House, located in an alleyway adjacent to the
Nanking Theatre on Avenue Ed.VII.
On or about the 16th. of Feb, 1939, Ah Dong came to
Shanghai again, putting up in the Nanking Lodging House (room
situated on the third floor, near the stair case, & number
forgotten). When I paid him a visit, I met Ah Dong in the
company of another, named "Sai Ts". The former informed me that
business had been very bad and that he could not even afford to
buy some thick clothing for the winter. It was true, as I
noticed that he was still wearing autumn clothes in cold Feb.
weather. However, on the 20.2.39, when I called at the room
for the second time, I found the room already vacant.
During my first visit in his room I saw 2 or 3 tires
pages.zh:
- 3 -

工部局交通处登记为Gordon & Co.雇佣的司机。然而，在我康复后，他没有将驾驶执照交还交通处以注销。他故意保留执照，担心失业六个月后执照会被吊销。
1938年4月，我得知他成了一名轮胎经销商。他经常往返于上海和南京之间，携带一批新轮胎或旧轮胎。在上海，他通常将轮胎卖给跑马厅附近广东路上的福祥卡车行（Foh Siang Truck Co.），在那里他可以在到达时立即获得贷款，并在离开前结清账目。在本市，他没有固定住所，以旅馆和客栈为住处。我通常通过电话得知他的下落。他最喜欢的住处是爱多亚路（Avenue Ed.VII）南京大戏院旁巷子里的安隆客栈（An Laung Lodging House）。
1939年2月16日左右，阿东再次来到上海，住在南京客栈（房间位于三楼，靠近楼梯，房号已忘）。我去拜访他时，遇到阿东与另一名名为“赛茨”（Sai Ts）的人在一起。前者告诉我，生意很差，他甚至买不起过冬的厚衣服。确实如此，因为我注意到在寒冷的二月天气里，他仍穿着秋装。然而，1939年2月20日，当我第二次去房间拜访时，发现房间已经空了。
在我第一次去他房间时，我看到2或3条轮胎

pages.en:
- 4 -

which he had brought to Shanghai for sale. On that occasion,
he informed me that he had lost his driving permit that should
long be returned to the Traffic Office, requesting that I would
see Mr. Yui of Gordon & Co. asking the latter to write a letter
to the I.M.P. to that effect. This, however, was rejected on
the grounds that he had long left the firm and that it would
be silly for me to approach Mr. Yui with such a request. My
refusal marks the end of our friendship.

On the forenoon of 9.3.39, a letter addressed to Tai
Ah Deung by Tsung Sing Ding (whom I do not know) was delivered
to my house . As I used to know that Tai visited the Foh Ziang
Truck Hong on Canton Road whenever he was in Shanghai, I handed
this letter to the above truck hong for delivery to the right
person. However, on arrival, I was informed that Tai had left
on the previous day (8th.inst.), so I had to bring it back with
me and kept it in my house. Subsequently, I wrote a letter
to Tsung Sing Ding in Nanking, whose address was found on the
cover of the let. letter, informing him of the absence of Tai
Ah Dong. However, on the 16th. inst. I received a letter
(No.3) addressed to me by Ah Dong, who requested me to open the
letter which was left in my care and cash a $10 order cheque,
with which I was further requested to redeem from a pawnshop
an overcoat belonging to Tsung Sing Ding. I was also asked to
obtain the pawn ticket from his friend, named Kwei Tseong, who
was usually found around the sweets stalls in the Great World
Amusement Park. Accordingly, I opened the letter (No.I) and
found the order cheque. Then I sent him a letter informing him
pages.zh:
- 4 -

那是他带到上海出售的。在那次场合，他告诉我，他丢失了早就应该归还给交通处的驾驶执照，请求我去见Gordon & Co.的余先生（Mr. Yui），请后者为此事给工部局警务处（I.M.P.）写一封信。然而，这一请求被拒绝，理由是他早已离开公司，我带着这样的请求去找余先生是很愚蠢的。我的拒绝标志着我们友谊的终结。

1939年3月9日上午，一封由宗新亭（Tsung Sing Ding，我不认识此人）写给戴阿东（Tai Ah Deung）的信送到了我家。由于我知道戴每次在上海时都会去广东路的福祥卡车行（Foh Ziang Truck Hong），我将这封信交给上述卡车行转交正确的人。然而，到达后，我被告知戴已于前一天（本月8日）离开，所以我不得不把它带回来，放在家里。随后，我给在南京的宗新亭写了一封信，地址是从信封上找到的，告知他戴亞堂不在。然而，本月16日，我收到阿东写给我的一封信（第3号），信中请求我打开留在我处的信件，兑现一张10美元的指定支票，并用这笔钱从当铺赎回属于宗新亭的一件大衣。我还被要求从他的朋友桂强（Kwei Tseong）那里取得当票，桂强通常在大世界游乐场糖果摊附近出现。 accordingly，我打开了信件（第1号），发现了指定支票。然后我给他发了一封信，告知他

pages.en:
- 5 -

(No.4) informing him that the first letter (No.1) had not
been opened until I obtained his permission in his letter
(No.3).

Since my arrival in Shanghai in 1932, I have always
been with Gordon & Co. and have on no occasion left Shanghai
for other places. I have been living at 159 Taku Road for
the past six years.

I have never been employed by military, naval,
police, volunteers or any other government organs.

This is the truth.

Signed : YU WING CHENG.
pages.zh:
- 5 -

（第4号），告知他第一封信（第1号）直到我在他的信（第3号）中获得许可后才打开。

自1932年抵达上海以来，我一直在Gordon & Co.工作，从未离开上海去其他地方。过去六年我一直住在大沽路159号。

我从未受雇于军队、海军、警察、义勇队或任何其他政府机构。

以上属实。

签名：俞永成（YU WING CHENG）。

pages.en:
LIST OF DOCUMENTS SEIZED IN THE FRONT
ROOM (UPSTAIRS) OF HOUSE 159, TAKU RD.
OCCUPIED BY YEE VUNG CHING (美文卿).

1) Four letters (2 in draft form), addressed to "Ah Dong"
Yee Vung Ching and Tsaung Sing Ding, or vice versa.
( translations attached ).
2) One "Driving Permit"(No.1874) issued to Yee Vung Ching
by the "Concession Francaise", Tientsin.
3) Four photographs.
4) Two visiting cards (one named Zau Zui Vai (曹予蕃) and
the other Yee Vung Ching.)
5) Several waste papers.
6) One letter addressed to Yee Vung Ching by one named Kung
Sung, (宋 笙), requesting the former to purchase
in Shanghai 6 oil pumps for motor cars, preferably
of British make.
pages.zh:
在大沽路159号前屋（楼上）查获的文件清单，
该处由YEE VUNG CHING（美文卿）居住。

1) 四封信（两封为草稿），收件人为“阿东”、Yee Vung Ching和庄新亭（Tsaung Sing Ding），或反之。（附译文）。
2) 一张由天津“法租界”签发给Yee Vung Ching的“驾驶执照”（第1874号）。
3) 四张照片。
4) 两张名片（一张名为曹予蕃（Zau Zui Vai），另一张为Yee Vung Ching。）
5) 几张废纸。
6) 一封由名为宋笙（Kung Sung）的人写给Yee Vung Ching的信，请求前者在上海购买6个汽车油泵，最好是英国制造。

TRANSLATION OF A LETTER ADDRESSED TO
TAI AH DONG (戴阿东), C/O YEE VUNG CHING
BY TSAUNG SING DING & DONG ZUR KUNG IN
NANKING. (章新亭) (唐祖康).

( LETTER NO. I ).

March 7, 1939.

Dear Ah Dong,

We hope you had a pleasant trip and arrived
safely in Shanghai. Owing to the absence of the chief
of our "squad" (?), the matter relating to the sale of
his car cannot be discussed at present. However, there
is another car near the Chungsan Gate, and we have sent
men over to find out if its condition is O.K. Regarding
the tires, we have so far purchased three, two are second-
handed ones (about 80 % new) and the other absolutely new
with its packing still unremoved. The price for those
tires being $100.00.

As we have so many things to speak about, we
hope you would come back to Nanking immediately.

I have left one of my shirts in the hotel.
Please bring it back on your way to Nanking.

I inclose herewith an order cheque for $10.
You will please cash it and redeem the things which I
have pawned.

Hoping to see you soon,

Yours very sincerely,

Sd: TSAUNG SING DING.
DONG ZUR KUNG.
pages.zh:
章新亭（TSAUNG SING DING）和唐祖康（DONG ZUR KUNG）在南京写给戴阿东（TAI AH DONG）、由YEE VUNG CHING转交的信件译文。

（第一封信）。

1939年3月7日。

亲爱的阿东，

希望你旅途愉快，平安抵达上海。由于我们“小队”队长缺席，目前无法讨论有关出售他的汽车的事宜。然而，中山门附近还有另一辆车，我们已经派人去查看其状况是否良好。关于轮胎，我们目前购买了三条，两条是二手的（约八成新），另一条是全新的，包装尚未拆除。这些轮胎的价格为100.00美元。

因为有很多事情要谈，希望你立即返回南京。

我把一件衬衫落在旅馆了。请在回南京的路上把它带回来。

随函附上一张10美元的指定支票。请兑现并赎回我典当的物品。

希望能很快见到你，

您真诚的，

签名：章新亭（TSAUNG SING DING）。
唐祖康（DONG ZUR KUNG）。

TRANSLATION OF ATTACHED LETTER (NO.III)
ADDRESSED TO YEE VUNG CHING BY AH DONG.

March 14, 1939.

Dear Vung Ching,
I have arrived in Nanking safely. I have to
apologise for not being able to pay my respects to your
mother during my brief stay in Shanghai. I wanted to,
but after I lost so much in gambling, I felt ashamed of
myself to see her without bringing her any presents.
I have just learned that Sing Ding had sent
me a letter, enclosing a $10 order cheque, which arrived
in Shanghai after I had left. I am sure you are still in
possession of that letter, as it was sent to me care of
your home.
You know, during my stay in Shanghai, I had
an urgent need for some cash. As I had lost almost every
cent from gambling, I had to pawn some of Sing Ding's
clothes for some pocket money and to pay my way back to
Nanking. As Sing Ding did not know that I had already
left Shanghai, he sent to me the $10 order cheque to
redeem his clothes.
At present, you have to undertake the trouble
of cashing the cheque, and have Sing Ding's clothes redeemed
and sent back to Nanking by post. Please send them to
us, care of House No.9, Sih Ka Hong Alley, Nanking, the home
of Mr. Tsaung Sing Ding.
With kindest regards to your mother,
Yours etc.
"Ah Dong".
pages.zh:
附件信函（第三号）译文
阿东致叶荣庆。

1939年3月14日。

亲爱的荣庆：
我已平安抵达南京。对于我在上海短暂停留期间未能向令堂请安，我深表歉意。我本欲前往，但因在赌博中输掉太多钱财，我觉得空手去见她实在羞愧难当。
我刚得知，新丁曾给我寄来一封信，内附一张10美元的汇票，该信在我离开上海后才送达。我相信那封信仍由你保管，因为它是通过你家转交给我的。
你知道，我在上海逗留期间急需用钱。由于我在赌博中几乎输光了每一分钱，我不得不典当新丁的一些衣物，以换取零用钱并支付返回南京的路费。由于新丁不知道我已经离开上海，他寄给我那张10美元的汇票，以便赎回他的衣物。
目前，需劳烦你将汇票兑现，赎回新丁的衣物，并通过邮政寄回南京。请将衣物寄至南京四家巷9号庄新丁先生寓所转交我们。
代我向令堂致以最亲切的问候，
此致
“阿东”。

来信收悉。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie.

At 6.45 a.m. on the 19-3-39, D.J. Fowler attached to Crime Branch Headquarters informed this station by telephone that the above section had rendered assistance to the Japanese Gendarmerie and had arrested a male Chinese in Chengtu Road District.

Enquiries by the undersigned ascertained that at 6.10 a.m. on the 19-3-39, D.S.I. Craighton, D.S. Fowler, C. 1, with D.S. Sugimoto and D.S. Yamahara, S.P.O. had in the company of Sgt. Major Tatota and three other Japanese Gendarmerie, proceeded to 159 Taku Road where they effected the arrest of a male Chinese named Kyi Vung Ching (紀文卿) who was wanted in connection with terroristic activities.

The information concerning the above man had been obtained by the Japanese Gendarmerie from a prisoner in Nanking.

No details are as yet available as to the disposal of the arrested man, but this report is forwarded for information.

于1939年3月26日向日本宪兵队提供的协助，参见 C.I. Misc. 37/39。该报告的副本已送至捕房。

看来，1939年3月27日提供的协助旨在逮捕一名名为 Tseu Chi Lien ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) 的人，据称是一名居住在格兰特饭店306号房间的游击队首领。该信息是从一名名为 Loh Kuh Tsung ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) 的人处获得的，此人当时在日本宪兵队的监管之下，并于1939年3月27日下午5时在爱丁堡路 Ts Ung Peng 被上述当局逮捕。据称，线人是与通缉犯同一团体的成员，他指出通缉犯应对1939年1月公大纱厂爆炸案负责。

此次协助证明毫无结果，未实施任何逮捕。

Loh Kuh Tsung 后来被日本宪兵队临时释放，条件是他需找到 Tseu Su Lien，但他一直受到两名中国线人的严密跟踪，这两名线人是 Tsang Yoong Fei（从侦探手中逃脱）和 Wong Ts Yoong，别名 Wong Kying Kung（被捕并移交给法国警察）。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Informers attended 94 Jessfield Road, where they stated that Loh Kuh Tsung had been seized in Room No. 722, New World Hotel, by members of the Guerrilla unit led by Tseu Shih Lien, and in view of this information Itō, Hashimoto and Suzuki, in company with the informers, proceeded to the hotel in Motor Car, License No. 3965, borrowed from A. Kosei, No. 56 N. Haining Road.

The Japanese members of the party remained in the car, whilst the two Chinese informers proceeded to Room No. 722, where they were arrested, and, following the story of an accomplice being in the car told by Tsang Yoong Pei, the French Detectives in company with the latter named person proceeded to the car, and the informer escaped.

In connection with this aspect of the incident, the Japanese Gendarmerie state that they desired to proceed to Ziangtu Road Station with the detectives and arrests, but this appears doubtful in view of their rescue of the informer, also the fact that they drove away and failed to make any immediate report or request for assistance.

The facts as obtained give the reason for the illegal functioning and details leading to it, however, it was later ascertained from the French Police that

随行中的日本成员留在车内，而两名中国线人进入722房间，随即被捕。据曾永培（Tsang Yoong Pei）所述，车内有一名同伙，法国侦探遂与此人一同前往汽车处，线人趁机逃脱。

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

D.S.I. Pryde
C.D.I, Grubb

At 8.30 p.m. on 26.3.39 assistance was rendered to Sgt.
Major Shida, two member of the Japanese Gendarmerie and one
Interpreter attached to the Western District Detachment
Japanese Gendarmerie by D.S.I. Pryde, D.S. Rhodes, D.S.I. Lieu
Kyung Ching and C.D.S.s 129 and 104.

The Japanese Gendarmerie brought with them a male Chinese
named Loh Koh Tsung (陸國楨) whom they claimed to have
arrested at 5 p.m. 26.3.39 in the Ts Ong Peng off Edinburgh
Road. They stated that they had seized three pistols at time
of arrest and that this man had admitted being a member of a
guerrilla unit which had bombed the Kong Dah Cotton Mill in
January 1939. They also stated that this man had implicated
one named Tseu Shi Lien (周軒廉) as the leader of this
guerrilla unit and that he occupied room 368 of the Grand
Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road. That they had telephoned to this
room at 7 p.m. and the wanted man was still there. Before
proceeding to this address, Sgt. Major Shida caused the
arrested man to again telephone to this room and it was
ascertained that the wanted man had already left there.

A visit was then paid to this room and one named Lee
Ah Kung (李阿恭) was found inside. This man proved to be
a tout for a girl guide Bureau and as he was not required by
the Japanese Gendarmerie, he was not arrested. It was
ascertained that the room had been engaged by one named Zah
Foo Kung, age about 30, native of Kempe on 2.2.39 and he had
left the room at 6 p.m. 26.3.39. Sgt. Major Shida then
requested assistance to visit rooms Nos. 422 and 464 of the
same hotel, as he stated the wanted man might be visiting

副首席督察 普赖德（Pryde）
首席侦探督察 格鲁布（Grubb）

1939年3月26日晚8时30分，副首席督察普赖德、副侦探罗德兹（Rhodes）、副首席督察刘景清（Lieu Kyung Ching）以及首席侦探警员129号和104号，向日本宪兵队西区分队的小队长志田（Shida）少佐、两名日本宪兵队员及一名翻译提供了协助。

日本宪兵队带来一名名叫陆国桢（Loh Koh Tsung）的中国男子，声称于1939年3月26日下午5时在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）附近的乍浦路（Ts Ong Peng，音译）将其逮捕。他们称在逮捕时缴获三支手枪，且此人承认是1939年1月轰炸公大纱厂（Kong Dah Cotton Mill）的游击队成员。他们还称此人供出周轩廉（Tseu Shi Lien）为该游击队首领，并住在亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road）大华饭店（Grand Hotel）368房间。他们称于晚7时致电该房间，被通缉者当时仍在那里。在前往该地址之前，志田少佐让被捕者再次致电该房间，经查实被通缉者已离开。

随后派人查看该房间，发现里面有一名名叫李阿恭（Lee Ah Kung）的男子。此人证实是一名向导社的女导游拉客者，因日本宪兵队不需要他，故未予逮捕。经查，该房间由一名名叫查福根（Zah Foo Kung，音译）、约30岁、肯佩（Kempe，音译）籍人士于1939年2月2日租用，他已于1939年3月26日下午6时离开房间。随后，志田少佐请求协助查看同一旅馆的422和464房间，因为他称被通缉者可能正在拜访

REPORT

Subject Assistance to Japanese Naval Authorities and Consular Police in
Searching houses without a warrant.

Made by R. S. Jones Forwarded by [签名] C/I.
Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 1.28 p.m. on 31-3-39, J.P.C. 144 Ogata accompanied by
two N.C.O's from the Japanese Nav. Office, one Consular police
official and a Mr. Yaman, attached to the Japanese Liaison
Corporation Office, came to this Station and requested
assistance in visiting certain houses in the district.
Thinking that the assistance required was of the same nature as that
indicated in the attached Memo. File No. 25/38, I
accompanied the party of Japanese to the following addresses:-
Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6, 31 and 37 Kaying Terrace. No. 6 was
occupied by a Japanese family, while all the other houses were
tenanted by Russians.

On arrival at each of the houses the procedure was
invariably as follows: as soon as the door opened all the
Japanese troopers went in and started to explore the premises from
top to bottom, questioning the occupants.

Fortunately no incident occurred, but as I was afraid
something might happen as a result of such unwarranted intrusion
I told J.P.C. 144 to ask them what they were really seeking.
After much interrogation it came out that they were looking
for furniture supposed to have been left behind by the
Japanese Naval Landing Party in these houses when they were
unoccupied. At least, this was the best explanation I could
get from J.P.C. 144, who speaks little English.

Through the Japanese constable I tried to explain to the
party of officials that this mode of procedure if not actually
illegal was certainly against Municipal Police Regulations.
Although this was done with the utmost tact and courtesy it

（左侧手写批注：C/4 / Ross / 4/4 / [签名]）

报告

事由：协助日本海军当局及领事警察在无搜查令的情况下搜查房屋。

呈报人：R. S. 琼斯（Jones） 转呈人：[签名] C/I.
主管警官。

先生，

1939年3月31日下午1时28分，日本领事警察144号绪方（Ogata） accompanied by 两名来自日本海军办事处的士官、一名领事警察官员以及隶属于日本联络公司办事处的一名山曼（Yaman，音译）先生来到本巡捕房，请求协助探访辖区内的某些房屋。考虑到所需的协助性质与附件备忘录第25/38号文件中所述相同，我陪同日本一行人前往以下地址：嘉应台（Kaying Terrace）3、4、5、6、31和37号。6号住有一户日本家庭，而其他所有房屋均由俄国人租住。

到达每处房屋时，程序 invariably 如下：门一打开，所有日本士兵便闯入，开始从上到下搜查房屋，并盘问住户。

幸运的是未发生任何事件，但由于我担心这种无端侵入可能导致某种事端，我便告诉日本领事警察144号，让他们询问对方究竟在寻找什么。经过多方讯问，得知他们正在寻找据称是日本海军陆战队在这些房屋无人居住时遗留在那里的家具。至少，这是我从英语不太好的日本领事警察144号那里得到的最好解释。

通过这名日本巡捕，我试图向这伙官员解释，这种行事方式即便不算是违法，也肯定违反了公共租界警务规章。尽管此举极尽委婉与礼貌，但

（左侧手写批注：C/4 / Ross / 4/4 / [签名]）

ENQUIRIES RE EXTORTION AND INTIMIDATION
AND ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

Since the arrest of the seven accused they
have been thoroughly interrogated regarding their
activities and it was ascertained that the 1st, 3rd,
5th. and 6th. accused were concerned together in
extorting $570.00 from the complainant Yue Lien Zien
(俞廉亭) employed by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha by
posing as members of a mobile unit.

Zung Van Sung (陳維昇) the 3rd. accused
admits that it was he who suggested to the 6th. accused
that they extort $5,000.00 from the complainant, because
he was dealing in scrap iron and brass with the Japanese.
The 3rd. and 6th. accused then decided to write a
letter of warning to the complainant and at the same
time make a demand for the $5,000.00.

The letter was written by the 3rd. accused
and on 22/3/39 or 23/3/39, the 1st, 3rd. and 6th.
accused attempted to deliver the letter to the com-
plainant at his home at No.15 Lane 839 Avenue Road,
but as he was not at home the letter was not delivered.
On the night of the same date the 1st, 3rd,
5th. and 6th. accused planned to deliver the letter
on the following day at noon. The letter was

关于敲诈勒索和恐吓的调查
及协助日本宪兵队。

自七名被告被捕以来，已就其活动进行了彻底讯问，经查实，第一、第三、第五和第六被告共同冒充流动小组成员，向三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）雇员俞廉亭（Yue Lien Zien）敲诈勒索570.00美元。

第三被告陈维昇（Zung Van Sung，音译）承认，是他向第六被告建议向投诉人敲诈5,000.00美元，因为投诉人正与日本人进行废铁和黄铜交易。随后，第三和第六被告决定写一封警告信给投诉人，同时索要5,000.00美元。

信件由第三被告撰写，1939年3月22日或23日，第一、第三和第六被告试图将信件送至投诉人位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）839弄15号的家中，但因他不在家，信件未能送达。同日当晚，第一、第三、第五和第六被告计划于次日中午送达信件。信件已

subsequently delivered by the 5th. accused, the 3rd.
accused remaining outside. Whilst the 5th. accused
was on the premises, he did not see the complainant
but interviewed one named Tsang who stated that he was
a representative of the complainant. It was arranged
by Tsang that he should meet the representatives of
the mobile unit at 4 p.m. the following day, 23rd. or
24th. of March 1939, whereupon the 5th. accused departed
after leaving his name card which represented him as
captain of a mobile unit.

At the appointed time the 1st. and 5th. accused
proceeded to the complainant's home where they met
Tsang and a lawyer named Wong Sheng Dong (王 **〔此处转录不清〕** )
who suggested that they adjourn to the China Hotel and
discuss the situation. At the China Hotel Tsang paid
$400.00 to the 5th. accused and it was promised that the
complainant would not be molested. The 1st.accused
admits having received $45.00 as his share of the money
and at a later date he received the further sum of
$100.00 from Tsang on Szechuen Road. This $100.00 was
seized on the person of the 1st. accused at the time
of arrest.

The 3rd. accused denies having received any
money as his share of the extortion, but the 5thaccused
avers that he paid him $310.00. The 6th. accused

随后由第五被告交付，第三被告留在外面。当第五被告在屋内时，他并未见到报案人，而是会见了一位姓曾（Tsang）的人，此人声称他是报案人的代表。经曾某安排，他将于次日，即1939年3月23日或24日下午4时与流动部队（mobile unit）的代表会面，随后第五被告留下了一张名片后离去，名片上显示其身份为流动部队队长。

在约定时间，第一被告和第五被告前往报案人家中，在那里他们会见了曾某和一位名叫王盛东（Wong Sheng Dong，王 **〔此处转录不清〕** ）的律师，后者建议他们移步至中国饭店（China Hotel）商议情况。在中国饭店，曾某向第五被告支付了400.00元，并承诺不再骚扰报案人。第一被告承认收到45.00元作为其分得的款项，并在稍后日期于四川路从曾某处又收到100.00元。这100.00元在第一被告被捕时从其身上搜出。

第三被告否认收到任何作为勒索分赃的款项，但第五被告坚称已支付给他310.00元。第六被告

also denies having received any money from the 5th.
accused.
It is definite that these men are not members
of a mobile unit nor have they ever possessed firearms
and they only posed as guerillas to terrorize the
complainant into paying over a sum of money.
The 1st. and 5th. accused have been recognized
by the lawyer Wong Shing Dong as the persons who called
at the house of the complainant and who received the
money from Tseng in the China Hotel.
The 3rd. and 6th. accused have been identified
by the 1st. and 5th. accused as accomplices and they
themselves also admit participation in the extortion.
The letter written to the complainant by the
3rd. accused was burned by him prior to any arrests
being made. The complainant has not visited Crime
Branch Headquarters, but in a statement he admits that
a friend named Tsang paid the accused several hundred
dollars on his behalf and that Tsang is now in Hongkong.
Further questioning of the accused elicited
that at about 5.30 p.m. 30/3/39, the 5th. accused
telephoned to a Formosan named Ling Ts Kyuin (林資炯),
employee of the Japanese Fui Co. (福益公司), 20 Canton
Road, to the effect that the caller was the captain of

也否认从第五被告处收到任何款项。
可以确定的是，这些人并非流动部队的成员，他们也从未拥有过枪支，他们只是冒充游击队以恐吓报案人交出钱款。
律师王盛东（Wong Shing Dong）指认第一被告和第五被告就是那些前往报案人家中并在中国饭店从曾某处接收款项的人。
第三被告和第六被告被第一被告和第五被告指认为同伙，他们自己也承认参与了勒索。
第三被告写给报案人的信件在任何逮捕行动发生之前已被其烧毁。报案人未曾前往刑事侦缉处总部，但在一份供词中他承认，一位名叫曾某的朋友代他向被告支付了数百美元，且曾某现在香港。
对被告的进一步讯问获悉，大约在1939年3月30日下午5时30分，第五被告致电一名名为林资炯（Ling Ts Kyuin）的台湾人，此人是位于广东路20号的日本福益公司（Fui Co.）的雇员，来电声称打电话的人是拥有52名队员的游击队队长，急需资金以便前往九江，如果林资炯不支付300.00元，将采取严厉措施。

（批：另见 J 8846）

pages.en:

a guerilla unit of 52 men who were in need of funds to
enable them to proceed to Kiukiang and if $300.00 was
not paid over by Ling Ts Kyuin drastic measures would
be taken. The 5th. accused gave his name and suggested
that Ling should meet him at the entrance of the Wing On
Building between 5.30 p.m. and 6 p.m. next day, 31/3/39.
At about 3 p.m. 31/3/39 a further telephone call was
received by Ling reminding him of the appointment.

At the appointed time another employee of the
Fui Co. named Ching Hsing ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) kept the appoint-
ment and there met the 5th. accused and another male
Chinese and they discussed the payment of the $300.00.
Ching Hsing was warned not to report the case to the
S.M.Police or the Japanese Military for if he did his
life would be in danger from the 1000 guerillas in and
around the Western District of Shanghai.

The 5th. accused then gave Ching a card
similar to the one left at the home of Yue Lien Zien and
a further appointment was made in the Wong On Tea Room
for 10.30 a.m. - 11 a.m. 1/4/39.

As already mentioned in diary 2, the 5th.
accused was arrested when he kept the appointment because
of the complainant reporting the matter to the Japanese
Gendarmerie.

第五被告报上姓名，并建议林某于次日，即1939年3月31日下午5时30分至6时在永安大楼入口处与他见面。
1939年3月31日下午3时许，林某接到另一个电话，提醒他赴约。

在约定时间，福益公司的另一名雇员名为程兴（Ching Hsing， **〔此处转录不清〕** ）前去赴约，在那里会见了第五被告和另一名中国男子，他们讨论了支付300.00元的事宜。程兴受到警告，不得将此案报告给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.Police）或日本军方，否则他在上海西区及其周边的1000名游击队将危及他的生命。

随后，第五被告给了程兴一张卡片，类似于留在岳连先（Yue Lien Zien）家中的那张，并另行约定于1939年4月1日上午10时30分至11时在宏安茶室（Wong On Tea Room）见面。

正如日记2中已提到的那样，由于报案人向日本宪兵队报告了此事，第五被告在赴约时被逮捕。

Subsequent enquiries proved that the 6th.
accused had been employed by the complainant to sell
5 coloured flags used by the Reformed Government and
it was his information to the 5th. accused that caused
the extortion attempt to be made. Both the 5th. and
6th. accused have been identified by the complainants.
The 1st, 3rd, 5th. and 6th. accused are
definitely involved in extorting money by means of
threats and it is suspected that the 2nd, 4th. and
7th. accused are subsidiary members of the gang.
Shanenko No.390 has been received from the
Japanese Authorities requesting that all seven accused
be handed over to them for trial.
The 6th. and 7th. accused were handed over
to the S.M.P. by the French Police to answer a charge
of extortion.

J. Handley

随后的调查证实，第六被告受雇于报案人，出售维新政府使用的五面彩旗，正是他向第五被告提供的情报导致了此次勒索企图。报案人已指认出第五和第六被告。
第一、第三、第五和第六被告确实参与了以威胁手段勒索钱财，怀疑第二、第四和第七被告是该团伙的从属成员。
已收到来自日本当局的第390号 Shanenko 函件，要求将所有七名被告移交给他们进行审判。
第六和第七被告由法国巡捕房移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，以应对勒索指控。

AUNG VI SING (          ), 27, S/Unemployed,
Haimen, Chekiang,                D. I. I. Soong Sing Tsung,
C.1             31. 3. 39                      Yao Dinsin.

My name is Aung Vi Sing, aged 27 years, native of Haimen, S/
Unemployed, M.P.A.

    One day in January, 1939, when dining at the Tsunghsin
Restaurant, Foochow Road, I overheard from the diners of a
separate table, to the effect that a traitorous merchant, named
Yui Lai Ding, who had amassed an immense fortune through trading
in scrap iron with the Japanese, had been victimized by an
extortion gang, who relieved him of a handsome sum of money,
using threats under the name of patriotic organisations. Further
I overheard that Yui was a nervous sort of man, who would prove
an easy victim under intimidation.  I was at that time in
extreme poverty, and was eager to make some money, even if I
was to run afoul of the law.  I was glad to obtain the above
information, deeming it an excellent opportunity to make some
easy money.  Efforts were then made to find out who and where
the intended victim was, and that whether he was actually
concerned in traitorous activities.  Enquiries were continued
for about a month, when finally, I succeeded in ascertaining
the address of Yui Lai Ding, as well as the fact that he had
actually been dealing with the Japanese in scrap iron etc.
    As everything was ready, I went to see my friend, Lee
Dah Mei, at the Koh Tai Lodging House, Rue Hue, E/C, inviting
the latter to take part in the intended extortion.  Lee was in
stringent circumstances as well, and he immediately agreed to
give me a hand.  This was on 20.3.39, and after a lengthy
discussion with Lee, we finally decided to deliver a letter of
threats to the intended victim, under the name of a patriotic
pages.zh:
AUNG VI SING (          )，27岁，单身/无业，
浙江海门，                D. I. I. 宋信宗 (Soong Sing Tsung),
C.1             1939年3月31日                      姚丁新 (Yao Dinsin).

我叫 Aung Vi Sing，27岁，浙江海门人，单身/无业，M.P.A.。

    1939年1月的一天，我在福州路的新新酒楼（Tsunghsin Restaurant）用餐时，无意中听到邻桌食客谈话，大意是一名名为余来定（Yui Lai Ding）的奸商，通过与日本人交易废铁积累了巨额财富，遭到一个勒索团伙的侵害，该团伙以爱国组织的名义进行威胁，骗走了他一大笔钱。此外，我还听说余某是个神经质的人，在恐吓下很容易成为受害者。当时我极度贫困，渴望赚些钱，即使触犯法律也在所不惜。我很高兴获得上述信息，认为这是一个赚取轻松钱财的绝佳机会。于是 efforts 设法查明预定受害者的身份和地点，以及他是否确实从事叛国活动。调查持续了约一个月，最终，我成功查明了余来定的地址，以及他确实与日本人进行废铁等交易的事实。
    万事俱备后，我去法租界华山路（Rue Hue）的科泰旅馆（Koh Tai Lodging House）看望我的朋友李达梅（Lee Dah Mei），邀请他参与预谋的勒索。李当时处境也很艰难，他立即同意帮我一把。那是1939年3月20日，在与李长时间讨论后，我们最终决定以爱国

society. As the letter should be chopped, I obtained a large
piece of soap, and by means of a small knife, I carved thereon,
the characters " ", i.e. "The Sweat and Blood Group
For Termination of Traitors." In the letter which I wrote,
I strongly denounced Yui Lai Ding as a traitor, using all sorts
of phrases with a threatening nature, & demanding that Yue pay a
$5,000.00 fine to save his neck. We decided to deliver the
letter in person, and after sealing same, we set out toward
our destination. However, on leaving, Lee appointed me to
meet him at the intersection of Avenue and Park Roads, as he
had to go and obtain the aid of another man. We then parted,
and when I got to Avenue Park Road Corner, Lee was already
there, and in his company, there was one, named Tsang Tsoo Zung,
whom Lee had engaged to take part in the attempt also. It was
raining when we arrived at the entrance of Bing Woo Li, in
which lived the intended victim. I then handed the letter to
Tsang Tsoo Zung, who was to deliver it. Whilst Tsang was
on his way to House 15, home of Yui Lai Ding, Lee and I shared
an umbrella at the entrance of the alleyway, awaiting Tsang's
return. A few minutes later, Tsang came out and informed us
that Yui was not in, so the letter was not delivered, he handing
same back to me for safe keeping. The three of us then proceeded
to the Jing S Tai Tea Shop, Ginza Road, where we held another
discussion, after which, we parted with each other, but
appointing to meet at the Koh Tai Lodging House whenever needed.
At about 4 or 5 p.m. same date, when I proceeded to
Lee's room in the Koh Tai Lodging House, Tsang and Lee were br
pages.zh:
- 2 -

社团的名义向预定受害者投递一封恐吓信。由于信件需要盖章，我弄来一大块肥皂，用小刀在上面刻了“ ”字样，即“肃清汉奸铁血团”。在我写的信中，我强烈谴责余来定为汉奸，使用了各种带有威胁性质的措辞，并要求余支付5,000.00元罚款以保命。我们决定亲自投递信件，封好信后，我们便出发前往目的地。然而，离开时，李让我在大西路（Avenue Road）和公园路（Park Roads）交叉口等他，因为他要去寻求另一个人的帮助。随后我们分开，当我到达大西路公园路口时，李已经在那里，和他在一起的还有一个名叫曹祖宗（Tsang Tsoo Zung）的人，李雇佣他也参与此次尝试。当我们到达预定受害者居住的炳武里（Bing Woo Li）门口时，正下着雨。我将信件交给负责投递的曹祖宗。当曹前往余来定家（15号）时，李和我在巷口共撑一把伞，等待曹回来。几分钟后，曹出来说余不在家，所以信没送成，他把信交还给我保管。随后我们三人前往静安寺路（Ginza Road）的景星泰茶馆（Jing S Tai Tea Shop），在那里进行了另一次讨论，之后我们各自散去，但约定如有需要便在科泰旅馆见面。
同日大约下午4或5点，当我前往科泰旅馆李的房间时，曹和李都在

pages.en:
.. 3 -

there. At about 7 p.m. same date, Lee Kwong Ying also came.
At 10 p.m. Yang Tsoh Ping appeared. After a lengthy planning,
it was finally decided, that(Yang's suggestion) Kwong Ying
Lee/and I
would deliver the letter again on the morrow at 12 noon. At
the appointed time, the next day, Lee Kwong Ying and I set
out toward Yui's house. On arrival, Lee entered the house
with the letter, whilst I remained outside. Several minutes
later, Lee Kwong Ying came out and told me that he had
interviewed one, Mr. Tsang, a representative of Yui Lei Ding's
who had appointed him to meet again at 4 p.m. the next day,
23.3.39 for a detailed discussion of the matter. Lee told
me that it seemed everything was quite alright, and that we
could from then on meet at the Sun Sun Roof Garden. I did not
suspect him at all and returned with him to the Koh Tai L.H.
where we discontinued the hire of our room therein. However,
I visited the Sun Sun Roof Garden on many an occasion, but
could find no trace of Lee Kwong Ying and Tsang Tsoo Zung.
Soon, I learned that Lee Kwong Ying and Tsang Tsoo Zung had
succeeded in extorting a large sum of money from the victim
and they had kept every cent themselves. I was eager to find
them, so I visited the roof garden every day, and on 28.3.39
when I was again looking for these two men, I was arrested by
police. This is the truth.

DESCRIPTIONS :
1) LEE KWONG YING ; age 23/4, Hsuchow, 5'3/4", long sallow
face, hair brushed backwards, Shanghai
dialect, wearing foreign clothes and
brown felt hat.
2) LEE DAH MEI : age 23/4, Honan, 5'5/8", medium build, long
dark face, hair backwards, Shanghai dialect
wearing blue cloth gown and grey felt hat.

Signed etc by : ZUNG VHE SING.
pages.zh:
.. 3 -

那里。同日晚上7点左右，李广英（Lee Kwong Ying）也来了。晚上10点，杨佐平（Yang Tsoh Ping）出现。经过长时间的策划，最终决定（根据杨的建议），由李广英、李达梅和我于次日中午12点再次投递信件。次日约定时间，李广英和我出发前往余家。到达后，李带着信进入屋内，而我留在外面。几分钟后，李广英出来告诉我，他会见了一位姓曾的先生，他是余来定（Yui Lei Ding）的代表，并约定第二天，即1939年3月23日下午4时再次会面，详细讨论此事。李告诉我，看来一切都很顺利，从此我们可以在新新屋顶花园（Sun Sun Roof Garden）见面。我完全没有怀疑他，随他回到科泰旅馆，我们在那里退掉了房间。然而，我多次去新新屋顶花园，却找不到李广英和曹祖宗的踪迹。不久，我得知李广英和曹祖宗已成功从受害者那里勒索到一大笔钱，并将每一分钱都私吞了。我急于找到他们，所以我每天都去屋顶花园，1939年3月28日，当我再次寻找这两人时，被警察逮捕。以上属实。

体貌特征描述：
1) 李广英（LEE KWONG YING）；年龄23/4岁，徐州人，身高5英尺3/4英寸，长脸面色蜡黄，头发向后梳，讲上海话，穿西装，戴棕色毡帽。
2) 李达梅（LEE DAH MEI）：年龄23/4岁，河南人，身高5英尺5/8英寸，中等身材，长脸面色黝黑，头发向后梳，讲上海话，穿蓝布长衫，戴灰色毡帽。

签署人等：ZUNG VHE SING。

pages.en:
LEE KWONG YING (        ), 21, M/Unemployed,
residing at 33 Route Remi, F/C,
Anhwei                                // D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung,
C.1           3. 4. 39                      Yao Dinsin.

At 8 p.m. 22.3.39, when visiting the Sun Sun Roof
Garden, I happened to encounter Lee Dah Mei, a bosom friend
of mine, who invited me to his room in the Poh Tai Lodging
House in Frenchtown, saying that he had something to discuss
with me. On arrival, I noticed Tsang Tsao Zung already in
the room, and in a short while, Zung Vee Sing also arrived.
Zung proposed that plans be made to extort money from one,
Lai Ding, under the names of patriotic organisations. We all
agreed to his proposal and decided that threatening letter be
prepared and delivered to the intended victim by Zung Vee Sing
and Tsang Tsao Zung at 7 a.m. the following morning.

On the next morning, however, Tsang Tsao Zung all of
a sudden had a severe stomach ache and was unable to go with
Zung Vee Sing to deliver the letter. Through the suggestion
of Lee Dah Mei and Zung Vee Sing, I was selected to take
Tsang's place and go with Zung to deliver the letter. I did
not object, and at the appointed time, Zung Vee Sing and I
set out toward our destination, Zung handing me a letter,
which I placed in my pocket. On arrival at the intended
victim's house, situated in Bing Wo Li, Avenue Road, Zung
remained outside, whilst I alone gained admittance into the
house, where I was received by one Mr.Tsang, a representative
of Yui Lai Ding, who appointed me to meet again the next day.
I came out and informed Zung of the foregoing, after which
both returned to the lodging house I went to bed and got up
the next day
at 1 p.m./when Tsang Tsao Zung accompanied me to a restaurant
for
on Shantung Road/Tiffin. There we discussed the matter :
pages.zh:
李广英（LEE KWONG YING）(        )，21岁，男性/无业，
居住于法租界雷米路（Route Remi）33号，
安徽                                // D.S.I. 宋平宗 (Soong Ping Tsung),
C.1           1939年4月3日                      姚丁新 (Yao Dinsin).

1939年3月22日晚上8点，当我在新新屋顶花园时，偶然遇到了我的挚友李达梅，他邀请我去法租界博泰旅馆（Poh Tai Lodging House）他的房间，说有事与我商量。到达后，我注意到曹祖宗（Tsang Tsao Zung）已经在房间里，过了一会儿，钟伟成（Zung Vee Sing）也到了。钟提议计划以爱国组织的名义向一名叫来定（Lai Ding）的人勒索钱财。我们都同意他的提议，并决定准备一封恐吓信，由钟伟成和曹祖宗于次日早上7点投递给预定受害者。

然而，第二天早上，曹祖宗突然严重腹痛，无法与钟伟成一起去送信。在李达梅和钟伟成的建议下，我被选中代替曹，与钟一起去送信。我没有反对，在约定时间，钟伟成和我出发前往目的地，钟递给我一封信，我把它放在口袋里。到达位于大西路炳武里的预定受害者家中时，钟留在外面，而我独自进入屋内，接待我的是余来定的一位代表曾先生，他约定第二天再次见面。我出来告知钟上述情况，之后两人都回到了旅馆。我上床睡觉，第二天
下午1点起床/当时曹祖宗陪我去一家餐馆
在山东路/吃午饭。在那里我们讨论了此事：

pages.en:
- 2 -

After tiffin, Tseng Tsoo Zung telephoned to Yui Lai Ding's
house, reminding them of the appointment that day, and was
told to go to Yui's house immediately. At once, Tseng and I
proceeded to Yui's home, where on arrival, Tseng remained
outside, whilst I entered the premises again myself. I was
received by one Mr.Tsang and another Mr.Wong, who suggested
going to the China Hotel for a lengthy discussion. We agreed
to this, and after hiring 4 rickshas, we all proceeded to the
above mentioned hotel, where in a room on the 3rd.floor, we
finally agreed to settle this case on payment of $400.00.They
paid us immediately, and after receiving this money, Tsang
and I proceeded to the lodging house to inform Zung Vee Sing
of the foregoing. On our way, however, we happened to meet
Zung Vee Sing, who had left the lodging house looking for us.
Then, instead of going further, the three of us went to the
Sun Sun Billiard Room, where the money was handed to Zung Vee
Sing for distribution. Zung gave Tsang and myself each $45,
keeping the balance (over $300) himself, after which, we
separated.

On the next day, when visiting the Gt.Eastern Tea Room,
I happened to meet Mr.Tsang the representative of Yui Lai Ding
who enquired if I had received a slice of the $400; and I replied
that I had been allotted $45.00. Tsang voluntarily gave me
$7.00 on that occasion. With the $45 plus the $7, I redeemed
a gold finger ring from a pawnshop (pawned for $48.00).

Several days later, in the Sun Sun Roof Garden, I met
Zung Vee Sing, who accused me that I had received $2000.00
pages.zh:
- 2 -

午饭后，曾祖宗（Tseng Tsoo Zung）打电话到俞来定（Yui Lai Ding）家中，提醒他们当天的约会，并被告知立即前往俞家。随即，曾和我一同前往俞家。到达后，曾留在外面，而我再次独自进入屋内。我受到一名姓张（Tsang）先生和另一名姓黄（Wong）先生的接待，他们建议去中国饭店（China Hotel）进行长时间商谈。我们同意了这一建议，雇了四辆人力车后，大家一同前往上述饭店。在三楼的一个房间里，我们最终同意以支付400.00美元来了结此案。他们立即付了款，收到这笔钱后，张和我前往寄宿处告知宗维成（Zung Vee Sing）上述情况。然而，在路上我们碰巧遇到了宗维成，他正离开寄宿处寻找我们。于是，我们三人没有继续前行，而是去了新新台球室（Sun Sun Billiard Room），在那里将钱交给宗维成分配。宗给了张和我各45美元，自己留下了余额（超过300美元），随后我们分头离开。

次日，当我造访大东茶室（Gt.Eastern Tea Room）时，碰巧遇到了俞来定的代表张先生，他询问我是否分得了那400美元中的一份；我回答说我分得了45.00美元。当时，张自愿又给了我7.00美元。用这45美元加上7美元，我从当铺赎回了金戒指一枚（典当价为48.00美元）。

几天后，在新新屋顶花园（Sun Sun Roof Garden），我遇到了宗维成，他指责我收到的不是400.00美元，而是2000.00美元

pages.en:
- 3 -

instead of $400.00, insisting that I should engage a room to
talk it over. I was indignant over this accusation, and at
once engaged Room 2C2 Dah Wo Loiging House, where Zung and
four others arrived. In their presence, I produced 3 banknotes
and one gold ring which I had redeemed from a pawnshop. However
they still insisted that I should hand over to them the balance
of the alleged $2000.00, threatening that they would kill me
if I failed to comply. They left and were never seen again.
I was arrested on 1.4.39. The above is the truth.

Signed etc. by : LEE KWONG YING.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

并坚持要我开一个房间详谈。我对这一指控感到愤怒，随即在大华旅馆（Dah Wo Loiging House）开了2C2号房间，宗和其他四人随后到达。在他们面前，我出示了三张钞票和我从当铺赎回的一枚金戒指。然而，他们仍坚持要我交出所谓2000.00美元的余额，并威胁说如果我不照办就杀死我。他们离开后就再也没有出现过。我于1939年4月1日被捕。以上所述属实。

签署人等：李广英（LEE KWONG YING）。

pages.en:
TSANG TSOO MING (        ), 28, M/unemployed,
residing 1 Su Tuh Faung, Avenue Haig, French Concession.
Chakiang,           -- D.S.I. Soong Ping Tsung,

C.1                 30. 3. 39             Clerk Yao Dinsin.

    On or about 25.3.39, when I was in Room 314, Nying
Saung Lodging House, engaged by my friend, Lee Vung Ziang, I
was given a letter by Lee Dah Mei, who visited the room and
whispered to me to the effect that the said letter should be
delivered to Mr. Yui Lai Ding of House 15, Bing Hoo Li, Avenue
Road. Consequently, Lee and myself proceeded to the above
address to deliver the letter. On arrival, Lee stayed outside,
whilst I alone gained admittance into the house and interviewed
Mr. Yui Lai Ding in person. During the conversation, I found
that Mr. Yui was a man of sober disposition, who asked me many
a question regarding the purpose of this visit. I dare not
deliver the letter to him at that time and left him. After
leaving the house, Lee Dah Mei and I proceeded to the "Jung S
Dai" Tea shop, near Sinza Road, to discuss further plans for
the matter. As no decision could be reached at that forenoon,
Lee and I appointed to meet each other in the Koh Tai Lodging
House for further discussions at 10 p.m. same day.
    At the appointed time, on my arrival in the Koh Tai
Lodging House, there were about 6 or 7 men already present, i.e.
Lee Kwong Ying, Zung Vi Sung, Li Dah Mei, Yang Tsoh Ping and
three others whose names I do not know and friends of Lee Kwong
Ying. After a lengthy discussion, we decided to extort money
from various wealthy men under the pretext that we were members
of a patriotic society. Finally, Lee Kwong Ying, Lee Dah Mei
and myself were selected to handle the matter, and that we
were going to extort $5,000.00 from Yui Lai Ding, by falsely
accusing him of being concerned in traitorous activities and
pages.zh:
唐祖宗（TSANG TSOO MING）（音译），28岁，男/无业，
住址：法租界霞飞路（Avenue Haig）苏德坊（Su Tuh Faung）1号。
浙江籍，           -- 巡官宋秉忠（Soong Ping Tsung），

C.1                 1939年3月30日             书记员姚丁辛（Yao Dinsin）。

    大约在1939年3月25日，当我在朋友李永祥（Lee Vung Ziang）包下的宁松寄宿处（Nying Saung Lodging House）314号房间时，李大美（Lee Dah Mei）来访该房间，递给我一封信，并低声对我说，这封信应送至爱文义路（Avenue Road）宾胡里（Bing Hoo Li）15号的俞来定先生。因此，李和我一同前往上述地址送信。到达后，李留在外面，而我独自进入屋内并亲自会见了俞来定先生。在谈话中，我发现俞先生是一个举止稳重的人，他就此次来访的目的问了我许多问题。我当时不敢把信交给他，便离开了他。离开那所房子后，李大美和我前往新闸路（Sinza Road）附近的“众士大”（Jung S Dai）茶馆，进一步商讨此事的计划。由于那天上午未能达成决定，李和我约定当晚10点在科泰寄宿处（Koh Tai Lodging House）见面，作进一步讨论。
    在约定时间，当我到达科泰寄宿处时，那里已经有大约六七个人在场，即李广英（Lee Kwong Ying）、宗维成（Zung Vi Sung）、李大美（Li Dah Mei）、杨佐平（Yang Tsoh Ping）以及另外三个我不知道名字的人，他们是李广英的朋友。经过长时间讨论，我们决定以爱国团体成员为借口，向多位富商勒索钱财。最后，选定由李广英、李大美和我来处理此事，我们将通过诬陷俞来定参与叛国活动，

pages.en:
- 2 -

that he had sold a consignment of copper and iron to the
Japanese, saying that the $5,000.00 would be a fine imposed
upon him by this patriotic society. Besides, Yui should also
write a letter repenting his wrongful acts. Both the letter
and the chop thereon, were made ready by Lee Dah Mei, which
was delivered to Yui Lai Ding on the following morning by Lee
Kwong Ying and Sung Vi Sung. During the delivery, however, Yui
Lai Ding appointed the above mentioned two messengers to meet
at his house again at 5 or 6 p.m. same date, to talk it over.
Prior to the appointed time, Lee Kwong Ying asked me
to visit the Sun Sun Billiard Room, where I was to warn the
occupants of the Yui House that the two representatives of the
patriotic society were on their way to the house, and at the
same time, Lee Kwong Ying and myself set out toward our desti-
nation (Yui's home).
On arrival, we were received by the representatives,
who appeared to be quite sincere in their manners, one named
Wong and the other named Sung, who subsequently, appointed us
to talk it over somewhere else, preferably the China Hotel. We
approved of their suggestion and proceeded to a room on the 3rd
floor of the China Hotel, where, on the arrival of their two
representatives, negotiations were carried on, we demanding a
minimum of $500.00 in settlement of the case. Finally, the sum
was reduced to $ 450.00, which was paid to Lee. Lee and I then
proceeded to the billiard room together, and, on arrival, Lee
gave me $45.00. Several days later, I telephoned Yui's house
and enquired if Lee had been there, and was told in the affirmative
pages.zh:
- 2 -

并将一批铜铁卖给日本人，以此向他勒索5,000.00美元，声称这5,000.00美元是该爱国团体对他 imposed 的罚款。此外，俞还应写一封悔过书，承认其错误行为。信件及其上的印章均由李大美准备好，并于次日上午由李广英和宋维成（Sung Vi Sung）送达俞来定。然而在送达过程中，俞来定指定上述两名信使于同日傍晚5点或6点再到他家面谈。
    在约定时间之前，李广英让我去新新台球室（Sun Sun Billiard Room），我要去警告俞家的人，爱国团体的两名代表正在前往该处的路上，同时，李广英和我出发前往我们的目的地（俞家）。
    到达后，我们受到了代表的接待，他们的态度显得相当诚恳，一人姓黄（Wong），另一人姓宋（Sung），随后，他们指定我们去别处商谈，最好是中国饭店。我们赞同他们的建议，前往中国饭店三楼的一个房间，待他们的两名代表到达后，谈判开始，我们要价最低500.00美元以了结此案。最后，金额减至450.00美元，支付给了李。随后李和我一同前往台球室，到达后，李给了我45.00美元。几天后，我打电话到俞家，询问李是否去过那里，得到的答复是肯定的

pages.en:
- 3 -

In addition, the man who answered the telephone, asked me to
proceed to 625 Szechuen Road - one auction hong, to see one Mr.
Tsang for further particulars. When I went there, Mr. Tsang
informed me that Lee had received from him a further sum of
$70.00. At the same time, Mr.Tsang presented me with $100.00,
a part of which has now been seized by the Police, the balance
being spent in buying clothes, spectacles and wrist watch etc.
This is the truth.

SIGNED : TANG TOO ZUNG.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

此外，接电话的人还让我去四川路625号的一家拍卖行，见一位张先生以了解详情。当我去那里时，张先生告诉我，李从他那里又收到了70.00美元。同时，张先生给了我100.00美元，其中一部分现已被警方扣押，其余部分用于购买衣服、眼镜和手表等。以上属实。

签署人：唐祖宗（TANG TOO ZUNG）。

pages.en:
LING TS KYUIN ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ) & CHING HSING ( 〔此处转录不清〕 )

Yao Dinsin.

Regarding the case of extortion, we hereby report as follows :
THE FIRST OCCASION :
It occurred at about 5:30 p.m. 30.3.39, when one named
Lee Kwong Ying, claiming to be the captain of a guerilla unit,
telephoned to Ling Ts Kyuin to the effect that he (Lee Kwong
Ying) in the name of his unit of some 52 men, who had been left
behind in Shanghai, was in urgent need of some funds to enable
them to travel to the rear of Kiukiang for participation in
guerilla activities. During the telephone conversation, Lee
Kwong Ying demanded the payment of $300.00 as travelling fees,
threatening that in the case of non-payment, drastic measures
would be adopted against us. Finally, Lee appointed us to
meet him at the entrance of the Great Eastern Tea Room, Kiukiar
Road, at 5:30 - 6:00 p.m. on the morrow, for detailed discussion
THE SECOND OCCASION :
At about 3 p.m. 31.3.39, the next day, an anonymous
telephone message was received, reminding us of the appointment
at 5 p.m. and stating that we should be present by all means.
At the appointed time, I (Ching Hsing) proceeded to the Great
Eastern Tea Room and awaited at the entrance for about 15 minutes
Soon, I noticed, standing in front of the Dah Woo Dai Chinese
Theatre, just opposite the Great Eastern Tea Room, two Chinese,
one in foreign clothes (wearing a grey felt hat and a pair of
hexagonal horn-rimmed spectacles), and the other in blue cotton
jacket and pants, usually worn by men of the coolie class. I
began to pay attention to these two men, who by that time,
seemed to have noticed me as well. They came forward and

凌子权（LING TS KYUIN）（〔此处转录不清〕）及 程兴（CHING HSING）（〔此处转录不清〕）

姚丁辛（Yao Dinsin）。

关于勒索案，兹报告如下：
第一次：
发生在1939年3月30日下午5:30左右，一名叫李广英的人自称是游击队队长，打电话给凌子权，称他（李广英）代表其滞留在上海的约52人的部队，急需一些资金以便他们前往九江后方参加游击活动。在电话交谈中，李广英要求支付300.00美元作为旅费，并威胁说如果不付款，将对我们采取严厉措施。最后，李约定我们于次日下午5:30至6:00在九江路（Kiukiar Road）大东茶室门口见面，进行详细讨论
第二次：
次日（3月31日）下午3点左右，接到一个匿名电话，提醒我们下午5点的约会，并称我们必须务必到场。在约定时间，我（程兴）前往大东茶室，在门口等候了约15分钟。很快，我注意到在大东茶室正对面的大舞台（Dah Woo Dai Chinese Theatre）前站着两个中国人，一个穿西装（戴着灰色毡帽和一副六角形玳瑁框眼镜），另一个穿着通常由苦力阶层男子穿的蓝色棉布夹克和裤子。我开始注意这两个人，此时他们似乎也注意到了我。他们走上前来，
