- 2 -

asked me if my name was Ling. I replied that my name was
Ching, and that I had been detailed by Mr. Ling to attend
the appointment on his behalf. The three of us then entered
the Tea Room, and after selecting a suitable table, we all
sat down and discussed the matter at length. During the
interview, they warned me from time to time not to report
the case to either the S.M.Police or the Japanese military
Police, saying that we would lose our lives in case we did so.
They informed me that there were approx. 1000 guerillas in and
around the Western District of Shanghai and that the squad of
58 men which they commanded was only a small unit which
functioned under the same leader. In support of this, the
man in foreign clothes produced from his sock a visiting card
on which was printed the characters, " Captain - Fourth Regiment
Guerilla Troops of Yangtse Valley".

Despite the late hours, no definite results were
obtained. The interview came to an end when I suggested
that we should meet again some other time, promising that I
would raise the fund in the meanwhile. He insisted that the
matter must be concluded not later than the next day, and
to
after appointing me/meet again at the same place at 10:30 a.m.
to 11:00 a.m. on the morrow, we left the tea room and parted,
each hiring a ricksha, and they disappeared in a westerly
direction.

THE THIRD OCCASION :

At about 9 a.m. the next morning (1.4.39), Lee Kwong
Ying telephoned to me, reminding me of the interview at 10 a.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

问我是否姓凌。我回答说我姓程，是受凌先生委派代为赴约。随后我们三人进入茶室，选了一张合适的桌子坐下，并对此事进行了 lengthy 讨论。在会谈期间，他们不时警告我不要向工部局警务处（S.M.Police）或日本宪兵队报案，说如果我们这样做就会丧命。他们告诉我，在上海西区及其周边约有1000名游击队员，而他们指挥的58人小队只是同一领导人下属的一个小单位。为了证明这一点，那个穿西装的人从袜子里掏出一张名片，上面印着“长江流域游击队第四团团长”字样。

尽管时间已晚，但未取得确切结果。当我建议改日再会，并承诺在此期间筹集资金时，会谈结束。他坚持此事必须在次日之前解决，并
约定次日（明天）上午10:30至11:00在同一地点再次会面后，我们离开茶室并分手，各自雇了一辆人力车，他们向西方向消失。

第三次：

次日（1939年4月1日）上午9点左右，李广英打电话给我，提醒我上午10点

pages.en:
- 3 -

to 11 a.m. that forenoon and saying that the money must be
paid in full that day. I then set out from my office and
proceeded to the Great Eastern Tea Room, where after waiting
for about 15 minutes, Lee Kwong Ying alone appeared. As he
demanded payment, I handed over to him $42.00 which I had on
my person. After counting it, he placed the money in his
pocket, saying that the balance of $258.00 should be paid in
full at the earliest possible opportunity. At this moment,
the police party arrived. Lee made an attempt to leave, but
was unsuccessful. He was placed under arrest and was escorted
away by the police party.

On all occasions when we met, he always talked about
guerillas in the Western District of Shanghai, where, he
alleged to have a total of about 10000 men. I was made to
pay the money under constant threats. Lee Kwong Ying also
told me that the officer commanding the 1000 guerillas in and
around Shanghai, was one, named LEE TS KING. This is the
truth.

Signed and chopped by :
LING TS KYUIN.
CHING HAINO.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

至11点的会面，并称当天必须付清全款。于是我离开办公室，前往大东茶室，在等了约15分钟后，只有李广英一人出现。当他要求付款时，我将身上带的42.00美元交给了他。他数过钱后，把钱放进口袋，说剩余的258.00美元应尽快全额支付。此时，警察小组到达。李试图离开，但未成功。他被逮捕并由警察小组押走。

在我们每次见面时，他总是谈论上海西区的游击队，据称那里共有约10000人。我是在不断的威胁下被迫付款的。李广英还告诉我，指挥上海及周边1000名游击队的军官名叫李泽金（LEE TS KING）。以上属实。

签署并盖章：
凌子权（LING TS KYUIN）。
程海诺（CHING HAINO）。

pages.en:
Lee Kwang Ying (李廣印)
Anhwei
C.).3. 172
O.B.E.Q. C.1 3.4.39 translated Clerk Hsia
//////

My name is Lee Kwang Ying (李廣印), age 21, native
of Anhwei, married, unemployed, residing at 35 Rue Remi,
French Concession.

At about 12 noon on the 31st. March, 1939, Lee Dah Mai
(李大美) (in custody) returned, I asked him where he
came from. I was told by him that he had gone to Hongkew
for the purpose of selling five coloured "Reformed Govern-
ment" flags on behalf of one named Ling (林) of the
Foh Hyi & Co. (福義公司), The Bund, near Canton Road.
I then told him that Lee was a traitor, and we may extort
some money from him. He agreed with my suggestion and told
me that Ling's office telephone number 18212 referring me to
ask for a loan by telephone. At about 5 p.m. on the same
day, I had dinner at the Ong Kwang Lor (興光樓) Restaur-
Hupeh Road, I rung up Ling (name unknown) I told him that I
was a chief of a guerilla units named Lee Kwang Ying with
an intention to leave Shanghai but in short of money. On
the understanding that he was working with Japanese in a
good financial condition, so requested him to negotiate with
me between 10.30 a.m. and 11 a.m. the following day at the
Dah Tung Tea Room (大東茶室). On arrival at the
above mentioned tea room I met one named Kying (name
forgotten), a representative of Ling, whom I negotiated
and I demanded for $300.00. When Kying (金) gave me
$24.00 and promised me to pay the remainder of $276.00
at about 10.30 a.m. 1.4.39 at the same place. After our
conversation, a party of S.M.Police together with members
pages.zh:
李广英（Lee Kwang Ying）（李廣印）
安徽籍
C.).3. 172
O.B.E.Q. C.1 1939年4月3日 翻译员 夏（Hsia）
//////

我叫李广英（李廣印），21岁，安徽籍，已婚，无业，住址：法租界雷米路（Rue Remi）35号。

1939年3月31日中午12点左右，李大美（李大美）（在押）回来，我问他从哪里来。他告诉我，他代表外滩广东路附近的福义公司（Foh Hyi & Co.）的一位姓林（Ling）的人，去虹口出售五面彩色的“维新政府”旗帜。于是我告诉他，林是个汉奸，我们可以向他勒索一些钱。他同意我的建议，并告诉我林的办公室电话号码是18212，让我打电话去借款。当天下午5点左右，我在湖北路的兴光楼（Ong Kwang Lor）餐馆吃晚饭，我打电话给林（名字不详），告诉他我是名叫李广英的游击队队长，打算离开上海但缺钱。鉴于他为日本人工作且经济状况良好，我要求他于次日上午10:30至11:00在大东茶室（Dah Tung Tea Room）与我洽谈。到达上述茶室后，我遇到了一位姓金（Kying）（名字忘了）的人，他是林的代表，我与他在谈判中要求300.00美元。当金（Kying）（金）给了我24.00美元，并承诺于1939年4月1日上午10:30左右在同一地点支付剩余的276.00美元。谈话结束后，一队工部局警察会同成员

pages.en:
(2)

of the Japanese Military Police in plain cloth came in and
took me into custody. Later, I led them to effect the arrest
of one named Lee Jai Kai.
This is a truth.

Signed:- Lee Kwang Ying
pages.zh:
(2)

几名便衣日本宪兵进来，将我逮捕。随后，我带领他们去逮捕了一名名叫李载凯（Lee Jai Kai）的人。
此乃实情。

签署：- 李广英（Lee Kwang Ying）

pages.en:
Lee Dai Mai ( 〔此处转录不清〕 )
Honan                                U.S.I. Soong
C.B.H.Q. C.l        4/4/39           translated  Clerk Hsia
                                     ////////

My name is Lee Dai Mai, age 27, native of Honan. My
wife is in my native place. I came to Shanghai in the year
of 1935 (24th. Year of the Republic of China) and assisted
my cousin named Lee Dah Ching ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ) in a cake shop
situated at Newchang Road. About one year later, I raised
some money from my cousin and started a business myself at
No.802 Tongshan Road. Owing to the Sino-Japanese hostilities
I removed from the above mentioned address to No.63 Rue
Remi, French Concession to continue the business. When I
was in No.802 Tongshan Road I became acquainted with one of
my tenants Lee Yoong Chong's (watchman) son named Lee Kwang
Ying ( 李 〔此处转录不清〕 ). Since I removed to the No.63 Rue Remi,
French Concession, he assisted me in my shop. In May or
June, 1938, he left me and I did not know anything about
his activities.

During the month of June or July, 1938, one named Zung
Vee Sing frequently purchased cakes from me and therefore
became acquainted with him. I knew him that he was an
ex-policeman in Nantao through our conversation.

At about 20th. day, 1st. Moon (March, 1939) Zung came
to me and produced a letter, which I could not read, so he
explained that this was a threatening letter addressed to
a certain shop relating their business to collect waste brass
or iron and supplied same to the Japanese Authorities,
whereupon the shop owner gained a good profit on it, so we
may threaten him (proprietor) to obtain some money. I agreed
with his suggestion. A few days later, Zung visited me
pages.zh:
李大梅（Lee Dai Mai）（〔此处转录不清〕）
河南                                U.S.I. 宋
刑务总部 C.l        1939年4月4日   翻译员 夏职员
                                     ////////

我叫李大梅，27岁，河南人。我的妻子在老家。我于1935年（民国二十四年）来到上海，在新昌路的一家糕点店协助我的表亲李大清（Lee Dah Ching）（〔此处转录不清〕）。大约一年后，我从表亲那里筹得一些资金，自己在同山路802号开始做生意。由于中日战事，我从上述地址搬至法租界雷米路63号继续经营。当我住在同山路802号时，我结识了我的房客李永忠（看门人）的儿子李广英（李〔此处转录不清〕）。自从我搬到法租界雷米路63号后，他在我的店里帮我忙。1938年5月或6月，他离开了我，我不再知晓他的任何活动。

在1938年6月或7月间，一名叫曾维新（Zung Vee Sing）的人经常向我购买糕点，因此与他相识。通过交谈，我得知他是南市的一名前警察。

大约在1939年3月（农历正月初二十日左右），曾某来找我，拿出一封信，我看不懂，于是他解释说，这是一封写给某家从事收集废铜铁并供应给日本当局、从而从中获利的商店的恐吓信，因此我们可以威胁店主以获取一些钱财。我同意了他的建议。几天后，曾某来访

pages.en:
(2)

whilst I just left the premises, when I told him that I
would go to the Room 314 Ning Song (寧商) Lodging House
to play Mah Jong. The room was hired by one of my fellow
countrymen named Kao Tsung Yee. On arrival I saw Lee Kwang
Ying (李廣英), Kao Tsung Yee (高宗義), and one other
known as Tsang Tsoo Zung through the introduction of Kao.
In turn I introduced Tsang to Zung Vee Sing. Hereafter,
we, Lee Kwang Ying, Tsang Tsoo Zung, Zung Vee Sing and
myself played Mah Jong in room every day.
Several days later, Zung came to my shop and told me
that he had talked to Tsang Tsoo Zung relating to the
threatening letter. Tsang also agreed with our suggestion
and we could fulfill our plan. I hoped it would be succeeded
in an early date to get the money. After, they never visited
me in any time and I did not receive a single cash from them.
This is a truth.

Signed:- Lee Dah Mai
pages.zh:
(2)

当时我刚离开店铺，我告诉他我要去宁商旅馆314房间打麻将。该房间是由我的同乡高宗义（Kao Tsung Yee）租下的。到达后，我见到了李广英（李廣英）、高宗义（高宗義），以及经高介绍认识的另一个人曹祖宗（Tsang Tsoo Zung）。随后我将曹介绍给曾维新。此后，我们四人——李广英、曹祖宗、曾维新和我——每天都在房间里打麻将。
几天后，曾某来到我的店里，告诉我他已经就恐吓信一事与曹祖宗谈过。曹也同意了我们的建议，我们可以实施计划。我希望早日成功拿到钱。之后，他们再也没有来找过我，我也没有从他们那里收到一分钱。
此乃实情。

签署：- 李大梅

D. C. (Special Branch).

P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)
R. D. U. RT 80
CRIME BRANCH
APRIL 2,
39.

C.1. I.C.M.
58/39.

ENQUIRIES RE EXTORTION AND INTIMIDATION.
and assistance to Japanese Gendarmerie

On the forenoon of 1.4.39, J.D.C. Yamahar attached
to C.1, reported that Sgt. Major Hikiji of the
Japanese Gendarmerie H.Q. Bridge House, requested
the assistance of the S.M.P. to arrest a certain
Chinese at about 10 a.m. even date, at a certain
place near the intersection of Kiukiang and Chekiang
Roads.

Enquiries previous to the assistance being
given elicited that the Gendarmerie had received
certain information that a male Chinese named
LEE KUANG YING (李廣印) was meeting an informer
of the Gendarmerie in the Tea Room on the 1st floor
of the Wing On (永安) Co. Building, No. 30 Kin Wo
Ka to discuss certain business regarding the extort-
ing of money from a Chinese employed by the Mitsue
Bussan Kaisha Ltd. 185 Szechuen Road.

From this information, it was obvious to
the undersigned that the man they wished to arrest
was the person whose name card was left at the home
of Yue Lien Zien (俞廉臣), No. 15, Lane 239,
Avenue Road, when the 1st accused went to that
address to extort money from the inmate, and in
pages.zh:
副督察（特科）。

致副督察（特科）助理
R. D. U. RT 80
刑事处
4月2日，
1939年。

C.1. I.C.M.
58/39.

关于敲诈勒索和恐吓的调查。
及协助日本宪兵队

1939年4月1日上午，隶属C.1的日本侦探山原（Yamahar）报告称，日本宪兵队总部（百老汇大厦）的警长Hikiji请求工部局警务处协助，于当日上午10点左右，在九江路与浙江路路口附近的某地逮捕一名中国人。

在提供协助之前进行的调查表明，宪兵队收到情报，称一名名叫李广印（LEE KUANG YING，李廣印）的中国男子正在九江路30号永安公司大楼一楼的茶室与宪兵队的一名线人会面，讨论有关向受雇于四川路185号三井物产株式会社（Mitsue Bussan Kaisha Ltd.）的一名中国员工敲诈钱财的事宜。

根据这一情报，下文签署人显然看出，他们想要逮捕的人，就是第一名被告前往俞廉臣（Yue Lien Zien，俞廉臣）住所（爱多亚路239弄15号）向住户敲诈钱财时留下名片的那个人，并且与此

pages.en:
2/2.

connection with which four arrests had been made
by C.I. detectives.
The subsequent arrest of ....... YING (李原印),
21, Anhwei, unemployed, N.S.A., in the Sing On
Tea Room at 10.55 a.m. same date, proved that he
was the person mentioned in diary one, page 2,
paragraph 4 as being one of the gang which had
visited the complainant's home.
In his possession were found 3 name cards similar
to the one left in the home of the complainant and
he freely admitted that he was concerned in the
extortion. On the name cards he claimed to be
a guerilla leader.
An identification parade was held at C.D.H.Q.
and Lee Sang Ying, the 5th accused, identified
the 1st and 3rd accused as accomplices.
He was then questioned and stated that there
was a chance of arresting one more accomplice at
311 Rue du Seikwei, French Concession.
Assistance was then obtained from the French
Police and at about 12.15 p.m. same date the stated
address was visited and two male Chinese were identified
by the 5th accused and arrested. Nothing incriminating
was found either on the persons of the two men or
in their residence but An Lakwei, Lee Dah Mai
pages.zh:
2/2.

案相关，刑务处侦探已实施了四次逮捕。
随后，在同日上午10点55分，在兴亚茶室逮捕了____英（李原印），21岁，安徽人，无业，南市区协会成员，这证实了他就是日记一第2页第4段中提到的曾到访投诉人家中的团伙成员之一。
在他身上发现了3张与留在投诉人家中的那张相似的名片，他坦率承认参与了敲诈。在名片上，他自称是游击队队长。
在刑务处总部进行了列队辨认，第五名被告李尚英（Lee Sang Ying）指认第一名和第三名被告为同伙。
随后对他进行了讯问，他表示有机会在法租界西格威路311号再逮捕一名同伙。
随后获得了法国警察的协助，并于当日下午12点15分左右前往上述地址，第五名被告指认了两名中国男子并将其逮捕。在这两人身上或其住所内均未发现任何罪证，但安拉克伟（An Lakwei）、李大梅

pages.en:
2/3.

李大彝, Honan, Unemployed, 63 Route Remi,
admitted that he had participated in an extortion
case with the 5th accused, whereupon he and Lee
To Hung (李道恒), 30, Honan, Unemployed, 311
Rue de Meikwei, were handed over to the C.I.D.
after they were finger printed.

The 5th accused stated that he had no fixed
abode and he led detectives to Room 13 of the
Han Dong Tsoong (      ) Lodging House, 12 Yue
Tuh Li off Yunnan Road, where he had slept on the
night of 31.3.39 . It was found that the room
had been engaged by Lee Deh Hai, 6th accused and the
two persons had occupied it for one night only and
nothing incriminating was found.

All seven of the arrested men are detained in
Central Station whilst further enquiries are being
made into their activities and the Japanese Gen-
darmerie have intimated that they would like to
be represented when the accused were being questioned.

The 5th accused admitted that the meeting place
for the gang was in the Sun Sun Roof Garden and that
he was not aware of the arrest of the other members
of the gang or he would have gone into hiding.

C.I. detectives have been held up in their
pages.zh:
2/3.

李大彝，河南人，无业，住雷米路63号，
承认他与第五名被告一起参与了一起敲诈案，于是他和李道恒（Lee To Hung），30岁，河南人，无业，住梅格威路311号，在按捺指纹后被移交给刑务处。

第五名被告称他没有固定住所，并带领侦探前往云南路月德里12号汉东松（Han Dong Tsoong）（      ）旅馆的13号房间，他在1939年3月31日晚曾在此过夜。经查，该房间由第六名被告李德海（Lee Deh Hai）租用，两人仅占用了一晚，未发现任何罪证。

所有七名被捕男子均被拘留在中央巡捕房，同时对其活动进行进一步调查，日本宪兵队表示希望在讯问被告时派代表在场。

第五名被告承认，该团伙的聚会地点是新新屋顶花园，并称他不知道其他团伙成员已被捕，否则他早就躲起来了。

ENQUIRIES RE EXTORTION AND INTIMIDATION.

Acting on the information of D.S.I. Soong Ping Sung
detectives attached to C.B.H.Q., arrested two male
Chinese in the Sun Sun Roof of Garden, Kweichow Road,
at 4.40p.m. 27.3.39 as they were suspected burglars.

been concerned in burglaries but they insisted that

On being interrogated the 1st accused stated
that he was a member of the 4th Section, 3rd Battalion

About one week ago the 1st accused together

Yue Lien Zien (俞蓮亭), No. 15, Lane 239, Avenue

关于敲诈勒索和恐吓的调查。

根据刑务总部侦探宋平松（Soong Ping Sung）提供的信息，侦探于1939年3月27日下午4点40分在贵州路新新屋顶花园逮捕了两名中国男子，因涉嫌入室盗窃。

两人被带至刑务总部，就其活动进行调查，他们否认参与入室盗窃，但坚称他们是活跃于浦东和上海西区的游击队成员。

ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE CONSULAR

协助日本领事警察寻找在大场附近一名日本国民被杀案中的证人。（未实施逮捕）。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
APR 1 1 1939
07752

Japanese Slain by
Chinese Bandits

Truck Held Up By Three
Men Near Tazang; Gunmen
Escape Pursuing Party

Dragged from a truck in which he
was riding with two others, Mr.
Seizo Iwau, 41-year old Japanese pro-
prietor of the Santo Yoko, a building
materials contractor, was the victim
of an attack by three Chinese armed
bandits near Tazang, close to Shang-
hai, at 9.30 o'clock on Sunday morn-
ing, the Japanese press reported
yesterday. Carried to the Foomin
hospital in an unconscious condition,
he succumbed to his wounds a short
time later.

On his way from Tazang to Lotien-
chien, west of Paoshan, to purchase
some iron plates, Mr. Iwau, accom-
panied by a Mr. Chang, a Chinese
iron broker, and a truck driver, ap-
proached a bridge spanning a creek
two kilometres from Tazung, when
three Chinese, emerging from beneath
the bridge, halted the truck at the
point of pistols, the reports said.

Pulling the victim from the truck
and routing his two terrified com-
panions, one of the armed men fired
a shot at the Japanese, the bullet
entering the right side of his back
and emerging near his right breast,
according to the papers. Another
terrorist fractured the victim's head
with a blow to the right side of his
head with a heavy iron weapon.

Another Party Arrives

Following the attack, the Chinese
remained on the scene of the crime,
apparently waiting to victimize an-
other Japanese, it was reported, when
two Japanese in the employ of the
Daido Kumi, a contracting firm,
accompanied by several Japanese
soldiers attached to a telegraph unit,
approached the scene. Noting their
approach, the Chinese fled, pursued
by the Japanese, who fired ten shots
in the chase. The bandits, however,
made good their escape.

The Japanese notified the Tazang
defence headquarters, which imme-
diately dispatched some troops to
conduct a search for the escaped
Chinese. The victim was rushed to
the Foomin hospital but he died from
his wounds shortly after noon. Police-
men of the Japanese Consular Police
crime section began an investigation
of the crime at once.

Wrist Watch Stolen

All possessions of the victim were
left on the body, except a wrist
watch, which had apparently been
stolen, as the strap of the watch was
left dangling on the wrist of the in-
jured man. In the absence of other
signs of robbery, it was believed the
crime was of an anti-Japanese ter-
rorist nature. Besides the head
wounds and the bullet wound in the
chest, scratches and marks on the
face indicated that a furious struggle
had taken place, the Japanese police
revealed.

A native of Ogura, in Fukuoka
Prefecture, Kyushu, Mr. Iwau came
to Shanghai on December 30 of last
year. He had been residing at the
Konsenso, a Japanese boarding house
on Scott Road. He opened an office
on the fifth floor of the Bank of East
Asia at 299 Szechuen Road. The
victim is survived by his wife and a
boy, who live in Japan, the Japanese
press stated.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》（NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS），
1939 年 4 月 11 日
07752

日本人遭中国匪徒杀害

卡车在大场附近被三人拦截；枪手逃脱追捕队伍

据日本媒体昨日报道，周日上午 9 时 30 分左右，在上海附近的大场（Tazang），三和洋行（Santo Yoko，建筑材料承包商）41 岁的日本业主岩尾清六（Seizo Iwau）先生与另外两人同乘一辆卡车时，遭到三名中国武装匪徒袭击，成为受害者。他被从卡车上拖下，在失去知觉的情况下被送往福民医院（Foomin hospital），不久后因伤身亡。

据报道，岩尾先生在从大场前往宝山（Paoshan）以西的罗店（Lotien-chien）购买铁板的途中，由一位姓张的中国铁器经纪人和一名卡车司机陪同，当行至距大场两公里的一座横跨小溪的桥梁时，三名中国人从桥下出现，用手枪逼停卡车。

据报纸称，其中一名武装分子将受害者从卡车上拉下，并驱散其两名惊恐的同伴，向这名日本人开了一枪，子弹从其背部右侧射入，从右胸附近穿出。另一名恐怖分子用重型铁器猛击受害者头部右侧，致其头骨骨折。

另一伙人到达

据报道，袭击发生后，中国人留在犯罪现场，显然是在等待侵害另一名日本人，此时，大同公司（Daido Kumi，一家承包商行）的两名日本雇员在几名隶属于电报单位的日本士兵陪同下接近现场。中国人注意到他们的接近后逃窜，日本人展开追击并开了十枪。然而，匪徒成功逃脱。

日本人通知了大场防卫司令部，司令部立即派遣部分部队搜寻逃逸的中国人。受害者被紧急送往福民医院，但他在中午过后不久因伤死亡。日本领事馆警察署犯罪科警员立即开始对案件进行调查。

手表被盗

除一只腕表 apparently 被盗外，受害者的所有财物均留在尸体上，因为表带仍 dangling 在受伤者的手腕上。由于没有其他抢劫迹象，人们认为这是一起具有反日恐怖主义性质的犯罪。日本警方透露，除了头部伤口和胸部枪伤外，面部的抓痕和痕迹表明曾发生过激烈的搏斗。

岩尾先生是九州福冈县小仓（Ogura）人，于去年 12 月 30 日来到上海。他一直居住在斯科特路（Scott Road）的一家名为“宏仙庄”（Konsenso，音译）的日本寄宿公寓。他在四川路 299 号东亚银行五楼开设了一间办事处。日本媒体称，死者遗孀及一子尚在日本生活。

pages.en:
April 10, 1939.

MAINICHI

JAPANESE KILLED BY THREE CHINESE NEAR LOTIEN
VILLAGE (NEAR DAZANG)

At about 9.20 a.m. April 9
as a Japanese named S. Iwanama, age 42, of Messrs
Sanda Yoko, No. 299 Szechuen Road, in company with
a Chinese broker named Chang Nyoh Lin, age 52, was
travelling in a truck on a road leading to Lotien Village,
near Dazang, he encountered three Chinese who were
hiding under a bridge two kilometres from the village.
The Chinese ordered the chauffeur and Chang to run away
and fired several shots at Mr. Iwanama hitting him in
the right side of the back and the head. While
awaiting their next victim they were discovered
by several Japanese soldiers and two employees of
Messrs Taido Kumi, who were passing on a truck. The
soldiers fired more than dozen shots at the Chinese who
made good their escape. Upon receiving a report, the
Garrison Headquarters at Dazang dispatched a company
of soldiers to the scene to make investigations. The
victim was removed to the Foo Ming Hospital on North
Szechuen Road but succumbed at 12.25 p.m. The
Japanese Consular Police made enquiries and found that
only the victim's wrist watch was missing while his
purse and other belongings were intact. The victim met
his death at the hands of terrorists.
pages.zh:
1939 年 4 月 10 日。

《每日新闻》（MAINICHI）

三名中国人在罗店村（近大场）附近杀害一名日本人

4 月 9 日上午 9 时 20 分左右，三田洋行（Sanda Yoko，地址：四川路 299 号）的一名 42 岁日本人名叫 S. Iwanama（音译），与一名 52 岁的中国经纪人名叫 Chang Nyoh Lin（音译）结伴，乘坐卡车行驶在通往大场附近罗店村的道路上时，遭遇了隐藏在距该村两公里处一座桥下的三名中国人。中国人命令司机和 Chang 逃跑，并向 Iwanama 先生开了几枪，击中其背部右侧和头部。当他们等待下一个受害者时，被几名日本士兵和两名途经此地的大同公司（Taido Kumi，音译）雇员发现。士兵向中国人开了十几枪，中国人成功逃脱。接到报告后，大场驻军司令部派遣一个连的士兵到现场进行调查。受害者被送往北四川路的福民医院（Foo Ming Hospital），但于下午 12 时 25 分身亡。日本领事馆警察经查询发现，仅受害者的腕表丢失，其钱包及其他物品完好无损。受害者死于恐怖分子之手。

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

At about 9.30 a.m. 13-6-39 the undersigned who was accompanied by D.S.I. Lieu Kyung Ching, D.S. Sugimoto and D.r.S. Yamahara proceeded to the "Land Bank of China" Godown, Soochow Road, where in the presence of Mr. C.C. Pun, manager of the Bank's "Property Dept.", five sacks and three baskets containing empty shell cases were handed over to representatives of the Japanese Gendarmerie.

Difficulty however, was experienced regarding cartridge, and shell cases which happened to be mixed with other scrap metal, and as this would involve several days work before this difficulty could be overcome, the representatives of the Japanese Gendarmerie decided to refer the matter to their superior officers before proceeding with the task involved, as in all probability the results obtained would not compensate them for the time spent.

Mr. Pun has raised an objection to the handing over of the cartridge cases as the Bank's legal advisers in their correspondence on this matter, stipulated that only shell cases were to be surrendered.

However, as this was probably an oversight on the part of Messrs. Ellis & Hay's, no difficulty is anticipated in getting this rectified.

S U M M A R Y
=============

At about 10:50 a.m. April 19, 1939, the
"Land Bank of China" Godowns, situated at Nos.955 -
979 Soochow Road, were searched by officers attached
to Crime Branch Headquarters (C.1), S.M.P. at the
request of Sergt.Major SAK MOTO of the Japanese
Gendarmerie (Floating Restaurant Detachment), as it
was alleged by an informer, named TSEU DEU SUNG
(朱头生), 40 years of age, M/Coolie, residing 22
Yangchow Road, that munitions of war, military
uniforms and field telephone wire, the property of
the Chinese Nationalist Government, were stored on
the premises.

Two of the godowns and stairways were searched
in the presence of Mr. Pan Chu Chung (潘起縱),
Manager of the "Property Department" of the above bank.

On the stairway of a godown situated at No.
955 Soochow Road, were found a number of sacks of
scrap brass which included used shell cases and
cartridge cases, all obviously collected after the
recent hostilities. In spite of the fact that these
could not logically be construed as munitions of war
to be used against the Japanese Forces, Sergt. Major
pages.zh:

                   五月      5日,       39年。

摘 要
===

1939年4月19日上午约10时50分，应日本宪兵队（水上餐厅分队）坂本（SAK MOTO）军曹的请求，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）总部罪案科（C.1）的警员对中国银行仓库（位于苏州路955-979号）进行了搜查。此举系因一名名为朱头生（TSEU DEU SUNG）、40岁、职业为苦力、居住在扬州路22号的线人举报，称该处存放有属于中国国民政府的军火、军服及野战电话线。

在上述银行的“产业部”经理潘起縱（Pan Chu Chung）先生的见证下，对其中两个仓库及楼梯间进行了搜查。

在位于苏州路955号的一个仓库的楼梯上，发现数袋废铜，其中包括使用过的炮弹壳和子弹壳，显然都是近期战事后收集的。尽管从逻辑上讲，这些物品不能被解释为用于对抗日军的军火，但坂本军曹

pages.en:

Sakamoto insisted that four shell cases should be
removed by the Municipal Police as evidence, which
was accordingly done.

In Godown No.46, situated at No.967 Soochow
Road, a number of bales of clothing, which the informer
stated were intended for military uniforms, were found.
No insignia or distinguishing marks were found on the
clothing to indicate that they were intended as
military uniforms.

According to Mr. Pan, this clothing, he was
given to understand, was intended for distribution
among local refugees.

A search of the godown failed to reveal any
military telephone wire, although pieces of wire which
might have been used in telephone cable, were found in
several bales of metal scrap.

Enquiries made by the undersigned through Mr.
C.C.Pan, show that the scrap metal, which includes the
shell and cartridge cases, was purchased by the "Yung
Chong Brass Works (永昌銅廠)" from the undermentioned
firms on the following dates : -

(1) 2.3.1939 - 50 bags of scrap zinc plate and brass,
valued $4,967.17, from the "Deeng Fah
Ziang (同芳祥 ) Metal Dealers, Peking
Road, East of Kweichow Road (Tel.91618).

坚持要求巡捕房移走四个炮弹壳作为证据，警方遂照办。

在位于苏州路967号的46号仓库内，发现了数包衣物，据线人称这些是准备用作军服的。但在衣物上未发现任何表明其 intended 为军服的徽章或特殊标记。

据潘先生称，他获悉这些衣物是打算分发给当地难民的。

对仓库的搜查未发现任何军用电话线，尽管在几包金属废料中发现了可能曾用于电话电缆的金属线段。

经签署人通过潘起縱（C.C.Pan）先生查询得知，包括炮弹壳和子弹壳在内的废金属，是由“永昌銅廠”于下列日期从下述商号购买的：-

(1) 1939年3月2日 - 50袋废锌板和黄铜，价值$4,967.17，购自“同芳祥”金属商号，地址：北京路，贵州路以东（电话91618）。

(3) 13.3.39 - 106 bags of white zinc plates & scrap

Four invoices relating to the above transactions

All the metal is mortgaged to the bank as that

The manager of the new factory, which is being

(朱鎮南), who resides at No.80 Joffre Terrace, Avenue
Joffre, French Concession.

This gentleman has been interviewed by
the undersigned and he corroborates the information
given by Mr. Pan. He stated that he had no idea
that the bags of metal contained some shell
and cartridge cases until informed by Mr. Pan,
following the search which was conducted by the

所有金属均已抵押给银行，因为该机构正在提供资金建造新厂房，以取代原位于江湾西億商號路（Si Tien Yah Wei Road）607号、在战事中被烧毁的旧厂房。

新工厂正在胶州路旁地籍地块6225-W.D.以东的一块土地上建造，其经理为朱鎮南（Chu Cheng Nan）先生，住址：法租界霞飞路霞飞坊80号。

签署人已约谈这位先生，他证实了潘先生提供的信息。他表示，直到潘先生在宪兵队要求下进行搜查后告知他之前，他并不知道那些金属袋中含有一些炮弹壳和子弹壳。

抵押贷款的金额未予明确，因为银行是以金属为担保，随着施工各阶段的完成而逐步放款。

关于棉衣，潘先生称，这是由“杨兴”公司（Yih Hsing Coy.）于1937年11月27日至1938年1月11日期间存入其仓库的。他们没有这家公司的地址记录，也未收到任何仓储费。

1939年5月3日收到两封日期为1939年5月2日的来信，来自该行的法律顾问埃利斯和海律师事务所（Messrs Ellis and Hay's），地址：北京路137号。信中抗议对完全合法且与战事毫无关联的正常商业活动进行任何干涉。他们指出，废金属是从当地经销商处按常规方式购买的，这些经销商收集各类金属以供后续熔炼和制造之用，这是行业中正常且普遍的流程，在世界各地皆然。

A. C. Glover
督察

向日本宪兵队提供的协助

随函附上1939年4月21日签发、由日本海军陆战队警官松崎（Y. Matsuzaki）上尉签署的水警第115号文件。该文件要求将中方声称是日本制造的炮弹壳和子弹壳，以及在中国银行仓库中发现的军服和电线，移交给日本当局。

经签署人通过上述银行“产业部”经理范先生（Mr. C. C. Fan）进一步查询得知，包括一定数量炮弹壳和子弹壳在内的废金属，是由“永昌銅廠”于下列日期从下述商号购买的：-

(1) 1939年3月2日 - 50袋废锌板和黄铜，价值$4,247.17，购自“同發祥”金属商号，地址：北京路，贵州路以东（电话91618）。

(2) 1939年3月7日 - 81袋废锌板和黄铜，价值$6,315.03，购自“華興”金属店，地址：爱文义路福達里3号。（分两批交货）。

(3) 1939年3月13日 - 106袋白锌板和废黄铜，价值$4,417.72，购自“恒源祥五金”，地址：南京路100号。

Four invoices relating to the above
transaction are being temporarily kept by the under-
signed for reference if required.
All the metal is mortgaged to the Bank,
as that institution is financing the erection of new
factory premises to replace those formerly situated at
No. 607 Si Tien Yah Wei (〔此处转录不清〕) Road, Kiangwan,
which were burnt down during the hostilities. The
manager of the new factory, which is being built on a
plot of land located east of Cadastral lot 6225-W.D.,
off Kiaochow Road, is a Mr. Chu Cheng Nan (朱镇南),
who resides at No. 80, Joffre Terrace, Avenue Joffre,
French Concession.
This gentleman has been interviewed by the
undersigned and he corroborates the information given
by Mr. Pan. He stated that he had no idea that the
bags of metal contained some shell and cartridge cases
until informed of the fact by Mr. Pan, following the
search which was conducted by the Police at the
request of the Gendarmerie.
The amount of the mortgage has not been
specified, as the Bank is advancing money, on the
security of the metal, as each section of the
construction work is completed.

与上述交易相关的四张发票由签署人暂时保管，以备查考。
所有金属均已抵押给银行，因为该机构正在提供资金建造新厂房，以取代原位于江湾〔此处转录不清〕路607号、在战事中被烧毁的旧厂房。新工厂正在胶州路旁地籍地块6225-W.D.以东的一块土地上建造，其经理为朱镇南（Chu Cheng Nan）先生，住址：法租界霞飞路霞飞坊80号。
签署人已约谈这位先生，他证实了潘先生提供的信息。他表示，直到潘先生在宪兵队要求下进行搜查后告知他这一事实之前，他并不知道那些金属袋中含有一些炮弹壳和子弹壳。
抵押贷款的金额未予明确，因为银行是以金属为担保，随着施工各阶段的完成而逐步放款。

April 22, 39.
2

ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

At about 9.45 a.m., April 21st, 1939,
Sergt. Major Sakamoto, who was accompanied by the
informer in this case, one named Tseu Deu Sung
(朱頭生), 40 years, Native of Hopei, M/Coolie,
residing 22 Yangchow Road, came to Headquarters
where he again requested assistance to interview the
foreman coolie of the Land Bank of China Godown, No.
979 Soochow Road, who had been arrested, but
subsequently released on security the previous day.
The foreman coolie, Tsang Ching Sai
(張全山), was sent for, and on arrival was further
interrogated, but he denied the allegation that he had
ever manufactured or been in possession of counterfeit
Japanese military notes.
The informer, on being questioned, stated
that about three months ago he was temporarily
employed as a coolie under the control of Tsang Ching
Sai. On one occasion during January 1939, whilst
alone in Tsang's office, he saw a bundle containing
about one hundred pieces of paper which he took to be
cigarette coupons. He stole one and placed it in his
pocket. Later he went to Yangtzepoo where he met a
friend to whom he showed the piece of paper. This

1939年4月22日。
2

向日本宪兵队提供的协助。

1939年4月21日上午约9时45分，本案线人朱頭生（Tseu Deu Sung，40岁，河北籍，苦力，住扬州路22号）陪同日本宪兵队坂本（Sakamoto）军曹来到总部，再次请求协助讯问中国银行苏州路979号仓库的领班苦力。该领班此前一天已被逮捕，但随后获保释放。
领班苦力张全山（Tsang Ching Sai）被传唤到场，并接受了进一步讯问，但他否认了有关他曾制造或持有伪造日本军用钞票的指控。
线人在接受讯问时称，大约三个月前，他曾在张全山的管辖下临时受雇为苦力。1939年1月期间，有一次他独自在张的办公室里，看到一捆大约一百张纸，他以为是香烟票券。他偷了一张放进口袋。后来他去了杨树浦，遇到一个朋友，便把那张纸给他看。这位

pages.en:
- 2 -

friend, whose name was not divulged and who happened
to be an agent of the Japanese authorities, immediately
recognised the note as a counterfeit Japanese military
note. He accordingly reported the matter to his
employers, who instructed him to make further
enquiries.

As Tsang Ching Sai had denied the
allegations of the informer and the evidence was
deemed insufficient, Sergt. Major Sakamoto stated that
his Department had decided to give the man the benefit
of the doubt and to drop the case.

As regards the shell and cartridge cases
found in the godowns amongst the bags of scrap metal,
he stated that these were undoubtedly of Japanese
origin, and therefore requested that one of the cases
be temporarily loaned to him so as he could submit
them to a higher authority for examination. This
request was acceded to and one of the shell cases was
handed over.

A.G.

A. C. Glover
D. I.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

朋友（姓名未透露）碰巧是日本当局的代理人，立即认出那张纸币是伪造的日本军用钞票。于是他随即向雇主报告此事，雇主指示他做进一步调查。

由于张全山否认了线人的指控，且证据被认为不足，坂本军曹表示，他的部门决定给予此人疑罪从无的处理，并撤销此案。

关于在仓库废金属袋中发现的炮弹壳和子弹壳，他表示这些无疑源自日本，因此请求暂时借给他其中一个弹壳，以便提交上级当局检验。此请求获准，其中一个炮弹壳被移交。

A.G.

A. C. Glover
督察

D. C. (Special Branch).

Headquarters
C. l. Misc. 44/39 Crime Branch
April 19, 39.
1

ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO THE JAPANESE GENDARMERIE.

During the morning of the 19th April 1939,
Sergt. Major Sakamoto of the Japanese Gendarmerie
stationed at the "Floating Restaurant", Peking Road
Jetty, requested assistance to search the "Land Bank
of China" Godowns, situated at No. 979 Soochow Road,
wherein it was alleged were stored shells, military
uniforms and military telephone wire, the property of
the Chinese Nationalist Government.

Sergt. Major Sakamoto also requested
assistance in arresting the Foreman Coolie of the above
concern named Tsang Ching Sai (張金山), residing No.
230, Yi Ching Li (行慶里), Amoy Road, as it was
believed that this individual was in possession of
counterfeit Japanese Military notes.

These allegations were based upon the
testimony of two Chinese who accompanied Sergt. Major
Sakamoto to Police Headquarters at the time that this
request was made.

British Military Headquarters, in whose
sector the premises are located, were immediately
informed of the intended raid, whilst S.I. Ring and
F.S. Bafer, attached to Louza Station, accompanied the
party, which carried out the search between 10.50 a.m.
and 1.30 p.m., April 19th, 1939.

（左侧手写批注：）

1939年4月19日。
1

向日本宪兵队提供的协助。

1939年4月19日上午，驻扎在北京路码头“水上餐厅”的日本宪兵队坂本（Sakamoto）军曹请求协助搜查位于苏州路979号的“中国银行”仓库，据称那里存放有属于中国国民政府的炮弹、军服和军用电话线。

坂本军曹还请求协助逮捕上述机构的领班苦力张金山（Tsang Ching Sai），住址：厦门路行慶里230号，因为相信此人持有伪造的日本军用钞票。

这些指控基于两名中国人的证词，他们在提出此请求时陪同坂本军曹来到警察总部。

 premises 所在辖区的英军总部立即获悉了此次拟议的突袭行动，同时隶属于老闸捕房的环（Ring）巡长和巴弗（Bafer）外勤警员陪同行动小组，于1939年4月19日上午10时50分至下午1时30分之间执行了搜查。

（左侧手写批注：）

- 2 -

... of the godowns and stairways were
searched in the presence of Mr. Fan Chu Chung
( **〔此处转录不清〕** ), Manager of the Property Dept. of the
above Bank.

On the stairway of the godown situated at
No. 966 Szechow Road were found a number of sacks of
scrap brass which included used shell cases and
cartridge cases, all obviously gathered during the
recent hostilities. In spite of the fact that they
could not be construed as munitions of war to be used
against the Japanese, Sergt. Major Sakamoto insisted
that four shell cases be removed by the Municipal
Police as evidence, which was accordingly done.

In Godown No. 46 situated at No. 967
Szechow Road, a number of bales of clothing, which
the informer stated were intended for military
uniforms, were found. No insignia or distinguishing
marks were found on the clothing to indicate that
they were intended as military uniforms.

According to Mr. Fan, this clothing was
intended for distribution among local refugees.

A search of the godown failed to reveal
any military telephone wire, although pieces of wire
which might have been used in telephone cable were
found in several bales of metal scrap.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

……在上述银行物业部经理范楚忠（Fan Chu Chung）先生〔此处转录不清〕的在场见证下，对仓库及楼梯间进行了搜查。

在位于四川路966号的仓库楼梯上，发现数袋废铜料，其中包括已使用的炮弹壳和子弹壳，显然均系近期战事期间收集之物。尽管这些物品不能被解释为用于对抗日军的军火，但坂本警曹长坚持要求工部局警务处移走四枚炮弹壳作为证据，遂照办。

在位于四川路967号的46号仓库内，发现数包衣物，据线人称这些衣物 intended 用于制作军服。但在衣物上未发现任何徽章或识别标记以表明其拟用作军服。

据范先生称，这些衣物旨在分发给当地难民。

对仓库的搜查未发现任何军用电话线，尽管在几包金属废料中发现了可能曾用于电话电缆的电线碎片。

pages.en:
- 3 -

The Foreman Coolie named Tsang Ching Sai,
who was found in the office attached to these
godowns, was then taken into custody on suspicion of
being concerned in the manufacture of counterfeit
Military notes, which the informer alleged were
manufactured in one of the godowns.

A further search of the godowns and the
arrested man's abode, situated in a loft in Lane No.
230, Yi Ching Li, Amoy Road, however, failed to
reveal any incriminating evidence.

From particulars obtained from the Godown
Books it was ascertained that the used shell and
cartridge cases were contained in consignments of
scrap metal sent on various dates and placed in
different godowns between the 2nd March and 15th March
1939, by Messrs. Yoong Tsang (永昌 ) Brass-smiths,
whose address up to the present has not been obtained.
The total consignment numbers two hundred and thirty
seven sacks.

The alleged uniforms contained in five
hundred and seven bales were received between the
27-11-37 and the 11-1-38, from Messrs. Hsieh Hsing
(协兴 ), whose address has not yet been ascertained.

These particulars will be forwarded to the
undersigned by Mr. Pan, who has undertaken to obtain
them.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

随后，在这些仓库附属办公室内发现的名为曾景赛（Tsang Ching Sai）的工头苦力因涉嫌参与制造伪军用票（据线人指控，伪钞是在其中一间仓库内制造的）而被拘留。

然而，对这些仓库以及被捕者住所（位于厦门路怡庆里230弄的一间阁楼）的进一步搜查，并未发现任何确凿证据。

根据从仓库账簿中获得的详情查明，这些使用过的炮弹壳和子弹壳包含在由永昌（Yoong Tsang）铜匠铺发送的废金属货物中。该铜匠铺的地址迄今尚未获取。这些货物于1939年3月2日至3月15日期间的不同日期送达，并存放在不同的仓库中。货物总数为二百三十七袋。

据称包含在五百零七包中的所谓军服，系于1937年11月27日至1938年1月11日期间从协兴（Hsieh Hsing）商行接收，该行地址亦尚未查明。

上述详情将由潘先生转交给具名者，潘先生已承诺负责获取这些信息。

pages.en:
- 4 -

At the conclusion of this search the
arrested man was conveyed to Headquarters, where he
was temporarily detained for questioning. On being
questioned he emphatically denied the allegations
made by the informers, one of whom, the Gendarmerie
officers stated, was formerly employed by the Land
Bank of China. As no evidence could be obtained
against this man, he was released after a written
guarantee had been given by Mr. Pan that the man would
attend Police Headquarters whenever he was required.
Sergt. Major Sakamoto will forward in due
course a statement from one of the informers relating
to the allegations made against the arrested man.

MC

M. C. Gilmore
D. I.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

搜查结束后，被捕男子被押送至总局，暂时扣留以备讯问。在接受讯问时，他坚决否认线人的指控。据宪兵军官称，其中一名线人此前曾受雇于中国土地银行。由于无法获得针对此人的证据，在潘先生出具书面担保，保证该男子在需要时会随时前往警察总局后，将其释放。
坂本警曹长将在适当时候提交一份来自其中一名线人的陈述，内容涉及对被捕男子的指控。

MC

M. C. Gilmore
侦探督察

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE RENDERED TO JAPANESE
GENDARMERIE HEADQUARTERS, BRIDGE HOUSE.
........

On the morning of April 27th. 1939, the seized
25 letters, 15 envelops, 5 name cards and 2 account paper
were handed over to the undersigned by the French Police.

On being scrutinized, 18 letters were found to
contain nothing but details relating to domestic affairs,
whilst the contents of the remaining 7 letters, fully
corroborate the accusation laid down by the Japanese
Gendarmerie Headquarters against the suspect.

The contents of the 7 letters show that the
suspect, Soong Poo Tsung, is wanted by the Japanese Mil.
Authorities in Yangchow, and that posters bearing the
suspect's photograph are published in Yangchow (Letter
No.3).

The authors of these letters, i.e. the suspects
mother and son, advised the suspect to stay in Shanghai,
informing him that two persons, namely :-
Siau Woo Zang (沙和尚)
& Kyi Zang Kying (化長金),
had been arrested by Japanese soldiers (Letters No.4 & 6)
Also, the authors of the letters advised the suspect to
destroy the letters because the publicity of same might
effect the opposite party. (Letters No.4 & 2).

（左侧手写批注：）

关于向日本宪兵司令部（百老汇大厦）提供进一步协助之事 ____ 

1939年4月27日上午，法国警察将查获的25封信件、15个信封、5张名片和2张账单纸移交给具名者。

经仔细审查，发现其中18封信件仅包含有关家庭事务的细节，而其余7封信件的内容完全佐证了日本宪兵司令部对嫌疑人的指控。

这7封信件的内容显示，嫌疑人宋宝宗（Soong Poo Tsung）正被扬州的日本军方当局通缉，且扬州张贴有印有嫌疑人照片的通缉海报（第3号信件）。

这些信件的作者，即嫌疑人的母亲和儿子，劝告嫌疑人留在上海，并告知他两人， namely :-
沙和尚（Siau Woo Zang）
及 化长金（Kyi Zang Kying），
已被日军逮捕（第4号和第6号信件）。此外，信件作者还建议嫌疑人销毁信件，因为信件的公开可能会影响对方。（第4号和第2号信件）。

（左侧手写批注：）
C.S.L

pages.en:
LIST OF DOCUMENTS SEIZED IN ACCUSED'S ROOM.

A perusal of the 25 seized letters showed that 18
of them relate to only domestic affairs, whilst the remaining
7 are gistcd as follows : -

LETTER NO.I : Addressed to "Father" by one, "Vung Yuen" :

" You stated in the letter that you would come to
Yangchow, but I did not expect you to return. Zang
Ching is a detective employed by the Japanese Army.
One day, Zang Ching led a party of Japanese Army
to effect the arrest of one, named KHON CHING FU, who
later was released on producing guarantor, and after
expending about $200.00. Zang Ching came to my
house yesterday in order to obtain the addresses of
you and my grand-mother at present in Chinkiang. They
are now looking for you, so I request you not to return

LETTER NO.II : Addressed to "Boo Tsung" by one, "Shing" :

"Dear Younger Brother, Boo Tsung,
Be patient and stay in Shanghai. Don't return
to this village, as circumstances at present are
abnormal.
Yesterday, your wife went to see Section Chief
Chang at Yangchow, and the latter is of the same
opinion as mine.
It is likewise, not advisable for your son to
come back here. You are clever enough to know that
by yourself.
Today, whilst on my way to the village for shopping
I encountered your son, Vung Yuen, who informed me of
your opinion too.
Your wife, as we know, is an able hand in domestic
affairs, you should seek her advice and take care in
all matters. Don't think of returning, please !
I hope you will destroy this note after perusal,
for in case it should fall into the hands of others,
they might despise you."
Signed : Shing. "

LETTER NO.III : Addressed by Sung Doo Sz to husband :

" Dear Husband,
Please give the address of Yui Gien Loong in your
forthcoming letter. Do not return home now, as
posters bearing your photo can be seen everywhere, in
search of you. "
Signed : Sung Doo Sz. "
pages.zh:
在被告房间内查获的文件清单。

查阅查获的25封信件显示，其中18封仅涉及家庭事务，其余7封的大意如下：-

第一号信件：由“Vung Yuen”致“父亲”：

“你在信中说你要来扬州，但我没想到你会回来。张静（Zang Ching）是日本军队雇佣的一名侦探。有一天，张静带领一队日军去逮捕一名叫孔庆福（KHON CHING FU）的人，后者后来通过提供担保人并花费约200美元后获释。张静昨天来到我家，目的是获取你和目前身在镇江的祖母的地址。他们正在找你，所以我请求你不要回来

第二号信件：由“Shing”致“宝宗”：

“亲爱的弟弟，宝宗，
请耐心留在上海。不要回到这个村子，因为目前的局势不正常。
昨天，你的妻子去扬州见了张科长，他的观点与我相同。
同样，你的儿子也不宜回到这里。你足够聪明，自己明白这一点。
今天，我在去村里购物的路上遇到了你的儿子 Vung Yuen，他也告诉了我你的想法。
众所周知，你的妻子在处理家务方面很能干，你应该征求她的意见，凡事小心。请不要考虑回来！
希望你阅后销毁此信，以免落入他人之手，让他们看不起你。”
签名：Shing。”

第三号信件：由宋杜氏（Sung Doo Sz）致丈夫：

“亲爱的丈夫，
请在下一封信中告知余根龙（Yui Gien Loong）的地址。现在不要回家，因为到处都能看到印有你照片的通缉海报，正在搜捕你。”
签名：宋杜氏。”

pages.en:
- 2 -

LETTER NO. IV : Addressed by Boo Tsoong to his son, Vung Nyoen
" How is it that you have no time to write?
You may be busy, but you certainly did not pay
any attention to your work. In future you should
write to me yourself and do not ask others to do
it for you. You must not show the letter to any-
one, as it might have some effect on the opposite
party. There is a detailed list coming here to
say that Siau Woo Zaung had been arrested by that
party. "
....................

LETTER NO. V. : Addressed by "mother" to her son, Kwang Ching.
" It is of great importance that you and your
father should not return home for the time being.
You two can eke out a living just the same and I'll
be contented at home. Should I hear anything
hopeful, a letter will be immediately despatched to
you to hasten your return. You two must be careful
in choosing your jobs. "
....................

LETTER NO. VI : Addressed by Doo Sze to husband, Kwang Ching.
" I think I will not go back to our native place
this year, but will do so next year. Day before
yesterday, in the country, Kyi Zang Kying and Siau
Woo Zaung were arrested and taken away by Japanese
soldiers. "
....................

LETTER NO. VII : Addressed by Sung Doo Sz to husband.
" A reply please send to Doo Sz Yuen, c/o Vung
Loong Mer, Tung Zah Zung Der, South Gate, Yangchow.
Please write a false name on the envelope instead
of your bona fide name. "
pages.zh:
- 2 -

第四号信件：由宝宗（Boo Tsoong）致其子 Vung Nyoen
“你怎么没时间写信？
你可能很忙，但你肯定没有专心工作。以后你应该亲自给我写信，不要让别人代劳。你不得向任何人展示这封信，因为它可能会对对方产生某种影响。有一份详细名单传到这里，说沙和尚（Siau Woo Zaung）已被那一方逮捕。”
 ____ 

第五号信件：由“母亲”致其子广清（Kwang Ching）。
“你和你的父亲暂时不要回家，这至关重要。你们两人在外同样可以谋生，我在家也会安心。如果我听到任何有利的消息，会立即写信催促你们回来。你们两人在选择工作时必须小心。”
 ____ 

第六号信件：由杜氏（Doo Sze）致丈夫广清（Kwang Ching）。
“我想今年我不会回故乡，而是明年再回。前天，在乡下，化长金（Kyi Zang Kying）和沙和尚（Siau Woo Zaung）被日军逮捕并带走。”
 ____ 

第七号信件：由宋杜氏（Sung Doo Sz）致丈夫。
“请将回复寄给扬州南门董家总德（Tung Zah Zung Der）陆龙梅（Vung Loong Mer）转交杜氏元（Doo Sz Yuen）。请在信封上写一个假名，而不是你的真名。”

pages.en:
further
SOONG POO TSUNG (宋宝宗),

H. J. C. B.           26-4-39           X      C.D.C. 2
                                      translated
                                      -------- Tsaung Zung Pau

The twenty five letters seized by the Police at
my place of abode were all sent to me by my friends and
relatives in my native place, warning me not to return home
as the Japanese would bring about my arrest. My wife was
prompted to write letters to me as the result of rumours
being circulated by my rivals in rattan business that I
was being sought by the Japanese authorities, so that they
could carry on their trade without my competition.

About one month after my arrival in Shanghai,
my native friend Zau Yok Vung also came here for the purpose
of selling ducks. One day, I encountered him at Tai-yuan
Vi Yang Theatre where he related the following incident to me:-

That the Acting Chief of our village named Chi
Zang Ching had been arrested by the Japanese at Hongjao, but
subsequently released after enquiries had failed to warrant
his detention. That the Japanese, on receipt of further
information that Chi was a member of a Mobile Unit, proceeded
to his home but finding that he was absent, arrested his
younger brother, Siau Wee Zaung. That Chi Zang Ching eventually
guaranteed for the release of his brother from the Japanese
Military Police after he had been detained there for about
three weeks. That the Japanese finally appointed Chi Zang
Ching as the Village Chief to work together with them.

The above is my true statement.

Signed, Cross-marked & Thumb-printed :
SOONG POO TSUNG.
pages.zh:
续
宋宝宗（SOONG POO TSUNG），

H. J. C. B.           1939年4月26日           X      C.D.C. 2
                                      已翻译
                                      -------- 张宗保（音译）

警方在我住所查获的二十五封信件均由我家乡的朋友和亲戚寄给我，警告我不要回家，因为日本人会逮捕我。我的妻子之所以写信给我，是因为我在藤器生意上的竞争对手散布谣言，说我正被日本当局搜捕，以便他们可以在没有我竞争的情况下继续做生意。

我抵达上海约一个月后，我的家乡朋友赵友文（Zau Yok Vung，音译）也来这里卖鸭子。有一天，我在太原维扬戏院遇到他，他向我讲述了以下事件：-

我们村的代理村长季张静（Chi Zang Ching，音译）曾在虹桥被日本人逮捕，但经调查后发现没有理由拘留他，随后获释。日本人收到进一步情报称季是某流动小组成员后，前往其家中，但发现他不在，便逮捕了他的弟弟萧伟章（Siau Wee Zaung，音译）。季张静最终为其弟向日本宪兵队担保，使其在被拘留约三周后获释。日本人最终任命季张静为村长，与他们合作。

以上是我的真实陈述。

签名、画押并按手印：
宋宝宗。

ARREST OF SUSPECTED GUERILLA.

〔批：C 5/4 Pwt 24/4〕
〔印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH〕

At 4 p.m. on the 22nd. of April, 1939, Sgt.
Major Katoda with two other members of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Headquarters, came to S.M.Police Headquarters
and requested that assistance be rendered in effecting
the arrest of a member of a guerilla unit.

According to the information obtained by
Sgt.Major Katoda through his agent (not produced in
person) that one named SOONG POO TSUNG (孫崇忠), a
member of a guerilla unit operating in Yangchow District,
Kiangsu Province, had evaded arrest when the members of
the Military Police Headquarters stationed in Yangchow,
had arrested two members of a guerilla unit, and had fled
to Shanghai, and that he was implicated by the arrested
two men in Yangchow.

Sgt. Katoda further stated that the wanted
man, SOONG POO TSUNG, could now be located at the Hwa
Yang Lou (華陽樓) Restaurant, 601 Nanking Road, where
he would attend a dinner party.

向日本宪兵司令部（百老汇大厦）提供协助 ____ 

逮捕疑似游击队员。

〔批注：C 5/4 Pwt 24/4〕
〔印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处〕

1939年4月22日下午4时，角田警曹长与另外两名日本宪兵司令部成员来到工部局警务处总局，请求协助逮捕一名游击队员。

根据角田警曹长通过其代理人（未亲自出面）获得的情报，名为孙崇忠（SOONG POO TSUNG）的人系在江苏省扬州地区活动的一支游击队的成员。当驻扎在扬州的宪兵司令部成员逮捕了两名游击队员时，他逃脱了逮捕并逃往上海，且被扬州的两名被捕者供出牵连其中。

角田警曹长进一步指出，通缉犯孙崇忠现可定位在南京路601号华阳楼餐厅，他将出席那里的晚宴。

The necessary assistance was rendered by C.D.C.s
2, 206, C.D.S.129, D.S.I. Wong Zung Wo, D.S.I. Watanabe,
D.S. Sugimoto and the undersigned in presence of the
Officer i/c C.I, C.D.I. Grubb.

At 4:30 p.m. same date, the mentioned detectives
together with the members of the Japanese Gendarmerie,
proceeded to 621 Hankow Road, where, on the first floor,
it was found to be occupied by a party of Chinese male
and female persons attending a dinner.

On being questioned as to their identity, one
male person of the party identified himself by the name
of the wanted man :-

SOONG POO TSUNG (孫步忠), alias SOONG KWONG CHING
(孫廣慶), 43, native of Yangchow,
M/Unemployed, N.F.A.

At the time of his questioning, Soong Poo Tsung
made an attempt to discard a Chinese note book, which
on being later examined, was found to contain a number of
names of Chinese persons only.

At the request of Sgt.Major Katoda, two other
members of the party, namely : -

S TING LAI (施亭蘭), 45, Chekiang, M/
accountant, Rue B.Gross

TS YOONG LIM (朱耀林), 40, Chekiang, M/
theatre owner, Rue
Saigon.

刑事侦缉处（C.D.C.）第2、206号警员，刑事侦缉科（C.D.S.）第129号警员，副督察黄宗和（Wong Zung Wo），副督察渡边（Watanabe），侦探杉本（Sugimoto）及具名人在刑事情报科（C.I.）主管、首席侦探督察格鲁布（Grubb）在场下提供了必要协助。

同日下午4时30分，上述侦探会同日本宪兵队成员前往汉口路621号，在该处一楼发现有一群中国男女正在聚餐。

经询问身份时，其中一名男子自称为通缉犯：

宋步忠（SOONG POO TSUNG），又名宋广庆（SOONG KWONG CHING），43岁，扬州人，男/无业，非上海籍（N.F.A.）。

在接受盘问时，宋步忠试图丢弃一本中文笔记本，后经检查，发现该笔记本内仅载有多名中国人的姓名。

应卡托达（Katoda）巡佐的要求，另外两名在场人员，即：

施亭兰（S TING LAI），45岁，浙江人，男/会计师，住格罗西路（Rue B.Gross）

朱耀林（TS YOONG LIM），40岁，浙江人，男/戏院老板，住西贡路（Rue Saigon）。

pages.en:
- 3 -

were taken to C.B.H.C. C.I Offices together with the
suspect, Soong Foo Tsung, for questioning.
On being questioned regarding his address, the
suspect, Soong Foo Tsung, first stated that he has no
place of abode in Shanghai, but finally admitted that he
shared a room with his friend, named CHOU YUNG FUNG
(周永丰), a watchman residing in House 8, Lane 126, off
Rue Squet Allegre, French Concession.
At 7:30 p.m. the investigating detectives with
the assistance of the French Police, searched the room
at the above address and found therein, 25 letters, 15
envelops, 5 name cards and 2 account papers. The seized
articles are now being detained by the French Police,
Political Section, and will be handed over to the S.M.P.
on Monday, 24.4.39.
Upon being interrogated, the suspect Soong Foo
Tsung denied being a member of a guerilla unit or ever
being engaged in any anti-Japanese activities. He stated
that in the latter part of November, 1938, he fled from
Tangchow to Shanghai because members of a guerilla unit
operating in that area had requested him to donate a sum
of $500.00 to their funds; when he refused to meet the
request, the guerilla unit kidnapped his son, demanding a
ransom and at the same time threatening his life.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

连同嫌疑人宋福宗（Soong Foo Tsung）[注：此处原文名字拼写与前文Soong Poo Tsung不一致，依原文译出]被带至中央捕房刑事情报科办公室接受讯问。

当被问及住址时，嫌疑人宋福宗起初声称在上海无固定住所，但最后承认他与朋友周永丰（CHOU YUNG FUNG）合租一间房间，周永丰是一名更夫，居住在法租界亚尔培路（Rue Squet Allegre）126弄8号。

晚上7时30分，调查侦探在法国警察的协助下，搜查了上述地址的房间，并在房内发现信件25封、信封15个、名片5张及账目单据2张。所扣押物品现由法国警察局政治科暂时保管，并将于1939年4月24日（星期一）移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）。

经审讯，嫌疑人宋福宗否认是游击队成员，也否认曾参与任何反日活动。他称，1938年11月下旬，因在该地区活动的游击队成员要求他向他们的基金捐款500美元，他拒绝该要求后，游击队绑架了他的儿子，索要赎金，并同时威胁他的生命，因此他从唐州（Tangchow）逃往上海。

pages.en:
- 4 -

On arrival in Shanghai, he was employed for a
period of one month, i.e. Feb.7th. to March 6th. 1939,
as a ticket collector at the Tai Yuen ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) Chinese
Theatre and at present is unemployed.

This part of his statement referring to his
employment was corroborated by S Ting Lai and Ts Yoong
Ling, who are the owners of the theatre.

These two men were subsequently released as no
complicity with the suspect could be found.

Statement has been taken from the suspect and is
now being translated.

Sgt.Major Katoda, stating that he will communicate
with the Japanese Military Authorities in Yangchow with
a view to obtaining the necessary evidence against this
suspect, requested that Soong Foo Tsung be now detained.

The suspect, Soong Foo Tsung, is now detained in
Central Station Cells, pending production of evidence
against him.

It is not know at present whether or not the
seized letters, which are now temporary detained by the
French Police, contained any evidence against the suspect,
but when these letters are handed over to the S.M.Police
and perused, the contents of same will be the subject of
the next diary.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

卡托达（Katoda）巡佐表示，他将与扬州的日本军方当局联系，以获取针对该嫌疑人的必要证据，并要求目前拘留宋福宗。

嫌疑人宋福宗现被拘押于中央捕房监牢，以待提出针对他的证据。

目前尚不知由法国警察暂时扣押的查获信件中是否包含针对该嫌疑人的证据，但当这些信件移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处并查阅后，其内容将成为下一篇日志的主题。

当就被宣传单建议招募技工一事进行询问时，奥利弗先生表示，他们是代表京钟（Kying Zung）( ) 机械厂行事。奥利弗先生出示了一封写给中华基督教青年会职业介绍所的信件，写信人名叫顾（Koo）( ) ，是云南省京钟机械厂的代表。信中指出，顾先生希望为工厂雇佣多名技工，并请求允许使用中华基督教青年会职业介绍所来招募技工。在这封信中，顾先生提供了一个通讯地址：南京路大陆大楼515室。

REPORT FOR THE SHANGHAI MILITARY POLICE.

On the afternoon of 2.5.39, Sgt. Major
Katoda of the Japanese Gendarmerie Headquarters
requested assistance to arrest a certain member
of a guerilla unit at a certain address in Bubbling
Well Road.

The necessary assistance was given by D. S.
Fowler and the undersigned and room 107 of the
Burlington Hotel was visited at 5.10 p.m. but
the only occupants of the room were two foreign
women named Olivia Lewis, American, House 6, Lane
15, Carter Road, and Jina Mary Margaret Brodillini,
Unrecognised Foreigner, 45 Rue de Grouchy, who
were alleged to have rented the room for the
purpose of negotiating a bogus arms deal.

These women were taken to C. B. H. Q. by D. S. I.
Crighton for enquiries and the American woman was
questioned in the presence of the U. S. Marshal,
Mr. Gordon Campbell.

The Japanese Gendarmerie representatives
then left the Burlington Hotel without making any
arrests.

G Handley

1939年5月2日下午，日本宪兵队总部的卡托达（Katoda）巡佐请求协助，在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）某地址逮捕某游击队的一名成员。

WOO YEE MING (吳一鳴), age 28, S/Broker,
residing at 3 Al Too Li (愛多亞), Rue Bourane,
D.S.I. Pryde. Fr. Con.
Ningpo
H. Q. C. B. 8-5-39 Clerk Tsaung

I was born in Shanghai in the year 1911. I was
educated at the Zaushing Primary School (紹興旅滬小學);
Tiendong Road, from the age of 10 years to 17 years. I was
then employed as a boy in a foreign brothel at 14 Soochow
Road, where my father was employed as No. 1 Boy. I remained
in this employment for approximately three years. At that
time I got acquainted with a number of bad friends and was
arrested by West Hongkew Police Station on charges of larceny
of bicycles and attempted armed robbery. I was convicted
before the S.S.D.C. on 27-11-31 and sentenced to imprisonment
for one year. I was released from Ward Road Gaol on 31-8-32.
I next obtained employment as a bar tender in a cafe on
Avenue Joffre for approximately two months. I was next
employed as a broker for about six months. When I was 22
years old (1933) I went to Nanking and obtained a position
as office boy in the Post Office there and remained in this
employment for three years. I then sat for an examination
at which I failed, so returned to Shanghai and worked on and
off as a broker until the commencement of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937. I then joined the Young Men's Service
Corps (青年服務團) and obtained the rank of Captain with the
1st Section of the Ambulance attached to this corps, which
was employed removing the wounded from the front. On the
retreat of the Chinese troops from Shanghai I proceeded to
Nanking along with 11th Division of the Chinese Army, with
whom I was employed as a male nurse. When Nanking was
occupied by the Japanese forces I obtained a position as a

吴一鸣（WOO YEE MING），28岁，职业：掮客，
住址：法租界霞飞路（Rue Bourane，原文有误，应为Route Bourne或类似，但后文提及Rue Tourane及爱多亚路3号）爱多亚路3号（Al Too Li）。
督察：普赖德（Pryde）。来自：领事馆。
籍贯：宁波
总部中央捕房 1939年5月8日 书记员：庄（Tsaung）

我于1911年出生在上海。我就读于绍兴旅沪小学（Zaushing Primary School），
位于天潼路，从10岁至17岁。随后，我在苏州路14号的一家外国妓院当听差，
我的父亲在那里担任头号听差。我在那份工作中待了大约三年。那时，
我结识了一些坏朋友，并因盗窃自行车和持械抢劫未遂被虹口西区警察局逮捕。
我于1931年11月27日在特区地方法院（S.S.D.C.）被判有罪，判处监禁一年。
我于1932年8月31日从华德路监狱获释。
接下来，我在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）的一家咖啡馆当了大约两个月的酒吧侍者。
随后，我做了大约六个月的掮客。当我22岁（1933年）时，我去了南京，
在那里邮局谋得一份办公室勤务员的职位，并在此工作了三年。
后来我参加了一次考试但未通过，于是返回上海，断断续续做掮客，
直到1937年中日敌对行动开始。随后我加入了青年服务团（Young Men's Service Corps），
并在该团附属的救护队第一分队获得队长军衔，负责从前线运送伤员。
当中国军队从上海撤退时，我随中国军队第11师前往南京，
在那里担任男护士。当南京被日军占领时，我获得了一份

pages.en:
- 2 -

male nurse in a Refugee Hospital which was operated by an
American Subject named Mr. Mogei (?) and situated at the
rear of the Koo Lieu (鼓樓) Hospital in Nanking. On May
17th 1938 I came to Shanghai along with Mr. Mogei (?) and
went to live with my father at 3 Ai Too Li, Rue Tourane.
I stayed in Shanghai for approximately one month and then
proceeded to Hankow via Hongkong along with my foster-father
named Wang Siang Jing (孟湘琴), who was previously Chairman
of Fukien Province but is now unemployed. I was unable to
obtain any work in Hankow so returned to Shanghai via Hongkong
and arrived during October 1938. I then worked on and off as
a broker until arrested.
        Regarding the two Japanese passes seized at my
home :-
        I obtained one from an office which was situated
at Fukien and Foochow Road corner on payment of two dollars
and only used this on one occasion when I went to the North
Railway Station to accompany my fiancee who was proceeding to
Soochow. I obtained the other pass from a friend on payment
of three dollars and used same for visiting Hongkew in
connection with the brokerage business.
        Regarding the armed robbery which I was questioned
about by the detectives at Louza Station. I did not commit
this robbery but I know two of the four persons who are
arrested by Louza Station in connection with this crime.
One is named Wang Zang (汪成) and the other Hu (候).
The latter is the manager of the Chn Dah (久大) Co. (the firm
pages.zh:
- 2 -

在南京鼓楼（Koo Lieu）医院后方由一名叫莫吉（Mogei，音译）的美国侨民经营的难民医院担任男护士的职位。
1938年5月17日，我与莫吉先生一同来到上海，
并与我的父亲住在霞飞路（Rue Tourane，此处原文与前页Rue Bourane不一致，依后文统一为霞飞路或对应法文路名，但地址门牌号一致）爱多亚路3号。
我在上海待了大约一个月，然后与我的义父王湘琴（Wang Siang Jing，音译，括号内注孟湘琴）经香港前往汉口，
他曾任福建省主席，现失业。我在汉口找不到工作，
于是经香港返回上海，于1938年10月抵达。此后我一直断断续续做掮客，直到被捕。
        关于在我家中搜获的两张日本通行证：-
        其中一张是我在两美元的费用下，从福建路与福州路拐角处的一间办公室获得的，
        我只使用过一次，当时是去北站送我的未婚妻前往苏州。
        另一张通行证是我付了三美元从一位朋友那里获得的，
        我将其用于因掮客业务前往虹口。
        关于老闸捕房侦探向我讯问的持械抢劫案。我没有实施这起抢劫，
        但我认识老闸捕房因此案逮捕的四名嫌疑人中的两人。
        一人名叫汪成（Wang Zang，音译），另一人姓胡（Hu）。
        后者是久大（Chn Dah，音译）公司的经理（该公司

pages.en:
- 3 -
whose coolie was robbed). On the afternoon of 2-5-39 Waung
Zung sent a man to my home and called me to the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. on Boulevard de Montigny where Waung introduced me to
Eu. There were two other men present, one named Chang ( 張 )
and the other name unknown. We discussed robbing the Chu Dah
Co., but nothing definite was agreed upon and we arranged
to meet again on the following day at the Dah Loh Lodging
House (大陸公寓), Rue Auguste Boppe. At about 6.30 p.m. of
the same day, 2-5-39, I was passing along Kweichow Road on the
way to visit a friend named Doo Ming Chu ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), who lives
on North Chengtu Road, when I was arrested by Japanese and
conveyed to C.B.H.Q.

This is my true statement.

K.E.S

的苦力遭抢劫）。1939年5月2日下午，汪成（Waung Zung，音译）派人到我家，
叫我去蒙塔涅路（Boulevard de Montigny）的中国青年会，汪在那里把我介绍给欧（Eu，音译）。
当时还有另外两人在场，一人姓张（Chang），另一人姓名不详。
我们讨论了抢劫久大公司的事宜，但没有达成任何具体协议，
我们约定第二天在奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）的大陆公寓（Dah Loh Lodging House）再次见面。
同一天，即1939年5月2日下午6点30分左右，我正沿着贵州路走去拜访一位住在成都北路、
名叫杜明初（Doo Ming Chu，〔此处转录不清〕）的朋友，
这时我被日本人逮捕，并被押往中央捕房总部（C.B.H.Q.）。

这是我的真实供词。

K.E.S
5月8日

pages.en:
TRANSLATION

Brother "Yih Ming", (No. 3, Al Too Li, Ave. Ed. VII)
Words cannot describe my gratitude
for your assistance on three occasions.
I have myself to blame for the
miserable circumstances I am now in. Nevertheless,
my life has been spared and what I expect does not
eventuate. If God have mercy on me, I'll repay you
for what you have done to me.
I hope you will enable me to leave
this "Lone Island", which might emerge me from the
dark and see sparkling light.
I shall come to your place a week
later to hear from you.

BAH SIN.
2 p.m. 18th.
pages.zh:
译文

“一鸣”兄，（爱多亚路3号，爱德华七世大道）
言语无法表达我对您三次援助的感激之情。
我目前的悲惨处境只能怪我自己。尽管如此，
我的性命得以保全，而我所期望的并未发生。
如果上帝怜悯我，我会报答您对我的恩情。
我希望您能使我离开这个“孤岛”，
这可能会让我走出黑暗，看到闪耀的光芒。
我将于一周后到您的住处听取您的回复。

巴辛（BAH SIN）。
18日下午2点。

pages.en:
Translation of contents of an exercise book.

1.
To: Sian Coup

The 12th of December - the memorable day of
the Sian Coup. This day is a great climax to a series
of notable events in 5,000 years of Chinese history.
It is also the day of renaissance of our race. At the
time of this incident all our country-men showed their
anxiety as regards to the safety of our leader .........
Fellow countrymen! Warriors! Friends!
Their strategy is to exchange time for space of time.

1. (Reverse) :
Standard Evening News.
1st Regiment, 2nd Battalion of
4th district mobile unit.

2. Part of a love letter addressed to one named Tung Ming.

3.
Mobile Unit

No home and no fields. We are just a horde of
roaming citizens. The only way to live is to clash
with the "Devils". March forward and take the narrow
pass. Any forest is our encamping ground. Never let
the "Devil Soldiers" see us when they are moving along.
Strike them from the rear as soon as they halt. Our
weapons are scanty, but we can slay all the "Devils" as
we go ahead unceasingly. Recapture our home and our
fields; Our armed populace, we are the Guerillas Loyal
and Brave Corps.

3. (Reverse) :
Part of a love letter addressed to one named "Jing".
pages.zh:
练习簿内容译文。

1.
致：西安事变

12月12日——西安事变的纪念日。
这一天是中国五千年历史上一系列重大事件的高潮。
这也是我们民族复兴的日子。在这一事件发生时，
我们所有同胞都表现出对我们领袖 ____ 安全的担忧。
同胞们！战士们！朋友们！
他们的策略是以空间换取时间。

1. （背面）：
标准晚报。
第四区流动部队
第二营第一团。

2. 一封写给名叫董明（Tung Ming，音译）的人的情书片段。

3.
流动部队

无家无田。我们只是一群流浪的百姓。
生存的唯一途径是与“魔鬼”冲突。向前进，夺取险要关口。
任何森林都是我们的营地。绝不让“魔鬼兵”在行进时看到我们。
一旦他们停下，就从后方打击他们。我们的武器匮乏，
但只要我们要不断前进，就能杀死所有“魔鬼”。
收复我们的家园和田地；我们的武装民众，
我们是忠诚勇敢的游击队。

3. （背面）：
一封写给名叫“静”（Jing，音译）的人的情书片段。

Assistance to Japanese Consular Police.

At 6 p.m. on 2.5.39 Mr. Hashizume, Chancellor of
the Japanese Consular Police, came to Crime Branch Head-
quarters and requested assistance to wait on Kweichow
Road outside to Great China Hotel to arrest one named
Woo Yee Ming (吴义明), whom, Mr. Hashizume stated,
was the Commander of the 3rd. Battalion of Chekiang -
Kiangsu Guerrilla Troops.

Assistance was rendered accordingly by D.S.I.s
Frydo, Watanabe, Soong Ping Tsung, D.S. Sugimoto and
party, but on arrival at the scene at 6.45 p.m. it was
ascertained that the wanted man had already been arrested
by Japanese Consular Police who were waiting in the
vicinity, and conveyed to Crime Branch Headquarters.

When questioned the arrested man gave the following
particulars of himself.

Name, Woo Yee Ming, age 28, native of Ningpo, living
at No.3 Ai Tau Li, Rue Tourane, French Concession.

As the request of the Consular Police this address
was searched with the assistance of the French Police.
The arrested man's father and mother were found to be
living in a downstairs back room. Seized from the room
were:-

2

协助日本领事警察。

1939年5月2日下午6点，日本领事警察书记官桥爪（Hashizume，音译）先生
来到刑事处总部，请求协助在贵州路大华大戏院（Great China Hotel，此处原文为Hotel，但大华通常指戏院或饭店，依语境可能是大华饭店或大华戏院附近）外等候，
以逮捕一名名叫吴义明（Woo Yee Ming）的人，桥爪先生称此人是
浙苏游击队第三营营长。

弗莱多（Frydo，音译）、渡边（Watanabe）、宋秉宗（Soong Ping Tsung，音译）督察、
杉本（Sugimoto，音译）副督察及其随行人员随即提供了协助，
但当他们在下午6点45分到达现场时，发现通缉犯已被
在附近等候的日本领事警察逮捕，并被押往刑事处总部。

经讯问，被捕男子提供了以下个人资料。

27 Photographs,
2 Japanese Passes,
1 Letter,

Several of the photograph were of Chinese soldiers
in uniform. These documents have been kept by the
French Police, who will hand them over after perusal.
When questioned the arrested man first stated
that he was employed as a broker at 150 KiuKiang Road
but later denied this, and claimed to be employed by
the Post Office and later to be a doctor.
On the instructions of the D.C. (Crime), Woo Yes
Ming was handed over to the Japanese Consular Police
for enquiries at 11 p.m. on condition that he be returned
to the custody of the S.M.P. within 24 hours.

经讯问，被捕男子最初声称他在九江路150号受雇为掮客，
但后来否认了这一说法，声称受雇于邮局，后来又声称是医生。

将其归还给上海公共租界警务处羁押。

乔治·B·多伊尔（Geo. B. Doyle）
督察

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

I proceeded to the house of Loong Yu (龍裕)
of the Yue Hing Xang Ji (岳興祥記) firm,
No. 55 Ah Yih Village, etc.

I found that one O. School for the King
(王學校) was there, to reside
at No. 7 waiting room. I also found April, 1930.
He did not see, and went at 10 o'clock in
the afternoon.

I found bottles of cotton seed oil.

I entered a room block A April 15 for 36.25
re r. Tien (田).

I found daily papers relating to
the present hostilities.

It was learnt that room 310 had been engaged
on April 11, 1930 by one Hyien Ta Zai (賢大仔)
who however had left the room about half an hour
prior to the visit of the police party.

All persons denied residing in the room.
Some had gone to collect debts, others to play
Mah Jong as they had been in the habit of doing at
the request of Hyien Ta Zai. Some knew him personally
whilst others did not. All denied ownership of the
papers etc. seized.

FURTHER TO
ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE.

At 3.30 p.m. May 3rd, the Japanese Consular
Police informed C.I. C.D.H.Q. that they were
unable to bring over their informer in order
to proceed to Lokewai Station of the French
Police for purposes of identification re the
arrest of Yoeh Pai Tsang (杨玉章). They
however, asked that the Municipal Police request
the French Police to detain the arrested man
for a further 24 hours, during which period
they would produce their informer.

The undersigned interviewed Mr. Valentine
re the further detention of Yoeh Pai Tsang and
this he agreed to do until 12 noon May 4th.

The books etc. seized at the home of Yoeh
Pai Tsang were handed to the undersigned against
receipt. An itemised list (copy attached) has
been compiled. The detained man denies owner-
ship of them.

At 10.30 a.m. May 4th the Japanese Consular
Police brought to C.I C.D.H.Q. a male Chinese
whom they stated was their informer and would
be able to identify the detained man.

The informer gave his name as, one Ih sing
(      ) 30, native of anhui.
Accompanied by J.S. Sugimoto, S.I. Tang
and the undersigned, the party proceeded to
Lokawei where an identification parade was held.
The informer failed to identify the detained
man although he did pick out a male of similar
build wearing a coffee-coloured silk long gown.
It is worthy of note however, that the detained
man was, at the time of his arrest, also wearing
a coffee-coloured long gown.
Sgt. Sergeant Ninomiya of the Japanese
Consular Police then requested Mr. Jobez to detain
the arrested man for a further period pending them
producing definite proof that the detained man was
as alleged, namely, a Commander in the Chinese
army. Mr. Jobez informed J.S. Ninomiya that
the French Police would only render assistance to
the Municipal Police, therefore, if the Japanese

MAY 3rd, 39.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE.

On the afternoon of 2.5.39, Mr. Hashizume
of the Japanese Consular Police requested assistance
to arrest a certain Chinese, suspected to be an
officer of a guerilla unit residing at a certain
address on Robison Road.

The necessary assistance was rendered by
D.S. Krader, D.S. Bradley and Lieut. Stebel of
the Royal Italian Marines at 4.15 a.m. 3.5.39.

On arrival at the premises to be raided
it was found that the address was an unnumbered
Chinese dwelling house West of Jung Hwa Li (榮華里)
off Robison Road O.O.L. The Japanese Consular
Police raided the premises, and arrested a male
Chinese named Liang Han San (梁漢三), 37, N/Hope
Hsieng, Kiangsu, and seized 7 pamphlets of an anti-
Japanese nature.

The arrested man and the pamphlets were
taken away by the Japanese Consular Police.

Further to Assistant C.C. to Japanese
Military Water Police.

A notification has been received from Yuhechi
Matsumaki, Commander of the Japanese Military River
Police, to the effect that Yoe Shu Ling (夏寶林),
alias Zung Yah Tung (陳學東), who was arrested
on May 2nd. 1939, at Room 121 of the Shanghai Merchants
Stock Exchange Building, No.429 Kiukiang Road as a
suspected member of a guerrilla unit and who was
handed over to the Military Water Police A.M. on
May 6th. 1939, had died at 5.50 p.m. the same day
(May 6th. 1939).

A death certificate issued by Dr. Tadasu Kikuchi
who attended the now deceased, shows that death was
due to "Natural Causes", the result of heart failure
caused by a stricture of the heart.

The body was buried in Pootung on May 7th. 1939.
Copies of death certificate attached.

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO THE JAPANESE
WATER POLICE, AND ILLEGAL FUNCTIONING.

Resultant from further questioning of Tsung Dsu
Zah (陳樹澤) it has been ascertained that during
1938 he, through the introduction of a friend secured
a position as an agent with the Reformed Government
Police in Pestung, later he transferred to a similar
position in the Water Police at Yang Ka Zah.

It appears that his job was to make enquiries
regarding anti-Japanese elements as directed by the
Japanese Military Official in charge of the Station.

Regarding his visit to room No.191 of the Shanghai
Merchants Stock Exchange Building, No.429 Kinkiang Road,
he stated that he first visited this place to enquire
about Lee Yu Ming (李志明) at about 4 p.m. on April
30th. 1939, upon the instruction of a Japanese Gendar-
merie translated to him by an interpreter named Wang
Kang (王振)

续报协助日本水上警察及非法活动事宜。

经进一步讯问陈树泽（Tsung Dsu Zah），查明他在1938年期间，通过朋友介绍，在浦东（Pestung，音译）维新政府警察部门获得了一份特工职位，后来调往杨家宅（Yang Ka Zah，音译）的水上警察部门担任类似职务。

看来他的工作是根据负责该站的日本军方官员的指示，调查反日分子。

关于他前往九江路429号上海华商证券交易所大楼191室一事，他陈述说，他首次前往该地是为了打听李志明（Lee Yu Ming）的情况，时间是1939年4月30日下午4点左右，这是由一名名为王振（Wang Kang）的翻译向他传达的日本宪兵队的指令。

批：好

Again on May 4th, 1939 he received further
instructions from the same source to go to No.429
Kiukiang Road and continue enquiries regarding Lee
Te Ming, this visit resulted in his apprehension.

Enquiries have been continued at room No.121 and
it appears that the person who Tsung Dsu Zah (陳樹澤)
spoke to when he visited on April 30th, was Lee Pau
Kung (李宝振), son of the aged female Lee Jeung
Sa (李唐氏) who has failed to return since the
Police visited on May 2nd. 1939.

With the assistance of the French Police enquiries
have been made at No.80 Chen Yeen Li, Rue Prelupt, where
the wife of the arrested man corroborated his statement
as to how he was employed as a plain clothes agent in
the Poetung Water Police. No documents or any other
evidence was found.

The Military Water Police have again been communi-
cated with and requested that they confirm the man's
statement.

Meanwhile the man is being detained at Central
Station.

6/5/39.

已在121室继续进行调查，看来陈树泽（Tsung Dsu Zah）在4月30日走访时交谈的人是李宝振（Lee Pau Kung），他是老妇人李唐氏（Lee Jeung Sa）的儿子，自警方于1939年5月2日走访以来，李宝振一直未归。

在法国警察的协助下，已在普雷吕普路（Rue Prelupt）陈仁里80号进行了调查，被捕男子的妻子证实了他关于如何在浦东（Poetung，音译）水上警察部门便衣特工任职的陈述。未发现任何文件或其他证据。

已再次与军用水上警察联系，并要求他们确认该男子的陈述。

与此同时，该男子正被拘留在中央捕房。

H.C.S

3:

FURTHER TO ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY
WATER POLICE.

From further questioning of the arrested
female, Lee Deung Sz (李唐氏), it has been ascer-
tained that the wanted man, Lee Ts King (李志明),
is related to her, but she stoutly maintains that
he has never visited her at any time, and she claims
to have no knowledge of his present possible where-
abouts.

Regarding the belief that her son is Lee Ts
King, this does not appear to be so, since there is
a difference of ten years in their respective ages,
and both hail from different parts of the country,
consequently the supposition is without foundation.

In accordance with the instructions of the
D.C.(Sdsg) the said female was returned to her
home on Ngat Sin Lane, but is being kept under obser-
vation as requested by the Japanese Military.

Tientsin                                C.D.S. 104.

C.1.            5.5.39                  ////////    Hsu.

My name is Tsung Dzu h, age 33, native of Tientsin,
married, and residing at No. 50 Chien Yin Li, Rue Prelupt.

I was born in my native place (village off Tientsin), &
at the age of 7 I attended a primary school; I left school
at the age of 10, since when I have never attended any
other schools. After leaving school I assisted my
father in farming.

At the age of 15, I went to Tientsin City and there
obtained employment as an apprentice in the Hong Chang
Piece Goods Shop, Pah Lu Road, Tientsin, being thus em-
ployed for 3 years. On expiry of the apprenticeship
period (i.e. 3 years), I was promoted to shop assistant
and still employed in the same shop with pay of $3.00
per month.

Another three years elapsed, the piece goods shop
was closed and I returned to my country.

On the 6th of 9th moon of the 19th year of the
Chinese Republic (Lunar year) I left home and came to
Shanghai, when I was 25 years old.

On arrival at Shanghai I lived in the home of my elder
brother, Tsung Sze Te (陳仕德).

Three or four months later, through the introduction
of my elder brother, I procured a job as a salesman in
**〔此处转录不清〕**

天津                                C.D.S. 104。

C.1.            1939年5月5日                  ////////    徐 (Hsu)。

我叫陈树海，33岁，天津人，
已婚，现居住于蒲柏路 (Rue Prelupt) 建德里50号。

我出生于原籍（天津郊外的村庄），
7岁时进入小学读书；10岁辍学，此后未再
就读其他学校。辍学后，我协助父亲
务农。

15岁时，我前往天津市区，在天津白鹿路 (Pah Lu Road) 的
鸿昌布店当学徒，受雇于此3年。学徒期
满（即3年）后，我晋升为店员，
仍在同一家店铺工作，月薪3.00元。

又过了三年，布店关闭，我返回家乡。

民国十九年农历九月初六，我离开家乡来到
上海，当时我25岁。

抵达上海后，我住在兄长
陈仕德 (Tsung Sze Te) 家中。

三四个月后，通过兄长的介绍，我在

to this coy. as an inspector, with an increased pay of

I was thus employed until the outbreak of the current
hostilities on 13.8.37, when I became unemployed.

On or about 9th Oct. 1937, as the Chinese troops
retreated from Hanting, I came to take refuge in the
home of my father-in-law, Chen Wan Lai (陳萬來), at
No. 144 Rue Xastner, French Concession.

On the 5.12.37, the "Tao Tao" Government being formed
in Pootung, I, after taking an examination, joined the
Detective Squad of this Government as a detective with
pay of $38.00 per mensem.

In Aug. last year, being discharged from the Tao Tao
Police Bureau, I became a plain-clothes policeman of
the Pootung Water Police, and my pay was only $18.00
per month.

Not being satisfied with this small sum of pay,
I approached a friend of mine, one named Wong Tsang (王震),
who is a Japanese interpreter at the Pootung Gendarmerie
Headquarters, and asked him to seek a better position for
me.

In Sept. 1938, through the introduction of Wong Tsang,
I joined the Detective Service of the Pootung Gendarmerie
Headquarters, with a monthly pay of $30.00.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

该公司担任稽查员，月薪增至

我就职至此，直到1937年8月13日当前战事爆发，
我便失业了。

1937年10月9日左右，随着中国军队
从嘉定撤退，我来到法租界霞飞路 (Rue Xastner) 144号
岳父陈万来 (Chen Wan Lai) 家中避难。

1937年12月5日，“大道”政府在浦东成立，我
经过考试后，加入该政府的侦探队担任侦探，
月薪38.00元。

去年8月，我从大道警察局离职，成为
浦东水上警察的一名便衣警察，月薪仅为
18.00元。

因对这笔微薄的薪水不满意，我找到一位名叫
王震 (Wong Tsang) 的朋友，他是浦东宪兵队总部的
日语翻译，请他为我谋求一个更好的职位。

1938年9月，通过王震的介绍，我加入
浦东宪兵队总部的侦探部门，月薪
30.00元。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

- 3 -

the movements of Anti-Japanese elements.

I am unable to write, and thus must make verbal
reports of my daily work to my superior.

At 4 p.m. 30.4.39, acting on the instructions of
a Japanese officer and Wong Tsang, I proceeded to Room
121, The Chinese Merchants' Stock Exchange building, 489
Kiukiang Road to trace one named Lee To Ming, who was
allegedly to be a member of a guerilla unit.

On my arrival at the above mentioned address and on
pushing open the room door, I observed a male Chinese,
age about 30 years, pale complexion, small build, being
in the room.

I asked this man his name and in reply he told me
that his name was Lee. In turn he asked to know the
purpose of my visit. I then told him that I was coming
to look for one named Chang (which was a lie). I purposely
answered in this way in order to evade his suspicion.
I then returned to Footung and made a verbal report of the
results of my enquiries to Fong Tsang, who, in turn, reported
to a Japanese officer.

I do not know whether or not the man, who answered
my questions and who gave his name as Lee when I called at
Room 121, No. 489 Kiukiang Road, was Lee To Ming.

〔此处转录不清〕
pages.zh:
- 3 -

抗日分子的动向。

我不识字，因此必须向上级口头汇报
我的日常工作。

1939年4月30日下午4时，遵照一名日本军官和王震的指示，
我前往九江路489号华商证券交易所大楼121室，
追踪一名叫李道明 (Lee To Ming) 的人，据称他是
游击队成员。

到达上述地址并推开房门后，我看到房间内有一名
中国男子，约30岁，面色苍白，身材瘦小。

我问此人姓名，他回答说姓李。反过来他问我
来访的目的。我告诉他我是来找一位姓张的人（这是谎言）。
我故意这样回答以消除他的怀疑。随后我返回浦东，
向王震口头汇报了调查结果，王震随即向
一名日本军官汇报。

我不知道在九江路489号121室回答我问题并自称姓李的男子
是否是李道明。

〔此处转录不清〕

pages.en:
- 4 -

had visited the said room again, to which I answered in
the negative. He then instructed me to go there that
afternoon.

At about 3 p.m. 4.5.39, I came to Shanghai from
Pootung in a launch, and proceeded to Room 121, No. 489
Kiukiang Road.

I entered the building and on finding the door of
Room 121, half closed, I immediately stepped into the room,
and asked the occupants if Mr. Lee was in. One of the
four inmates then questioned me as to whom I was looking
for.

Seeing something amiss and definitely knowing that
the four occupants were police officers, I falsely said
that I came to inform Lee To Ming to leave the address at
once, for the Japanese Authorities were hunting for him.

I told them this lie because I felt it was very
shameful if I would tell them that I came to inquire about
Lee's movements on behalf of the Japanese.

I was previously arrested by Louza Detectives of the
S.M.Police, at about 10 a.m. 19.3.39 when I was, acting on
instructions of Japanese Authorities, enquiring into the
Tung Shing Lau (同興樓) Restaurant, Nanking Road, regarding
the matter of Tung Sun An **〔此处转录不清〕**
pages.zh:
- 4 -

是否再次去过该房间，我予以否认。于是他指示我
当天下午去那里。

1939年5月4日下午3点左右，我乘汽艇从
浦东来到上海，前往九江路489号121室。

我进入大楼，发现121室的门半掩着，便立即
走进房间，询问屋内的人李先生是否在。四名
住客中的一人随即质问我在找谁。

察觉情况不对，并明确知道这四名住客是警察，
我谎称我是来通知李道明立即离开该地址，因为
日本当局正在追捕他。

我撒这个谎是因为我觉得，如果告诉他们我是代表日本人
来查询李的动向，会非常丢脸。

此前，1939年3月19日上午10点左右，我遵照日本当局的指示，
就同兴安 **〔此处转录不清〕** 一事在南京路同兴楼 (Tung Shing Lau) 餐馆
进行调查时，被工部局警务处老闸捕房的侦探逮捕。

by S.M.Police, I feel awfully ashamed of myself, but I
was really sent here by Japanese Gend rmerie Headquarters
in Poetung to conduct enquiries re Lee Tu Ming.
The above is my true statement.

Lgn.G.
pages.zh:
- 5 -
被工部局警务处逮捕，我感到非常羞愧，但我
确实是受浦东日本宪兵队总部的派遣，前来
调查李图明 (Lee Tu Ming) 的情况。
以上是我的真实陈述。

Lgn.G.

ASSISTANCE TO JAPANESE MILITARY WATER POLICE.

At 3:30 p.m. on May 2nd. 1939, Sergt. Major
MATSUI, attached to the Japanese Military Water Police,
Headquarters, the Floating Restaurant, Peking Road Jetty,
requested that assistance be rendered in effecting the
arrest of a male Chinese member of the "National Salvation
Army".

According to the information supplied by a
Japanese agent, who was produced but not questioned, the
wanted man named, LEE TU MING (李志明), was a former
commander of the Third Sub-Division of the Chinese
National Salvation Army, and that some short time ago,
he had resigned from his position and had come to Shanghai,
with his family from some undisclosed place in the
country, bringing with him the sum of $150,000.00. This
money, it is believed, was funds etc. for the upkeep of
his unit, and further Sergt. Major Matsui was of the
opinion that Lee Tu Ming intended to escape to Hankow.

Sergt. Major Matsui further stated that this
wanted man was residing at Room No. 321 of the Shanghai
Merchants Bank Building, Nanking Road.
〔此处转录不清〕

协助日本军方水上警察事宜。

1939年5月2日下午3:30，隶属于日本军方水上警察总部、
驻北京路码头浮游餐厅的松井 (MATSUI) 军曹长，
请求协助逮捕一名“救国军”的中国男性成员。

根据一名被带来但未受讯问的日本线人提供的信息，
名为李志明 (LEE TU MING) 的通缉犯曾任中国
救国军第三分部指挥官，不久前他从国内某未公开地点
携家眷来到上海，随身携带150,000.00元。据信，
这笔钱是其部队维持经费等款项，此外松井军曹长认为
李志明打算逃往汉口。

松井军曹长还称，该通缉犯居住在南京路
上海商业储蓄银行大楼321室。

- 2 -

and C.D.C.'s 2 and 169, and at 3:40 p.m. 2.5.39 the
above premises were visited, which was found to be
occupied by four females and two males, the Japanese
agent failed to recognize any of them as the wanted
person.

After questioning all the inmates, the Sgt.Major
requested that the two following persons be taken to
Police Headquarters for further questioning :-
1) LEE DAUNG SZ (李唐氏), 68, Widow, Footung.
2) WOO PAU LING (夏宝林), alias ZUNG YAH TUNG
(陳学東), s/Fish Hawker, resident
at Footung.

One "Good Citizen's Badge" issued by the Japanese Army
authorities was seized from the person of Woo Pau Ling.
A draft of an essay wrote for the press eulogizing Lee
Ta Ming, one unstamped envelope addressed to the Dah Mei
Evening News, a portion of a radio morse code set and two
dry cell batteries were seized from a dressing table.

The female, Lee Daung Sz, stated that she came from
Foo Intard,F.K. about one month ago with her son, named
Lee Jun Hung (李宝根), aged 26, took up residence at
her present address. Her son, who was absent at the time
of the Police visit, is according to her statement
employed as a Fish Hawker.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

以及刑事侦缉处2号和169号人员，1939年5月2日下午3:40
对上述地点进行了走访，发现该处由四名女性和两名男性居住，
日本线人未能从中辨认出任何一人是通缉犯。

讯问所有住客后，军曹长要求将以下两人带至
警察总局作进一步讯问：-
1) 李唐氏 (LEE DAUNG SZ)，68岁，寡妇，住浦东。
2) 夏宝林 (WOO PAU LING)，别名陈学东 (ZUNG YAH TUNG)，
鱼贩之子，住浦东。

从夏宝林身上搜获一枚由日本陆军当局颁发的
“良民证”。
从梳妆台上搜获一篇为报刊撰写的颂扬李达明 (Lee Ta Ming) 的文章草稿、
一个寄给《大美晚报》的无邮票信封、一部分无线电莫尔斯电码装置
和两节干电池。

女子李唐氏称，她约一个月前与26岁的儿子
李宝根 (Lee Jun Hung) 从福建福州 (Foo Intard,F.K.) 来到此地，
并在现住址定居。据她陈述，警方走访时不在家的儿子
职业为鱼贩。

pages.en:
- 3 -

The Japanese are of the opinion that the son of
the aged female is the wanted man, Lee Is Ming, although
she avers that to her knowledge, he is not connected with
any political activities.

Woo Sau Ling claims that he is a friend of the
female, and her family, and that he came from Peotung
three days ago in connection with his business as a
fish hawker.

He claims to have no connection with any
political party or guerrilla unit and added that he
knew the old woman's son Lee Fan Kung (李宝柄) when
he was employed at a tea shop in Peotung prior to the
outbreak of hostilities.

The female cannot explain who wrote the essay
regarding Lee Is Ming, but added that her son may have
done so, she likewise is unable to account for the
presence of the Morse code apparatus.

At the request of the Japanese Military both
persons are being detained pending further enquiries.

Before leaving the Stock Exchange Building the
Japanese agent was accompanied to various other rooms
in the building and allowed to view the occupants since
it was thought that Lee may have been residing. Nothing
resulted from this visit.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

日方认为该老妇的儿子即是通缉犯李志明 (Lee Is Ming)，尽管
她坚称据其所知，他并未参与任何政治活动。

夏宝林 (Woo Sau Ling) 声称他是该女子及其家人的朋友，
三天前因鱼贩生意从浦东来到此处。

他声称与任何政党或游击队无关，并补充说，
他在战事爆发前在浦东一家茶馆工作时就认识
老妇人的儿子李宝柄 (Lee Fan Kung)。

该女子无法解释是谁写了关于李志明 (Lee Is Ming) 的文章，
但补充说可能是她儿子写的，她同样无法解释
莫尔斯电码装置的存在。

应日本军方要求，两人均被拘留以待进一步调查。

在离开证券交易所大楼之前，日本线人在陪同下查看了
大楼内的其他各个房间及住客，因为推测李可能
居住在此。此次走访未有结果。

pages.en:
- 4 -

Since the Japanese were of the opinion that
with the arrest of the aged female Lee would undoubtedly
return here, they requested that detectives be kept
on duty for a time, this was agreed to.

The seized enemy draft and statements will be
the subject of a further report.

G. Lioden
DeSalle
pages.zh:
- 4 -

由于日方认为随着老妇人被捕，李无疑会
返回此处，他们要求安排侦探值守一段时间，此提议
获准。

缴获的敌方草稿及陈述将另行报告。

G. Lioden
DeSalle
